refcocog.text: A referring-expression grounding set of roughly 85,000 descriptions for 54,822 objects in COCO images, collected non-interactively so the phrases are longer and more descriptive than in RefCOCO.

refspatial.text: A spatial referring resource from the RoboRefer work: a dataset of 20M question-answer pairs covering 31 spatial relations and reasoning chains up to five steps, released with RefSpatial-Bench for evaluating multi-step spatial referring.

repoqa.text: 500 Searching Needle Function tasks drawn from 50 popular repositories in five programming languages, where a model must locate the function matching a natural-language description inside a long stretch of repository code.

rewardbench.text: A dataset and codebase of prompt, chosen and rejected response trios across chat, reasoning and safety, used to test whether a reward model prefers the better answer when the difference is subtle but verifiable.

robospatial.text: A spatial reasoning resource for robotics that pairs 2D egocentric images with 3D scans and annotates 3 million spatial relationships in ego-centric, world-centric and object-centric frames, evaluated on spatial affordance and relationship prediction.

rtplx.text: A human-written and human-annotated corpus of toxic prompts and outputs in 28 languages, transcreated rather than translated so that culturally specific toxicity is represented.

ruler.text: A synthetic long-context benchmark with configurable sequence length and task complexity, extending needle-in-a-haystack retrieval with multiple needle types plus multi-hop tracing and aggregation tasks.

ruler32k.text: RULER run at a 32,000-token context length. RULER is a synthetic long-context suite of 13 tasks that extends needle-in-a-haystack with varied needle types and counts plus multi-hop tracing and aggregation, at a configurable sequence length.

saferlhf.text: A safety alignment dataset of about 44.6k prompts and 265k question-answer pairs with human preference annotations that separate helpfulness from harmlessness, plus safety meta-labels covering 19 harm categories at three severity levels.

sat.text: A math evaluation of the 32 questions without figures from the May 2023 College Board SAT examination, assembled by the Llemma authors as a post-cutoff test set.

scannet.text: An RGB-D video dataset of 2.5M views across 1,513 indoor scenes annotated with 3D camera poses, surface reconstructions and semantic segmentations, supporting 3D object classification, semantic voxel labeling and CAD model retrieval.

scicode.text: 80 research coding problems from 16 natural science subfields, decomposed by scientists into 338 subproblems, each with gold solutions and test cases.

scienceqa.text: About 21,000 multimodal multiple-choice science questions spanning school subjects, annotated with lectures and explanations so a model's reasoning chain can be evaluated alongside the answer.

screenspot.text: A GUI grounding benchmark covering mobile, desktop and web interfaces, where a model must locate the screen element referred to by a natural language instruction rather than produce text.

screenspotpro.text: A GUI grounding benchmark of authentic high-resolution screenshots with expert annotations, spanning 23 professional applications across five industries and three operating systems, where targets are small relative to the screen.

screenspot2.text: A re-annotated version of the ScreenSpot GUI grounding benchmark released with OS-Atlas, correcting roughly 11 percent of mislabelled samples across mobile, desktop and web screenshots while keeping the test set size unchanged.

sdqa.text: A spoken dialectal question answering benchmark in five languages (Arabic, Bengali, English, Kiswahili, Korean) with more than 68,000 audio prompts recorded by 255 speakers across 24 dialects.

seal0.text: The hardest subset of SealQA: fact-seeking questions kept because web search returns conflicting, noisy or unhelpful results, so the model must reason over bad evidence rather than just retrieve.

secbenchpro.text: 344 validated real vulnerabilities in V8, SpiderMonkey and the Linux kernel, where an agent must reproduce a working proof-of-concept input from a disclosed report, covering memory safety, sandbox, JIT and race condition bugs.

seed.text: SEED-Bench: about 19,000 human-annotated multiple-choice questions spanning 12 evaluation dimensions over both images and video, covering spatial and temporal comprehension for multimodal models.

seedbench2plus.text: 2.3K human-annotated multiple-choice questions on text-rich images in three categories, charts, maps and web pages, testing comprehension of text embedded in visuals.

seedtts.text: The seed-tts-eval objective test set for zero-shot speech generation: 1,000 English samples from Common Voice and 2,000 Mandarin samples from DiDiSpeech-2, scored by ASR word error rate and WavLM speaker similarity.

seqqa.text: A LAB-Bench subtask of DNA and protein sequence questions, covering sequence manipulation, restriction enzyme recognition and identifying genomic or proteomic elements inside longer sequences.

shadearena.text: An agent evaluation dataset pairing a benign main task with a harmful hidden side objective in complex environments, scoring whether a model completes the side task without being flagged by an LLM monitor.

simpleqa.text: 4,326 short fact-seeking questions with a single indisputable reference answer, adversarially collected against GPT-4 and graded automatically as correct, incorrect or not attempted to measure short-form factuality.

simpleqaverified.text: A 1,000-prompt factuality set filtered from OpenAI's SimpleQA by de-duplicating questions, rebalancing topics and reconciling sources to remove noisy labels, measuring short-answer knowledge recalled without external tools.

simplevqa.text: A multimodal factuality benchmark of short natural language questions about images, spread over nine tasks and nine topic domains, with static reference answers graded by an LLM judge.

siqa.text: About 38,000 multiple-choice questions on social and emotional commonsense, asking about people's motivations, reactions and the effects of everyday social actions, with distractors crowdsourced from related questions to limit stylistic artifacts.

slake.text: A bilingual English and Chinese medical visual question answering dataset of radiology images, annotated by physicians with semantic labels and paired with a structured medical knowledge base.

spider.text: 10,181 natural language questions paired with 5,693 SQL queries over 200 multi-table databases in 138 domains, with train and test on different databases so models must generalize to unseen schemas.

spreadsheetbench.text: 912 real spreadsheet manipulation questions collected from online Excel forums, graded like an online judge: each instruction ships with several test spreadsheet files so a solution must work across varying values.

ss2.text: 220,847 short videos filmed by crowd workers who were given an action template first and then recorded themselves performing it, labelled with 174 fine-grained templates for object manipulation.

storycloze.text: A commonsense narrative test built on the ROCStories corpus of roughly 50,000 five-sentence everyday stories: given the first four sentences, a system must pick the correct ending from two candidates.

strongreject.text: A jailbreak evaluation set of forbidden prompts that a model must answer with specific harmful information to count as broken, paired with an autograder that scores how useful the response is rather than whether the model merely failed to refuse.

stvqa.text: Scene Text Visual Question Answering: questions about images that can only be answered by reading the text appearing in the scene and combining it with the visual context, graded by a metric that separates reasoning errors from text recognition errors.

sunrgbd.text: 10,000 RGB-D images captured with four sensors and pooled from NYU Depth v2, Berkeley B3DO and SUN3D, annotated with 146,617 2D polygons and 58,657 oriented 3D bounding boxes plus room layouts, for 3D object detection, room layout estimation and holistic scene understanding.

supergpqa.text: A knowledge and reasoning benchmark spanning 285 graduate-level disciplines, including long-tail fields such as light industry and agriculture, filtered by a human and LLM collaborative process that removes trivial or ambiguous questions.

swe-bench.text: 2,294 software engineering tasks built from real GitHub issues and their merged pull requests across 12 Python repositories. The model edits the repository to resolve the issue and is graded by the pull request's tests.

swe-bench-verified.text: A 500-problem subset of SWE-bench, screened by professional software developers so that each GitHub issue is well specified and its unit tests are correctly scoped.

swebenchagentless.text: SWE-bench solved with the Agentless scaffold, a fixed three-phase pipeline of fault localization, patch repair and patch validation, with no autonomous tool use or planning by the model.

swebenchmultilingual.text: 300 real GitHub issue-resolution tasks drawn from 42 repositories across nine languages (C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby, Rust), graded by fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass unit tests as in SWE-bench.

swebenchpro.text: 1,865 long-horizon software engineering problems from 41 maintained repositories, split into public, held-out and commercial partitions; given a codebase and an issue, the model must write a patch, often spanning several files.

swemarathon.text: 20 ultra-long-horizon software engineering tasks, each with its own executable environment, a human-written reference solution and a multi-layer verification suite designed to block shortcut solutions.

synthetictext2sql.text: A synthetic text-to-SQL dataset of 105,851 records across 100 domains, each pairing a natural language request with database context, a SQL query and an explanation, and covering a range of query complexity.

t2icompbench.text: 6,000 compositional text-to-image prompts in three categories (attribute binding, object relationships and complex compositions) with six sub-categories, plus metrics designed to score each kind of composition.

tau-bench.text: Emulates conversations between a language-model-simulated user and an agent equipped with domain APIs and a policy document, across retail and airline domains, checking whether the final database state matches the required outcome.

tau2airline.text: The airline customer service domain of tau2-bench: the agent follows an airline policy document and calls booking tools while talking to a simulated customer, scored by comparing the final database state and required actions with an annotated goal.

tau2bench.text: Evaluates conversational agents in a dual-control setting where both the agent and a simulated user can call tools to change a shared environment, built around a telecom domain modeled as a Dec-POMDP.

tau2benchtelecom.text: The telecom domain of tau2-bench, a dual-control setting modeled as a Dec-POMDP in which the customer support agent and the simulated user both hold tools and must coordinate to change a shared device state.

tau2retail.text: The retail domain of tau2-bench, where an agent handles e-commerce account requests over multiple turns using a domain toolset while following a written policy document, in a dual-control setting where the simulated user can also call tools.

tau3banking.text: The banking domain of the tau-bench knowledge track: an agent handles fintech customer support conversations, retrieving from roughly 700 interconnected knowledge documents while making tool-mediated account updates that must be verifiable and policy-compliant.

tau3bench.text: The third release of the tau-bench agent suite, covering retail, airline, telecom and banking domains, where an agent talks to a simulated user, calls tools, retrieves policy documents and is scored on verifiable database end states.

taubenchairline.text: The airline domain of tau-bench, where an agent handles a simulated customer conversation using airline APIs and a policy document; a run passes only if the final database state matches the annotated goal state.

taubenchretail.text: The retail domain of tau-bench: an agent handles a customer service conversation with an LLM-simulated user using domain API tools and written policy rules, and is scored by comparing the final database state against an annotated goal state.

tempcompass.text: A video benchmark that isolates temporal understanding by pairing conflicting videos with identical static content but different speed, direction or order, asked in several answer formats and graded by a language model.

terminal-bench.text: 80 hand-written, human-verified command-line tasks, each shipped as a Docker environment with an instruction and a test script that checks whether the agent's work in the terminal actually succeeded.

terminalbench20.text: A curated set of 89 hard tasks in real computer terminal environments, each with its own container, a human-written solution, and tests that verify whether the agent's end state is correct.

terminalbench21.text: A verified refresh of Terminal-Bench 2.0 that repairs 28 of its 89 terminal agent tasks, fixing stale external dependencies, too-tight resource budgets, and instructions that did not match the tests.

terminalbench30.text: A community-sourced set of 74 terminal tasks across seven domains, extending Terminal-Bench beyond coding to artifacts like database snapshots, ML checkpoints, RTL designs, formal proofs and CAD files, with agent and verifier run in separate containers.

terminalbench40.text: The 4.0 release of Terminal-Bench, which scores agents on completing real software and systems tasks inside a live terminal; it drops saturated and flaky 3.0 tasks, revises verifiers and sets a flat eight hour agent timeout.

terminalbenchhard.text: The hard difficulty tier of Terminal-Bench, an agentic benchmark of terminal tasks spanning software engineering, system administration and data processing, checked by verification scripts run inside Docker containers.

terminalbenchscience01.text: 70 scientific research workflow tasks for terminal agents across life, physical, Earth, mathematical and engineering sciences, covering data analysis, simulation, optimization and signal processing, each verified against concrete artifacts the agent must produce.

textarena.text: An open-source collection of over 57 competitive text-based game environments (single-player, two-player and multi-player) for evaluating agentic skills such as negotiation, theory of mind and deception, with online play and TrueSkill ratings.

textcaps.text: About 145,000 captions over 28,000 images where the text printed in the scene matters, so a model must read that text, relate it to the visual context, and decide what to copy or paraphrase into the caption.

textvqa.text: A visual question answering dataset of 45,336 questions over 28,408 images where answering requires reading and reasoning about text that appears in the image.

tomato.text: 1,484 human-annotated questions over 1,417 videos across six task categories, designed so that questions cannot be answered from a single frame and require reading events as a continuous sequence.

toolathlon.text: 108 long-horizon agent tasks across 32 real software applications and 604 tools, from Google Calendar and Notion to Kubernetes and BigQuery, started from realistic environment states and checked by per-task verification scripts.

toolathlonverified.text: The verified final release of Toolathlon, a long-horizon tool-use benchmark over 600+ tools drawn from real software environments, with task prompts, ground truths and evaluators reviewed and aligned.

tooldecathlon.text: Also called Toolathlon, a benchmark of long-horizon agent tasks over 32 real applications and more than 600 tools, where a task typically needs around 20 tool calls and is verified by the final state of the environment.

toxicchat.text: A toxicity detection benchmark built from real user queries to an open-source chatbot rather than from social media text, targeting the nuanced phenomena specific to user-AI conversation.

toxigen.text: A machine-generated dataset of 274k toxic and benign statements about 13 minority groups, built with adversarial decoding to cover implicitly toxic language that classifiers miss.

triviaqa.text: A reading comprehension dataset of over 650K question-answer-evidence triples, built from trivia-enthusiast questions paired with independently gathered evidence documents, with compositional questions that often need cross-sentence reasoning.

truthfulqa.text: 817 questions across 38 categories, written so that a person holding a common misconception would answer falsely, testing whether a model repeats popular falsehoods it learned from human text.

tut17.text: TUT Acoustic Scenes 2017: binaural 10-second recordings made in Finland across 15 everyday environments such as buses, cafes, cars, forests, offices and parks, which a system must sort into one of the 15 scene classes.

tvbench.text: An open-source multiple-choice video question answering benchmark built so that questions cannot be solved from a single frame, from the text of the options alone, or from world knowledge, forcing temporal reasoning.

tvqa.text: A video question answering benchmark of 152,545 multiple-choice questions over 21,793 clips from six TV shows, where answering requires localizing the relevant moment, reading subtitle dialogue and recognizing visual detail.

tydiqa.text: 204,000 question-answer pairs in 11 typologically diverse languages, collected directly in each language from people who wanted the answer and did not yet know it, rather than by translation.

ucf101.text: An action recognition dataset of over 13,000 clips in 101 human action classes, about 27 hours of realistic user-uploaded video with camera motion and cluttered backgrounds.

unsafebench.text: A set of about 10,000 real-world and AI-generated images labelled safe or unsafe across 11 categories such as sexual, violent and hateful content, used to test image safety classifiers including ones built on vision-language models.

usamo25.text: The six proof problems of the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad, with model-written proofs graded by expert human annotators for rigour rather than scored on a final answer.

v.text: 191 high-resolution natural images with 191 questions split between attribute recognition and spatial relationship reasoning, testing whether a multimodal model can find small task-relevant details in visually crowded scenes.

vatex.text: A multilingual video description dataset of more than 41,250 videos and 825,000 English and Chinese captions, supporting multilingual video captioning and video-guided machine translation.

vbench.text: A video generation benchmark that decomposes quality into 16 disentangled dimensions such as subject consistency, motion smoothness, temporal flickering and spatial relationship, each with its own prompt suite and metric validated against human preference annotations.

vcr.text: Visual Caption Restoration: Wikipedia image and caption pairs in which part of the embedded text is occluded, so a model must recover the hidden words from pixel-level hints and context rather than plain OCR, in easy and hard splits.

vendingbench.text: A simulated environment in which an agent runs a vending machine business over a long horizon, balancing inventory, placing orders, setting prices and paying daily fees, to test sustained coherent decision-making.

vendingbench2.text: A year-long vending machine simulation from Andon Labs where the agent starts with $500 and must stay solvent against adversarial suppliers, delayed deliveries, refund requests and a daily fee, scored on the final cash balance.

vibeeval.text: 269 visual understanding prompts from Reka, including a 100-prompt hard subset, each with an expert-written gold response, scored by a model judge against that reference.

video-mme.text: 900 videos ranging from 11 seconds to an hour across six visual domains, with 2,700 manually written multiple-choice questions, testing video understanding with frames, subtitles and audio.

videoholmes.text: 1,837 questions over 270 manually annotated suspense short films, across seven tasks that require locating and connecting visual clues scattered through the film rather than reading a single segment.

videommmu.text: 300 expert-level videos and 900 annotated questions across six disciplines, organised into perception, comprehension and adaptation stages to measure how much a model learns from watching a video.

vidore2.text: The second version of the Visual Document Retrieval Benchmark, built from insurance, biomedical, economic and ESG document collections, using blind contextual querying so queries are less extractive, and emphasizing long-form and cross-document retrieval in several languages.

virologycapabilitiestest.text: 322 multimodal questions on troubleshooting wet-lab virology protocols, written with expert virologists, covering tacit and visual knowledge such as reading plaque assays and electron micrographs.

vision2web.text: A hierarchical website-development benchmark of 193 tasks in 16 categories with 918 prototype images and 1,255 test cases from real sites, spanning static UI-to-code generation, multi-page frontend reproduction and full-stack development.

vizwiz.text: A visual question answering dataset of over 31,000 photos taken by blind users with spoken questions about them, including questions that cannot be answered from the image at all.

vlmsareblind.text: BlindTest, a set of seven tasks on simple geometric images (overlapping circles, counting line intersections, identifying a circled letter) that are trivial for people and probe low-level visual perception.

vocalsound.text: Over 21,000 crowdsourced recordings from 3,365 speakers of six non-speech vocal sounds (laughter, sighs, coughs, throat clearing, sneezes and sniffs), with speaker metadata, for vocal sound classification.

voicebench.text: A multi-faceted benchmark for LLM-based voice assistants using real and synthetic spoken instructions that vary speaker characteristics, environment and content, rather than clean read speech.

voxpopuli.text: A multilingual speech corpus built from 2009 to 2020 European Parliament recordings: about 400K hours of unlabeled audio in 23 EU languages plus transcribed speech in 18 languages and accented non-native English.

vqa2.text: A balanced visual question answering dataset in which every question is paired with two similar images that yield different answers, so a model cannot answer from language priors alone.

vsibench.text: Over 5,000 question-answer pairs built on 288 egocentric indoor videos from ScanNet, ScanNet++ and ARKitScenes, covering eight spatial tasks of three kinds: configuration, measurement estimation and spatiotemporal reasoning.

vsr.text: Over 10,000 image and caption pairs labelled true or false for the spatial relation they assert, covering 66 English relations such as under, in front of and facing.

webarena.text: A self-hostable web environment with four functioning sites (shopping, a forum, a code host and a content management system) plus 812 long-horizon natural language tasks, scored on functional correctness of the end state rather than on matching an action trace.

webarenaverified.text: A re-audited release of WebArena in which every task, reference answer and evaluator was corrected, replacing brittle string matching with deterministic JSON and network-event checks; it ships the full 812 tasks plus a 258-task hard subset.

webdevarena.text: A live head-to-head arena where two models each build an interactive web app from the same user prompt, such as a chess game or a Hacker News clone, and human voters pick the better result, aggregated with a Bradley-Terry ranking.

webquestions.text: 6,642 question-answer pairs built from popular web search queries, mostly centered on a single named entity, with answers annotated as Freebase entities so the task is question answering against a knowledge graph.

webvoyager.text: Open-ended browsing tasks on 15 real websites for an end-to-end multimodal web agent that acts from screenshots, with completion judged automatically by a vision-language model.

wemath.text: 6.5K visual math problems decomposed into 67 knowledge concepts, scored on a four-dimensional diagnostic (insufficient knowledge, inadequate generalization, complete mastery, rote memorization) rather than only end-to-end answers.

wenetspeech.text: A multi-domain Mandarin speech corpus with over 10,000 hours of high-quality labelled audio collected from YouTube and podcasts, shipping three manually labelled evaluation sets: Dev, Test_Net from internet audio and Test_Meeting from real meeting recordings.

where2place.text: 100 real photographs of homes and offices, each paired with an instruction naming a vacant region relative to other objects and a separately annotated ground-truth mask. A model must output image points, scored by the fraction falling inside the mask.

widesearch.text: An agentic search benchmark of 200 hand-curated questions (100 English, 100 Chinese) from over 15 domains, each requiring an agent to collect many atomic facts and arrange them in a structured output that is verified item by item.

wildchat.text: A corpus of one million real user conversations with ChatGPT, collected with opt-in consent, spanning many languages and including toxic and adversarial use cases.

wildguardtest.text: A human-annotated safety moderation test set of about 5,000 labeled items covering vanilla and adversarial jailbreak prompts paired with refusal and compliance responses, used to score prompt harmfulness, response harmfulness and refusal detection.

winogender.text: Winograd schema style minimal pairs of sentences that differ only in the gender of a pronoun, used to measure gender bias in pronoun coreference resolution.

winogrande.text: A 44,000-problem pronoun resolution set in the style of the Winograd Schema Challenge, crowdsourced at scale and then filtered with the AFLITE adversarial algorithm to strip instances solvable from dataset-specific word associations.

wmdp.text: The Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy: 3,668 multiple-choice questions on biosecurity, cybersecurity and chemical security, used both to measure hazardous knowledge in a model and to test unlearning methods that remove it.

wmdpbio.text: The biosecurity split of WMDP, multiple-choice questions used as a proxy measure of hazardous biology knowledge in a model and as a testbed for unlearning methods, filtered to exclude genuinely sensitive information.

wmdpchem.text: The chemical security subset of WMDP, a set of multiple-choice questions written as a proxy measurement of hazardous knowledge, used both to probe dangerous capabilities and to test unlearning methods.

wmdpcyber.text: The cybersecurity portion of WMDP, multiple-choice questions written as a public proxy for hazardous offensive-security knowledge, used both to measure such knowledge in a model and to test unlearning methods meant to remove it.

wmt24.text: An extension of the WMT24 translation test set to 55 languages and dialects, adding newly collected human-written references and post-edits for 46 additional languages.

worldvqa.text: 3,500 visual questions across nine semantic categories that ask a model to name the specific entity shown, deliberately stripped of reasoning, OCR and multi-hop steps so the score reflects only memorized visual world knowledge.

writingbench.text: A generative writing benchmark spanning 6 core domains and 100 subdomains, scored by a critic model against assessment criteria that are generated per query rather than fixed in advance.

xbenchdeepsearch.text: The DeepSearch track of xbench: 100 Chinese questions that require an agent to use search tools and retrieve information, with answers checked against reference responses.

xcopa.text: A typologically diverse translation of the COPA causal commonsense task into 11 languages, including low-resource ones such as Eastern Apurimac Quechua and Haitian Creole, where a model picks the more plausible cause or effect.

xstest.text: A test suite for exaggerated safety: 250 safe prompts across ten types that a well-calibrated model should answer, paired with 200 unsafe prompts that are lexically similar and should be refused.

xstorycloze.text: The English StoryCloze set professionally translated into 10 further languages: given four sentences of a story, the model picks which of two endings is correct.

xwinograd.text: Winograd schema pronoun resolution in six languages (English, Japanese, Chinese, Russian, Portuguese and French), where a sentence with an ambiguous blank must be resolved to one of two candidate entities.

youcook2.text: A procedure segmentation dataset of instructional cooking videos from YouTube, in which each recipe step is temporally localized within the video and described in natural language, supporting segmentation and dense video captioning.

zebralogic.text: Logic grid puzzles generated from constraint satisfaction problems at controlled difficulty, used to measure how logical reasoning holds up as the search space and number of constraints grow.

zerobench.text: 100 hand-designed visual reasoning questions plus 334 subquestions that isolate their individual steps, curated by adversarial filtering so that frontier multimodal models solved none of the main questions at release.

agenticmisalignment.text: Hypothetical corporate scenarios where a model with email access and an assigned business goal faces replacement or a goal conflict, testing whether it turns to blackmail or to leaking information.

frontiercode.text: Coding tasks authored by maintainers of 36 flagship open-source repositories, graded not only on passing tests but on whether the patch is scoped, styled and tested well enough that a maintainer would merge it.

cmmmu.text: About 12,000 Chinese multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes and textbooks across six disciplines and 30 subjects, paired with charts, diagrams, maps, music sheets and chemical structures.

piletest.text: The held-out test split of the Pile, an English corpus assembled from 22 subsets drawn largely from academic and professional sources; language models are scored in bits per UTF-8 byte so tokenizers stay comparable.

anlir3.text: The third round of Adversarial NLI, in which annotators wrote premise and hypothesis pairs designed to fool a model in the loop into the wrong entailment, neutral or contradiction label.

bchepython.text: The Python column of BabelCode-translated HumanEval, which ports the benchmark's problems and unit tests into a single execution harness so the same programs can be run and graded across many languages.

clicklinks.text: One arm of the Hidden Agenda persuasion study: a model holds an innocuous conversation with a human participant while secretly trying to get them to click a suspicious link, measured by how many comply.

doccitestpivots.text: One thousand images sampled from DOCCI's test split, each grouped with four visually similar distractors, used to check whether a long description of the pivot image picks it out of its group.

geneturing.text: Genomics question answering grouped into four categories: nomenclature, genomic location, functional analysis and sequence alignment, each module asking for a short factual answer of the kind found in genomic databases.

intercodectf.text: Capture-the-flag challenges collected from picoCTF: given a natural language prompt and the task's files, an agent works in a Bash shell and must submit the recovered flag, which is matched against the gold value.

microvqa.text: 1,042 expert-written multiple-choice questions over microscopy images, probing image interpretation, hypothesis generation and experiment design, with options rewritten by an agent to strip language shortcuts.

pixmopoint.text: A pointing evaluation set from the PixMo collection: each item pairs an image with an object name or referring expression, and the model must return pixel coordinates for the matching objects, checked against human annotations.

secretpatch.text: Code diffs from open-source projects labelled by whether they silently fix a security bug; the model must classify each diff as security related or not.

therapeuticdatacommons.text: A platform of AI-ready therapeutics datasets spanning 22 learning tasks across drug discovery and development, packaged with standard data splits, evaluation strategies and molecule generation oracles.

agievalenglish.text: The English portion of AGIEval, built from questions taken out of human standardized exams such as college entrance tests, law school admission tests and math competitions, in multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blank form.

coin.text: 11,827 instructional videos covering 180 everyday tasks in 12 domains, annotated with ordered step descriptions and the temporal boundaries of each step.

gorillabenchmarkapibench.text: Natural language requests paired with machine learning API calls gathered from HuggingFace, TorchHub and TensorHub, testing whether a model picks a real API with correct arguments instead of inventing one.

longcodecompletionlcc.text: Code completion examples filtered from GitHub for unusually long files, averaging roughly five times the preceding context of earlier completion datasets, so distant imports and definitions matter.

ndd20.text: Above-water and underwater photographs of two dolphin species collected off the Northumberland coast, annotated for both coarse and fine-grained instance segmentation and categorisation.

plmsgqa.text: 665 human-written open-ended questions about egocentric video recorded on consumer smart glasses, asked at the moment the clip ends, with answers graded by an LLM judge.

stanfordcars.text: Fine-grained image classification over 196 car classes, using 16,185 photographs split into roughly equal training and test halves.

olmocrbench.text: 1,403 PDFs with 7,010 unit tests covering arXiv math papers, old scans and other documents, checking a converter's markdown output for text presence and absence, reading order, tables and equations.

triviaqaspeech.text: A speech-synthesized version of TriviaQA: questions are first filtered and rewritten to be sayable, then rendered as audio, so the model must answer from listening rather than reading.

finsearchcompt2t3.text: The two historical task types of FinSearchComp, annotated by professional financial experts: fixed point-in-time lookups (T2) and multi-period investigations (T3) that an agent must answer by searching open sources.

mcpmarkverified.text: The stabilized default task set of MCPMark, with every environment version-pinned and every verifier fixed: agentic tasks over Notion, GitHub, filesystem, Postgres and Playwright MCP servers, each checked by a script.

arcagi1verified.text: 800 grid puzzles in which roughly three example input-output pairs define a transformation to infer and apply to a new grid, with figures produced by runs the ARC Prize Foundation conducts itself.

internationalolympiadininformaticsioi.text: Algorithmic programming problems from the annual International Olympiad in Informatics, attempted under contest conditions: six problems, ten hours, a capped number of submissions, and the official test data.

scalemcpatlas.text: Tool-use tasks spanning 36 real MCP servers and 220 tools, with prompts that deliberately avoid naming any tool so the agent must find and chain three to six calls, graded against a claims-based rubric.

timehorizon11.text: METR's updated time horizon measurement: agentic software and reasoning tasks are labelled with how long human experts need, and model results are fitted to the human task length completed half the time.

alfred.text: Household tasks in interactive 3D environments where an agent turns a high-level goal plus step-by-step directives into actions from egocentric vision, covering 25,000 natural language directives.

libero.text: Four suites totalling 130 procedurally generated simulated robot manipulation tasks, each shipped with human teleoperated demonstrations, built to study how knowledge transfers across a sequence of tasks.

mceval.text: 16,000 test samples spanning 40 programming languages, with code completion, understanding and generation tasks curated per language rather than translated from Python originals.

okapimmlu.text: MMLU's multiple-choice exam questions translated into dozens of languages, released as part of the Okapi multilingual instruction-tuning project.

pmcvqa.text: Medical visual question answering built from figures in PubMed Central articles, spanning many imaging modalities and diseases, with a manually verified test split scored on free-form generated answers.

speechio.text: Mandarin speech recognition test sets transcribed by paid professional annotators, drawn from news broadcasts, interviews, live streams, podcasts and film, and scored by character error rate.

vlad.text: Close-form driving questions spanning five domains, from traffic knowledge and element recognition through traffic graphs to ego decision-making, broken into 11 secondary aspects and 29 tertiary tasks.

koarenahardauto.text: The Arena-Hard-Auto v0.1 prompt set translated into Korean by LLMs and then checked by hand, used as the question set for automatic, model-judged evaluation of Korean responses.

lmarenatextleaderboard.text: A crowdsourced ranking of chat models in which users send their own prompt to two anonymous models and vote for the better reply, with the pairwise votes aggregated by statistical ranking methods.

bddx.text: Driving video segments from Berkeley DeepDrive paired with human written descriptions of what the vehicle did and why, aligned to the time interval in which each action occurs.

omniact.text: Screenshots of desktop and web applications paired with visually grounded natural language tasks, where the model must emit an executable script that carries the task out.

vabwebarenalite.text: The web environment of VisualAgentBench: a lightened task set built on the self-hosted WebArena and VisualWebArena sites, where a multimodal agent completes browsing tasks from visual input.

usmle.text: Official multiple-choice practice questions for the three Steps of the United States Medical Licensing Examination, administered as text with tables transcribed and images such as X-rays removed.

mcpuniverse.text: Agent tasks run against 11 real Model Context Protocol servers across six domains including location navigation, repository management and financial analysis, checked by execution-based evaluators that fetch live ground truth for time-sensitive answers.

tabmwp.text: 38,431 open-domain grade-school math word problems, each paired with a table given as an image, as semi-structured text and as a structured table, in free-text and multiple-choice form with annotated solution steps.

asimov20physicalsafetybenchmark.text: Physical-safety evaluations for embodied AI, grounded in real-world injury narratives and operational safety constraints that are turned into photorealistic images and videos of safe-to-unsafe transitions, testing whether a model perceives the risk and intervenes.

coir.text: Ten curated code retrieval datasets spanning eight retrieval tasks across seven domains, packaged as a pip-installable framework that shares its data schema with BEIR and MTEB.

evabench.text: End-to-end voice agent evaluation that orchestrates bot-to-bot audio conversations over 213 scenarios in three enterprise domains, with a controlled perturbation suite for accent and noise robustness and separate accuracy and experience metrics.

harveyslegalagentbenchmark.text: Open-source agent tasks covering real legal work across 24 practice areas, each supplying agent instructions and documents; an execution harness runs the agent and a model judge scores it against expert-written rubrics under all-pass criteria.

lbpp2.text: The multilingual second version of the Less Basic Python Programming set, extending its unit-tested, deliberately unleaked problems from Python into C++, Java, JavaScript, Rust and Go as approximately parallel translations.

monashforecastingarchive.text: Twenty public time series datasets from varied domains, differing in frequency, series length and missing values, gathered so global forecasting algorithms can be compared on a common collection with standard baselines and eight error metrics.

nejmcpc.text: 303 clinicopathological case reports from the New England Journal of Medicine, where a model reads the text-only case and returns a differential diagnosis list of ten candidates, scored on whether the correct diagnosis appears.

usmlemm.text: 46 multimodal multiple-choice questions taken from the official USMLE sample exams for Steps 1, 2 and 3, each containing an image the model must read alongside the question text.

xlsum.text: One million professionally annotated article and summary pairs extracted from BBC news in 44 languages, used to test abstractive summarization well beyond high-resource languages.

bfcl2.text: The Live edition of the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard: 2,251 query, function-documentation and answer triples contributed by real users, so the tool schemas and questions are not drawn from a curated set models may have trained on.

dollarstreet.text: A geographically diverse image set of household items, assembled with broader country coverage than standard object-recognition data so systems can be tested for accuracy gaps across countries and household income levels.

imagenetc.text: A robustness benchmark that applies common image corruptions to ImageNet and measures how far classifier accuracy degrades, targeting everyday distortions rather than worst-case adversarial perturbations.

mbppevalplus.text: The EvalPlus edition of MBPP: 378 Python programming tasks kept from the original set, each checked against roughly 35 times as many automatically generated test cases, so code that passes the original tests but is wrong is caught.

ovis.text: A video instance segmentation benchmark for heavily occluded scenes, with 296,000 instance masks over 25 semantic categories that a model must detect, segment and track through the occlusions.

saco.text: A benchmark for promptable concept segmentation: given a short noun phrase, an image exemplar, or both, a model must return masks and stable identities for every matching instance across images and videos.

tldr9.text: Over nine million Reddit posts paired with their author-written TL;DR line for extreme summarization, plus a smaller human-annotated high-quality subset distilled from it.

arabicmtbenchdev.text: An Arabic translation of MT-Bench's 80 open-ended multi-turn prompts, reviewed by humans and adjusted for Arabic cultural context, with GPT-4 acting as a uniform judge across both languages.

fleursspeechtranslation.text: The translation task of FLEURS, an n-way parallel spoken corpus in 102 languages built on top of the FLoRes-101 machine translation benchmark with roughly 12 hours of speech supervision per language.

sbcsae.text: Sixty roughly 20-minute stereo recordings of naturally occurring spoken interaction from across the United States, released with transcripts and time marks aligned at the level of individual intonation units.

infovqatest.text: The test split of InfographicVQA: natural language questions over infographic images that require joint reasoning about document layout, textual content, graphical elements and data visualisations, plus basic arithmetic.

ojbenchcpp.text: The C++ track of OJBench: 232 problems taken from China's National Olympiad in Informatics and the ICPC, sorted into three difficulty bands using contestant votes and real submission data.

apbiology.text: A simulated sitting of the College Board's Advanced Placement biology exam, combining publicly released multiple-choice questions with the 2022 free-response prompts and scored using the College Board's own published methodology.

frontiermathtier42.text: The 43-problem expansion tier of FrontierMath, made of research-level mathematics problems that take a specialist days, as revised in the June 2026 update. The model answers by writing a Python function that returns the value.

piimasking300k.text: Roughly 300,000 synthetic, human-validated text samples in six languages with personally identifiable information spans labelled, split into an open-domain set of 27 PII classes and a finance and insurance set, for training and testing privacy masking.

swelancerdiamondicswe.text: The public Diamond split of SWE-Lancer, restricted to its individual-contributor coding tasks: real paid freelance jobs from Upwork, graded by end-to-end tests triple-verified by experienced software engineers.

avut.text: Audio-centric video question answering, with tasks built so the soundtrack and audio-visual interaction are needed rather than the picture alone, filtered by an answer-permutation mechanism so questions cannot be solved from their text.

codeinterpreterbenchmark.text: Qwen's open-sourced test of a model's use of a Python code interpreter for mathematics, data visualisation and general tasks such as file handling and web scraping, measuring both whether the generated code executes and whether its result is correct.

expressbench.text: 777 exploration trajectories and 2,044 question-trajectory pairs for embodied question answering, scoring both how efficiently an agent explores the 3D scene and whether it then answers correctly.

gedit.text: An image editing benchmark rooted in real-world user editing instructions rather than synthetic prompts, used to assess how faithfully a model applies a requested edit to a reference image.

ifevalstrictprompt.text: The strict prompt-level scoring of IFEval, where a prompt counts only when a program checking the literal response finds every one of its verifiable instructions, such as word counts or required keywords, satisfied.

livecodebench625022505.text: The v6 release of LiveCodeBench narrowed to a recent window of problems: competitive programming tasks collected continuously from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces and graded by the contests' own tests, so problems postdate a model's training data.

mixeval.text: A benchmark assembled by mining real user queries from the web and matching each to a similar question from existing ground-truth benchmarks, so grading stays automatic while the query mix reflects real use.

mtaime24.text: The machine-translated AIME 2024 subset of the MCLM multilingual math suite: 30 competition problems per language across 55 languages, checked by a rule-based answer verifier.

navsim.text: A middle ground between open-loop and closed-loop driving evaluation: bird's eye view abstractions of real recorded scenes are unrolled for a short horizon in a non-reactive simulator to compute metrics such as progress and time to collision.

oneigbenchtextzh.text: The Chinese text-rendering split of OneIG-Bench: 200 prompts that ask a text-to-image model to render specified characters precisely inside the generated image.

prbenchlegal.text: The Law half of Professional Reasoning Bench: open-ended legal tasks written by qualified practitioners and graded against expert-curated rubrics, from a set of 1,100 tasks and 19,356 criteria spanning 114 countries and 47 US jurisdictions.

refspatialbench.text: 277 samples from cluttered real-world scenes where a model must output a 2D point satisfying a multi-step spatial referring instruction, split into locating a unique object, locating free space for placement, and an unseen-relation set.

seccodebench.text: A suite for evaluating the security of code produced by language models and agentic coding tools, built by Alibaba with several university security groups to address quality gaps in datasets scraped from open-source repositories.

unisvg.text: A 525,000-item scalable vector graphics dataset covering both directions of SVG work: generating SVG code from text prompts or reference images, and answering questions about an SVG's colour, category and usage.

wenetspeechnet.text: The Test_Net split of WenetSpeech, a manually transcribed Mandarin speech recognition test set collected from internet audio so that it matches the domains of the corpus's training data.

haerae.text: Korean questions across vocabulary, history, general knowledge and reading comprehension, written to require Korean cultural and contextual depth rather than being translated from English tests.

komtbench.text: MT-Bench's 80 multi-turn instruction-following questions translated into Korean, with some rewritten to reflect Korean linguistic and cultural nuance and the whole set reviewed by expert linguists.

deepswe10.text: Long-horizon software engineering tasks written fresh against active open-source repositories in TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust, each run in an isolated environment and checked by a program-based verifier.

drivelm.text: Graph-structured visual question answering for driving, linking perception, prediction and planning questions so a model reasons through the steps a human driver takes, instantiated on nuScenes and CARLA data.

roboaffordeval.text: 338 annotated real-world images testing affordance prediction by vision-language models on three tasks: identifying an object from attributes and spatial relations, pinpointing the functional part to grasp, and locating free space for placement.

ccbench.text: 74 real-world coding tasks across frontend, application development, UI work, build and deployment, data analysis and machine learning, run through Claude Code in fresh containers with a human evaluator driving several rounds of interaction.

libriother.text: The harder 'other' split of LibriSpeech, the 1,000-hour corpus of read English speech from LibriVox audiobooks, set aside as more challenging than the 'clean' split.

safetybench.text: 11,435 multiple-choice questions in Chinese and English spanning seven categories of safety concern, used to probe what a model understands about unsafe content.

webshop.text: A simulated e-commerce site with 1.18 million real products and 12,087 crowd-sourced text instructions, where an agent must navigate pages, reformulate queries and customise an item to meet the stated requirement.

vendingbencharena.text: A multi-agent version of the Vending-Bench 2 simulation: several models each run their own vending machine at the same location and can email, pay and trade with one another, and each is scored on its own closing balance.

mgsmzh.text: The Chinese split of Multilingual Grade School Math: 250 GSM8K word problems hand translated into Chinese, which the model must work through step by step in that language.

usaco.text: 307 competitive programming problems from the USA Computing Olympiad, each shipped with reference code, an official analysis and unit tests that decide whether a submitted solution counts as correct.

asimovagentic.text: A robot safety suite covering single-turn agentic decisions, gauge reading under glare and occlusion, closed-loop tool calling and human proximity detection, testing whether an agent refuses unsafe actions and asks for help when uncertain.

bigbench.text: 204 tasks contributed by 450 authors at 132 institutions, spanning linguistics, mathematics, common sense, biology, physics, social bias and software, chosen to sit beyond what language models could do at the time.

copa.text: A causal commonsense task: given a premise sentence, the system picks which of two alternatives is its more plausible cause or effect, over 500 handcrafted test items drawn from blogs and a photography encyclopedia.

eyepacs.text: De-identified 45-degree retinal fundus photographs from a diabetic retinopathy screening service, posed as a five-way severity choice (none, mild, moderate, severe, proliferative) against clinically determined labels.

healthsearchqa.text: 3,375 consumer medical questions curated from what people commonly type into a search engine, answered in free text and rated by clinicians for agreement with consensus, missing content and possible harm.

livecodebenchcodegeneration.text: The code generation scenario of a continuously refreshed contest benchmark: problems collected from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces after a set release date, run against the contests' own test cases to limit contamination.

nejmimagechallenge.text: Weekly diagnostic quizzes from the New England Journal of Medicine, each pairing a clinical image with a short case summary and multiple-choice options from which the model must pick the correct diagnosis.

recipe1m.text: Over a million structured cooking recipes, with titles, ingredient lists and instructions, paired with food photographs and used to test cross-modal retrieval between recipe text and images.

speechagentarena.text: Paid participants complete the same scenario as two live voice calls with hidden speech-to-speech models and then vote for one; 15 of the 35 scenarios require tool calls, which are separately checked for completion.

valsfinanceagent2.text: 927 expert-reviewed financial analyst tasks over SEC filings and related documents, across nine categories from retrieval to financial modelling, graded with severity-weighted partial credit and a stricter all-pass variant.

xm3600.text: 3,600 geographically diverse images with human-written captions in 36 languages, built as a reference set for evaluating multilingual image captioning without the artefacts of direct translation.

doors.text: Synthetic Blender-rendered imagery of boulders on the surfaces of small celestial bodies, annotated for segmentation to support hazard detection and vision-based navigation during close proximity operations.

imagenetreal.text: Re-collected labels for the ImageNet validation set, gathered with a more robust annotation procedure, so classifiers are scored against these reassessed labels rather than the original ones.

met.text: Around 224,000 classes, one per museum exhibit, trained on studio photographs from the Metropolitan Museum's open access collection and tested on visitor snapshots plus unrelated images, as instance-level recognition.

sacobio.text: The biomedical split of the SA-Co concept segmentation benchmark, assembled from existing microscopy and medical datasets: about 5,400 images and 166 noun phrases whose every matching instance must be masked.

trashcan.text: Underwater imagery of marine debris annotated with bounding boxes and segmentation masks, released in two class configurations, one grouping objects by material and one by object type.

arabictydiqagoldp.text: The Arabic subset of the TyDi QA gold passage task, a SQuAD-style setup in which the system must identify the answer span inside a passage already known to contain it.

fleurstranslation.text: The translation setting of FLEURS, an n-way parallel read-speech corpus in 102 languages built on the FLoRes-101 text benchmark, with roughly 12 hours of supervision per language.

kotlinhumaneval.text: All 161 HumanEval problems rewritten in Kotlin, with solutions and tests authored by an expert Kotlin programmer and independently checked by a second one; generated code is executed against those tests.

infovqaval.text: The validation split of InfographicVQA, whose questions over infographic images require reading text, layout, graphical elements and data visualisations together, often with elementary arithmetic or comparison.

openaudiobench.text: About 2,900 spoken questions gathered from five sub-sets (Reasoning QA, Llama Questions, Web Questions, TriviaQA and AlpacaEval), covering audio reasoning, general knowledge and open-ended replies.

apcalculusbc.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement Calculus BC exam used as an eval: 45 multiple-choice questions plus six free-response questions, combined into a final grade using the published AP scoring methodology.

capturetheflagctfchallenges.text: Offensive security exercises in which a model working from a Linux tooling image must recover a hidden text flag from a deliberately vulnerable system, across web exploitation, reverse engineering, binary exploitation and cryptography.

cybersecurityctfs.text: Over a hundred curated hacking-competition tasks split into high school, collegiate and professional tiers, most selected to need at least two chained exploitation steps rather than a textbook example.

fullduplexbench1.text: An evaluation of spoken dialogue systems that listen and speak at the same time, covering four interactive behaviours: pause handling, backchannelling, turn taking and interruption, all measured with automatic metrics.

instructionhierarchy.text: Adversarial tests of whether a model gives system messages priority over user text and tool output, covering direct and indirect prompt injection, system prompt and password extraction and jailbreaks, paired with over-refusal sets of benign lower-privilege instructions.

leetcodeeasy.text: The 41 easy-tier problems in the LeetCode slice of GPT-4's exam suite, taken from publicly available problems and cross-checked against the training data for contamination.

voicenativeevaluationssyntheticprompts.text: Safety prompts written from OpenAI's own policies to cover borderline and rarely sampled cases, then synthesised into speech and played to the model to check whether the intended behaviour survives in spoken form.

dialogcantonese.text: An in-house conversational Cantonese test set from Qwen3-ASR's robustness suite, used to measure transcription character error rate on multi-speaker dialectal dialogue.

extremenoise.text: A Mandarin speech test set recorded at extremely low signal-to-noise ratios, part of the in-house robustness suite used to stress test Qwen3-ASR transcription under difficult acoustic conditions.

geditbenchcn.text: The Chinese instruction track of the GEdit image editing benchmark: 606 real user edit requests gathered from the internet and sorted into 11 categories, with results rated by a multimodal judge for semantic consistency and perceptual quality.

mlcslm.text: Roughly 1,604 hours of real multilingual conversational speech released for an Interspeech challenge, with one task for transcribing the conversations and a second that also requires speaker diarisation from unsegmented audio.

mtebr.text: The retrieval subset of the English MTEB benchmark, used to score rerankers by having them reorder the top 100 documents an embedding model returned for each query.

onemillionbench.text: 400 professional questions, half Chinese and half English, spread across healthcare, finance, industry, law and natural science, each graded by a judge model against 5 to 23 weighted yes or no rubric items.

presentbench.text: 238 slide-deck generation tasks, each supplying around 34 pages of source material and an average of 54 binary checklist items covering layout, completeness, correctness and fidelity to the source, scored by a judge model.

repoeval.text: A repository-level code completion benchmark built from recent real-world projects, covering three granularities: finishing a line, completing an API invocation and writing a whole function body.

urobenchpro.text: The advanced half of URO-Bench, 20 test sets probing understanding, reasoning and oral conversation in end-to-end speech-to-speech models, including multilingual, multi-round and paralinguistic cases.

wenetspeechnetmeeting.text: Two manually annotated evaluation sets from the WenetSpeech Mandarin corpus: TEST_NET, internet-sourced audio matched to the training domain, and TEST_MEETING, real meeting recordings used as the harder mismatched condition.

haerae11.text: A Korean benchmark of six tasks across vocabulary, history, general knowledge and reading comprehension, written natively rather than back-translated so that knowledge cannot simply transfer from English.

kormedmcqa.text: 7,469 multiple-choice questions drawn from Korean healthcare licensing examinations sat between 2012 and 2024 for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and dentists.

egoplan2.text: Egocentric video planning questions covering four domains and 24 everyday scenarios, built semi-automatically and manually verified, asking a model to choose a reasonable next action given the current visual state.

roborefit.text: 10,872 real RGB-D images of graspable objects across 187 indoor scenes and 66 categories, paired with 50,758 referring expressions and annotated with boxes and masks, with many images holding look-alike distractors.

libritts.text: 585 hours of read English speech from 2,456 speakers at 24 kHz, derived from LibriSpeech and reprocessed to suit text-to-speech work rather than recognition.

sciworld.text: A text-based interactive environment built around the elementary school science curriculum, where an agent must run experiments to settle a question rather than recall a stated fact about it.

webvoyagersom.text: 643 task queries across 15 live websites, attempted from screenshots whose interactive elements are overlaid with bounding boxes, with GPT-4V shown the last few screenshots to judge whether the task was completed.

browsecompplus.text: Pairs BrowseComp's queries with a fixed corpus of roughly 100,000 documents, including human-verified supporting pages and mined hard negatives, so the retriever and the agent can be evaluated separately.

linuxarena.text: An AI control setting built on 20 live multi-service Linux production environments, with 1,671 legitimate software engineering tasks and 184 hidden side tasks such as data exfiltration or backdooring, used to test both sabotage and monitoring.

vibench.text: Evaluates end-to-end vibe coding: agents build web applications from natural-language product requirement documents taken from real production traces, covering both zero-to-one builds and feature extensions, and are graded by per-app test plans.

minif2ftest.text: One of the two even halves of miniF2F, whose 488 statements come from AIME, AMC and IMO problems plus high school and undergraduate coursework, each formalized in Lean, Metamath, Isabelle or HOL Light so a generated proof can be machine checked.

asimovinjury.text: Derived from 2023 hospital records in the US National Electronic Injury Surveillance System: generative models expand each real injury case into contexts and candidate actions, and the model must judge whether an action makes injury more or less likely.

cosmosreason1.text: NVIDIA's paired benchmarks for physical AI: 604 binary and multiple-choice questions over 426 internet videos on space, time and fundamental physics, plus 612 multiple-choice questions over 600 robot, egocentric and driving videos on embodied reasoning.

factsbenchmarksuite.text: Google's four-part factuality suite covering grounding in a supplied document, parametric knowledge without tools, web search use, and image-based prompts, with a public and a held-out private example set for each part.

livecodebenchpro.text: 584 problems captured from live Codeforces, ICPC and IOI contests as they appear, annotated for algorithmic category by international olympiad medalists who also analyze failed submissions line by line.

moviegenbench.text: Meta's two media generation prompt sets released with Movie Gen: 1,003 text-to-video prompts tagged by concept and motion level, plus 527 videos with sound prompts for video-to-audio and text-plus-video-to-audio generation.

neptune.text: Multiple-choice and open-ended question answering over videos up to 15 minutes long, with captions, questions and decoy answers produced by a VLM and LLM pipeline, and open-ended answers scored by the GEM model-based metric.

record.text: Cloze-style reading comprehension over CNN and Daily Mail news: an entity is removed from a summarizing sentence and the system must pick the right entity from candidates in the passage, across more than 120,000 crowd-validated queries.

vatexcaptioning.text: The captioning task over VATEX, a set of more than 41,250 video clips covering 600 human activities with 825,000 English and Chinese captions, where a model must describe a clip in each language.

xorqainen.text: Cross-lingual question answering from IndicGenBench: a question written in one of 29 Indic languages is paired with an English passage and the model returns a short answer span, with this variant scored against the English answer.

biotier1.text: 542 expert-written biology prompts split across catastrophe avoidance, biomedical dual-use research and ordinary related biology, used to check whether a model refuses the narrow high-risk sets while still answering the benign one.

dram.text: Semantic segmentation of figurative paintings from four art movements (Realism, Impressionism, Post-Impressionism and Expressionism), gathered mainly from WikiArt, with pixel labels only on the test paintings so training must transfer from photographs.

impossiblebench.text: Turns LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench tasks impossible by making the unit tests directly contradict the written specification, so any pass means the agent modified or gamed the tests instead of solving the problem.

miap.text: An Open Images Extended relabeling of 100,000 images of people: roughly 454,000 boxes drawn for a gender and age agnostic person class, each then labelled with perceived gender presentation and perceived age range for fairness evaluation.

paris.text: Landmark image retrieval over roughly 6,000 Flickr photographs of Paris buildings: 70 cropped query regions must be ranked against the whole collection, under three protocols of increasing difficulty.

sacobronze.text: The split of SAM 3's SA-Co benchmark assembled from nine existing datasets, with masks taken from their annotations or generated by prompting SAM 2 with boxes; the model must segment every instance matching a short text phrase.

triviaqawiki.text: The Wikipedia-evidence half of TriviaQA: trivia enthusiasts wrote the questions, Wikipedia pages were gathered afterwards as supporting evidence, and all documents for a question are pooled so scoring is per question.

aubenchmark.text: Mistral's in-house audio understanding set: 40 long-form audio recordings paired with challenging questions that the model must answer directly from the audio rather than from a transcript.

flteval.text: Lean proof engineering tasks taken from real pull requests to the Fermat's Last Theorem formalization repository, shaped like SWE-bench: a submitted diff is applied inside the task's Docker image and checked by Lean and SafeVerify against fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests.

simplesafetytests.text: 100 handwritten English prompts across five harm areas, including suicide and self-harm, physical harm and illegal items, that a general purpose model should refuse; every response was labelled by trained annotators.

aiofficebenchmark.text: Moonshot's internal productivity evaluation: the model must produce finished office deliverables end to end, including documents, spreadsheets, PDFs and slide decks, with output quality compared side by side against a baseline model.

paperbenchcodedev.text: The lightweight variant of PaperBench: agents reimplement 20 ICML 2024 papers and an LLM judge grades only the code development leaf nodes of each author-written rubric, skipping the execution and result-matching checks.

apchemistry.text: The College Board's high school chemistry exam: 60 multiple-choice questions plus seven free-response questions (three long and four short) on chemical models, experiment design and quantitative problem solving.

deceptionevaluationswithrepresentativepr.text: Prompts drawn from ChatGPT traffic that had previously elicited deception, where chain-of-thought monitors check whether the user-facing reply misrepresents the model's reasoning or actions, such as claiming to have run a tool it never ran.

fullduplexbench15.text: Automated probing of how a spoken dialogue model behaves when speech overlaps, across four scenarios (user interruption, backchannel, talking to others and background speech), reporting dialogue behaviour categories, stop and response latency, and prosodic adaptation.

belebele.text: Parallel multiple-choice reading comprehension in 122 language variants: each item gives a short Flores-200 passage and four answer options, curated to separate models by depth of language comprehension.

collegemath.text: 2,818 test problems extracted from nine college mathematics textbooks spanning algebra, pre-calculus, calculus, vector calculus, probability, linear algebra and differential equations, with several of those topics held out of the training split entirely.

dialogchinesedialects.text: An internal Qwen speech recognition test set covering 22 Chinese dialects, reported as a character error rate averaged across the dialects.

ezpoint.text: A card game task used in Qwen2-VL's agent evaluation: the model must combine the numbers on the dealt cards with basic arithmetic operations to reach a total of 12.

geditbenchen.text: The English half of GEdit-Bench, 606 real image editing requests filtered from user posts on sites such as Reddit across 11 editing categories, scored by a vision-language judge on semantic consistency and perceptual quality.

longtextbenchen.text: The English half of LongText-Bench, 160 prompts across eight scenarios that test whether an image generator can render long passages of text accurately and consistently.

mlcslmen.text: The English portion of the MLC-SLM challenge corpus: around 500 hours of two-speaker, roughly 20-minute conversational recordings spanning American, Australian, British, Filipino and Indian accents, transcribed and scored by word error rate.

needlebench.text: Bilingual long-context testing at adaptive context lengths, combining information-sparse needle retrieval with an information-dense Ancestral Trace Challenge whose relevant facts are spread continuously through the context.

opencpop.text: A studio-quality Mandarin singing corpus: 100 pop songs recorded at 44.1 kHz by a single professional female singer, annotated with lyrics, musical scores and phoneme and note boundaries, built for singing voice synthesis.

processbench.text: 3,400 step-by-step solutions to competition and olympiad mathematics problems, each annotated by human experts, where the model must name the earliest erroneous step or state that every step is correct.

reverie.text: Vision-and-language navigation through previously unseen real indoor environments: given a natural-language instruction, the agent picks its next viewpoint from the current observation and must finally localize the object referred to.

tau1airline.text: The airline domain of tau-bench: a tool-using agent serves a customer simulated by a language model while following the domain's written policy, and is scored by comparing the final database state against an annotated goal state.

videodrwsearch.text: 500 video-conditioned open-domain questions across six subject areas, filtered so neither the video nor the web alone suffices: the model must extract visual anchors across frames, search the open web, and reason over both, with a model judge checking answers.

wenetspeechwsnetmeeting.text: The TEST_NET and TEST_MEETING evaluation sets of WenetSpeech, a 22,400-hour Mandarin corpus collected from YouTube and podcasts; the first is matched internet audio and the second is harder real meeting audio.

hmmt2025nov.text: Short-answer olympiad-style problem sets from the November 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, covering the General and Theme individual rounds, the team round and the 36-problem Guts round.

marcja.text: The JGLUE text classification task built from the Japanese half of the Multilingual Amazon Reviews Corpus: star ratings become positive or negative labels with three-star reviews dropped, and dev and test items are kept only on crowdworker consensus.

eebench.text: Analog circuit design tasks that put an agent through the requirements, design and test loop. Submissions are verified deterministically by simulation and by building the circuit graph and bill of materials, with parts cost weighed alongside technical performance.

sweatlasqna.text: 124 deep code comprehension tasks over 11 open-source Go, Python, C and TypeScript repositories, each pinned in a Docker image: the agent must trace execution and answer a technical question without editing source, graded item by item against an expert rubric.

frontiersweimpl.text: The implementation track of FrontierSWE, an ultra-long-horizon coding agent benchmark: tasks such as reimplementing git in Zig run in a full Linux environment for up to 20 hours, with each model run five times per task.

robovqa.text: 829,502 video and text pairs with 29,520 unique instructions, collected bottom-up across three office buildings using both robot and human embodiments, for grounded high-level reasoning and question answering about long-horizon tasks.

llavabench.text: The small evaluation set released with LLaVA: images paired with conversation, detailed description and complex reasoning questions, where GPT-4 rates each answer for helpfulness, relevance, accuracy and detail against a text-only reference.

seedbenchimg.text: The image portion of SEED-Bench, a 19,000-question multiple-choice set spanning twelve image and video comprehension dimensions, built by an automated question pipeline with manual filtering so every item has human-annotated ground truth.

webvoyagesom.text: 643 tasks on 15 real websites where the agent acts from screenshots with interactive elements outlined and numbered in Set-of-Mark style, with trajectories judged by human annotators and by a multimodal auto-evaluator.

aideredit.text: The code editing benchmark of the aider CLI tool: 133 Python exercises from Exercism, where the model must edit the stub implementation file through aider's edit format until the exercise's own unit tests pass.

minif2fvalid.text: The 244-problem validation split of miniF2F, olympiad and course-level mathematics statements (AMC, AIME, IMO, high school and undergraduate) formalized in Lean, Metamath and Isabelle for neural theorem proving.

zerobenchmainwtools.text: The 100 hand-crafted main questions of ZeroBench, multi-step visual reasoning problems over natural and synthetic images that demand an exact answer, curated by adversarial filtering to be unsolvable by frontier models at release.

asimovmultimodal.text: Images of everyday scenes, some edited by an image generator to introduce hazards, each paired with candidate robot instructions that a model must judge desirable or undesirable; one dataset of Google DeepMind's ASIMOV semantic safety benchmark.

cb.text: The CommitmentBank, a SuperGLUE task: short texts containing an embedded clause, annotated for how far the speaker appears committed to that clause, framed as three-class textual entailment over Wall Street Journal, BNC fiction and Switchboard passages.

countbenchqa.text: A question-answering version of CountBench built for vision language models: web images paired with a question asking how many instances of an object appear, scored by exact match.

hiddenmath.text: A non-public Google eval of 179 math problems written from scratch so that they appear nowhere on the web, used to measure math reasoning without training-set contamination.

liveqa.text: Consumer health questions sent to the US National Library of Medicine and curated for the TREC 2017 medical task, each with a long reference answer written by a librarian; one of the long-form sets in Google's MultiMedQA.

mrcr28needle.text: A harder version of Google's multi-round co-reference resolution test: a long synthetic user and assistant conversation hides eight near-identical requests that differ by topic and writing style, and the model must reproduce one named instance.

nlvr2.text: 107,292 English sentences each paired with two web photographs, where the model decides whether the sentence is true of the pair; crowdsourced with a compare-and-contrast task to elicit compositional visual reasoning.

remi.text: Reasoning questions that each require several images at once, spanning math, physics, logic, code, charts and tables, and spatial and temporal reasoning.

squad2.text: Reading comprehension over Wikipedia paragraphs that adds more than 50,000 unanswerable questions written adversarially to look answerable, so a system must abstain when the paragraph supports no answer.

vatexzh.text: Chinese video captioning on VATEX, a dataset of more than 41,000 clips with captions in both English and Chinese; the model describes each video in Chinese.

xorqainxx.text: The cross-lingual QA task of IndicGenBench: a question in one of 28 Indic languages together with an English Wikipedia passage, where the answer must be generated in the language of the question.

bsds500.text: 500 natural images, each segmented by about five different people, split into train, validation and test, used to score contour detection and segmentation by boundary precision and recall plus region-based measures.

dream1k.text: 1,000 video clips split evenly across live-action movies, animation, stock footage, YouTube videos and short-form videos, each with a detailed human description of every event; generated descriptions are graded by an automatic event-matching method.

inaturalist18.text: Fine-grained species classification over 8,142 plant and animal species with 437,513 training photographs taken by citizen scientists, with a heavy class imbalance and many visually similar species.

parisretrieval.text: Landmark image retrieval over photographs of Paris in the revisited annotation, which re-created the ground truth for reliability, added harder queries, defined three protocols of increasing difficulty and supplies a million distractor images.

sacogold.text: The gold split of Meta's Segment Anything with Concepts benchmark: images from seven domains in which every noun-phrase prompt is annotated by three different people, so prompt ambiguity and human agreement can be measured for concept segmentation.

uvodense.text: The densely annotated split of Unidentified Video Objects: 1,200 three-second Kinetics clips in which every object is exhaustively masked at 30 fps with no predefined taxonomy, for open-world video segmentation.

llamaqa.text: 300 open-domain world-knowledge questions generated with LLaMA and checked by hand, then synthesized into speech, so a spoken language model answers from audio; replies are transcribed by ASR and searched for the reference answer.

polymathen.text: The English split of PolyMath, a multilingual math reasoning benchmark covering 18 languages and four difficulty levels from easy to competition-grade problems.

apenglishlanguageandcomposition.text: The College Board Advanced Placement exam in English Language and Composition, run under simulated exam conditions: a multiple-choice section plus free-response essays, which were graded by qualified human contractors against the exam rubric.

certifiedsommelier.text: The theory-knowledge paper of the Certified Sommelier examination, the middle of three sommelier certification levels, given as a multiple-choice test under simulated exam conditions and graded by the exam's own rubric.

destructiveactionavoidance.text: Coding-agent situations where an ordinary instruction such as clean the folder or reset the branch can mask a data-losing command like rm -rf or git reset --hard; it measures whether the model preserves the user's own edits.
