fullduplexbench3.text: Recordings of real human speech annotated for five categories of disfluency, paired with scenarios that need chained API calls across four task domains, to test full-duplex voice agents on accuracy, latency and turn-taking.

instructionhierarchyevaluations.text: Conflict cases in which a lower-priority input, a user message or third-party tool output, tries to override a higher-priority system instruction, checking that the model keeps to the privileged instruction.

leetcodemedium.text: Eighty medium-difficulty problems from the LeetCode practice site, the middle of the three LeetCode difficulty tiers OpenAI ran as coding exams under simulated exam conditions.

swelancericswe.text: The individual-contributor half of SWE-Lancer: real freelance jobs from Upwork, from 15-minute bug fixes to multi-week features, where the model's patch is graded by end-to-end browser tests written and triple-verified by professional engineers.

bfcl4.text: Measures how accurately a model calls functions, with calls checked against an abstract syntax tree rather than string matching; the fourth version widens the leaderboard from single-turn and multi-turn calls to holistic agentic evaluation.

commonvoice.text: A crowdsourced multilingual corpus of read speech with volunteer-validated transcripts, collected by Mozilla across dozens of languages and tens of thousands of speakers, intended mainly for speech recognition.

geditcn.text: The Chinese half of GEdit-Bench: 606 image editing instructions collected from real user posts and sorted into 11 editing types, each with its source image, scored by a multimodal judge on instruction compliance and picture quality.

imagereward.text: A reward model for text-to-image generation trained on 137,000 expert comparisons, used as an automatic stand-in for human preference over how well an image matches its prompt and how good it looks.

longtextbenchzh.text: Prompts that ask an image generator to render long passages of text accurately inside the picture, 160 of them across eight scenarios, reported separately for Chinese and English.

mldr.text: A multilingual retrieval test set built from long Wikipedia, Wudao and mC4 articles, where a query must be matched against whole documents rather than short passages; scored by nDCG@10.

mtggenre.text: Genre tagging on MTG-Jamendo, a music auto-tagging dataset of more than 55,000 full audio tracks released on Jamendo under Creative Commons licences and tagged by their uploaders; a multi-label task over the genre tag set.

opencpoptest.text: The held-out test split of the Opencpop Mandarin singing corpus: 206 utterances from five of its 100 studio-recorded pop songs, with lyrics, musical scores and phoneme and note boundaries, for singing voice synthesis.

rgb.text: A retrieval-augmented generation corpus in English and Chinese divided into four testbeds, each probing one ability: noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration and counterfactual robustness.

sfiction.text: A true-or-false task in L-Eval built from science fiction texts, where most correct answers contradict real-world physical laws, so the model must follow the long input context rather than its pretrained knowledge.

videomme2.text: Video understanding questions arranged in three levels of rising difficulty, from aggregating visual details to temporal dynamics to multimodal reasoning, graded in groups of related questions so guessed or fragmented answers earn no credit.

wildclawbenchmm.text: Sixty human-authored bilingual tasks run inside real CLI agent harnesses in Docker with genuine tools instead of mocks; the multimodal ones require perceiving images, video, audio or rendered PDFs, and grading mixes rule checks, environment audits and a model judge.

swemarathon11.text: Twenty ultra-long-horizon software engineering tasks, each with its own executable environment, a human-written reference solution and a multi-layer verification suite with hidden tests and adversarial checks against shortcut solutions.

frontiersweimplrank.text: The implementation category of FrontierSWE, an ultra-long-horizon coding agent benchmark whose tasks ask an agent to build substantial systems from scratch, such as git in Zig or a SPICE circuit simulator in Rust, with a 20-hour budget per run.

seeden.text: The English half of the Seed-TTS objective test set: 1,000 out-of-domain samples drawn from Common Voice used as reference clips for zero-shot speech generation, scored by ASR word error rate and speaker similarity.

longbenchcite.text: An automated benchmark for long-context question answering with citations, checking whether an answer carries sentence-level citations that point at the right spans of the supplied long document.

swebenchverifiedmini.text: A 50-instance subset of SWE-bench Verified picked to keep roughly the same difficulty and test pass-rate distribution as the full 500 problems, while needing about 5GB instead of 130GB of container storage.

wenetspeechmeeting.text: The meeting test split of WenetSpeech: 15 hours of far-field, spontaneous Mandarin conversation sampled from 197 real meetings on topics from education to finance, used as a deliberately mismatched speech recognition test.

matharena.text: An evaluation platform that runs models on math competitions right after they take place, so the problems postdate training cutoffs; it covers final-answer contests such as AIME and HMMT and proof-based olympiads such as USAMO and IMO.

factsparametric.text: Trivia-style factual questions answerable from Wikipedia, posed with no search or other tools so the answer must come from the model's weights; 1,052 public and 1,052 private questions.

mjhq30k.text: A text-to-image evaluation set of 30,000 high-aesthetic Midjourney images spread evenly over 10 categories such as animals, food, logo and people; models generate from the paired prompts and outputs are compared with the references by FID.

1hvideoqa.text: 125 five-way multiple-choice questions over public videos 40 to 105 minutes long, annotated so that answering depends on events lasting only a few seconds, which makes sparse frame sampling insufficient.

cbisddsm.text: A curated subset of the Digital Database for Screening Mammography: 2,620 scanned film mammography studies in which masses and calcifications are marked with regions of interest and labelled benign or malignant against verified pathology.

countbenchvqa.text: A question-answering version of CountBench: 540 web images, 60 for each count from two to ten, each paired with a hand-written question of the form "How many X are there in the image?" and graded by exact match.

fevbench.text: A time series forecasting benchmark of 100 tasks drawn from 96 datasets across seven application domains, 46 of them with covariates; models are aggregated by win rates and skill scores with bootstrapped confidence intervals.

hiddenmathhard.text: Competition-level math problems in the mould of AIME and AMC, written by experts and deliberately kept off the public web so they cannot leak into training data; part of Google's internal HiddenMath evaluation.

cococap.text: Over 1.5 million human-written captions covering more than 330,000 COCO images, five independent captions per image; generated captions go to an evaluation server and are scored with BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE and CIDEr.

objaversemultiview.text: Open-vocabulary object naming over 3D renders: 44,000 Objaverse models in roughly 1,100 categories, eight rendered views each with four prompts per view, the per-view answers aggregated and scored by sentence-embedding similarity to the label.

robospatialpointing.text: The point-prediction part of RoboSpatial: given an indoor or tabletop image and a request such as where a plate could be put, the model must return image coordinates of free space or a support surface that would take the object.

strategyqa.text: 2,780 crowdsourced yes/no questions whose reasoning steps are implicit and must be inferred rather than read off the question; each item also carries a decomposition and the supporting Wikipedia paragraphs.

vbenchi2v.text: The image-to-video track of VBench: a suite of input images at several aspect ratios paired with prompts, with generated video rated on dimensions such as subject and background consistency with the input image, camera motion and video quality.

xorretrieve.text: A cross-lingual retrieval task built from XOR-TyDi QA: given an information-seeking question written in one of seven non-English languages, a system must retrieve English passages containing the answer.

burst.text: Thousands of videos with high-quality object masks that unify six object tracking and segmentation tasks, including video object segmentation and multi-object tracking and segmentation, on shared data and comparable metrics.

dtd.text: 5,640 texture photographs collected in the wild, 120 for each of 47 human-describable attribute words such as striped, veined or polka-dotted; the task is to name the attribute, over ten fixed train, validation and test splits.

inaturalist21.text: Fine-grained species classification over 10,000 plant and animal species photographed by iNaturalist users, with about 2.7 million training and 500,000 test images; each image must be assigned one species, scored by top-1 error.

mose.text: 2,149 video clips of crowded, heavily occluded scenes with 431,725 masks over 5,200 objects in 36 categories, for video object segmentation where targets are often hidden or disappear from the frame entirely.

pascalconcept59.text: Semantic segmentation over the 59 most frequent object and stuff classes of PASCAL-Context, which adds whole-scene pixel labels to PASCAL VOC 2010 images and is a standard open-vocabulary segmentation test set.

sacosilver.text: The single-annotation image split of Meta's SA-Co benchmark for promptable concept segmentation, spanning ten domains: given a short noun phrase, a model must segment every instance of that concept in the image.

videohallucer.text: A video hallucination benchmark that pairs every basic question with an adversarial hallucinated counterpart in binary video QA, covering object-relation, temporal and semantic-detail errors plus extrinsic factual and non-factual ones.

beyondaime.text: 100 competition math problems at or above the difficulty of AIME questions 11 to 15, each manually rewritten so it does not appear verbatim in pretraining corpora, and each with a single integer answer for automatic grading.

llavaguard.text: An open framework and image dataset for vision safety assessment: pictures are annotated by human experts with a safety rating, a violated category from a customizable taxonomy and a written rationale, which the model must reproduce under a given policy.

spgispeech.text: 5,000 hours of English earnings-call audio with professional transcripts that keep capitalization, punctuation and non-standard word formatting, so recognition is scored against fully formatted text rather than normalized text.

apenglishliteratureandcomposition.text: The College Board's three-hour Advanced Placement exam in literary analysis: 55 multiple-choice questions on at least two prose fiction and two poetry passages, plus three timed essays on a poem, a prose passage and a self-chosen work.

gaia.text: 466 questions for general AI assistants that people find straightforward but that need web browsing, file and multimodal handling and multi-step tool use, each with a short unambiguous answer; 300 are kept for a public leaderboard.

lifescibench.text: 750 free-response life science research tasks written by 173 practising scientists, spanning seven research workflows from evidence handling to scientific communication, each graded against an expert-written rubric of specific claims and decisions.

monorepobench.text: An internal OpenAI coding eval: an agent is placed in a large repository checked out to a pre-change branch, told what change is required, edits files with shell and Python, and the result is graded by hidden human-written unit tests.

productionjailbreaks.text: A set of jailbreak prompts identified in production ChatGPT data, used to test whether adversarial framings can push a model into producing content its policy disallows; outputs are autograded for whether they were unsafe.

swelancericswediamond.text: The public Diamond split of SWE-Lancer's individual-contributor tasks: 237 real paid Upwork bug fixes and feature requests where a model patches the repository, each graded by Playwright end-to-end tests triple-checked by engineers.

bird.text: Over 12,751 text-to-SQL question and query pairs over 95 large, messy real-world databases across 37 professional domains; answers often need external knowledge beyond the schema, and query efficiency is measured alongside correctness.

contextasrbench.text: Up to 40,000 speech samples carrying more than 300,000 named entities across over ten domains, each supplied with a list of context entities, testing whether a recognizer can use that context and world knowledge to transcribe rare names.

diode.text: Roughly 27,000 high-resolution photographs of indoor and outdoor scenes captured with one sensor suite, each with dense long-range depth and surface normal maps, for benchmarking monocular depth and normal estimation.

gediten.text: The English-instruction half of GEdit-Bench: 606 de-identified real user image-editing requests gathered from the web and sorted into 11 edit types, with outputs rated by a vision-language judge on semantic consistency and perceptual quality.

imgedit.text: An instruction-based image editing benchmark with basic, hard single-turn and multi-turn suites, rating edits on instruction adherence, editing quality and preservation of untouched detail; it accompanies a 1.2 million pair editing dataset.

mlogiqa.text: The logical reasoning task of P-MMEval: multiple-choice deductive items taken from LogiQA's English and Chinese sets and translated into eight further languages, 80 per language, to test how reasoning transfers across languages.

mtginstrument.text: The instrument-tagging subset of MTG-Jamendo: 25,135 Creative Commons music tracks annotated with any of 41 instrument tags, evaluated as multi-label audio auto-tagging.

rmb.text: A reward model benchmark covering more than 49 real-world scenarios, testing a reward model both on pairwise preference comparisons and on Best-of-N selection so that it tracks usefulness for alignment rather than ranking alone.

tedlium.text: English speech from TED talks with time-aligned transcripts, used to measure speech recognition error rates; release 3 supplies 452 hours of transcribed audio plus a separate partition built for speaker adaptation experiments.

hrm8k.text: 8,011 math problems presented in parallel Korean and English, built to separate whether a model's drop on non-English input comes from understanding the question or from the reasoning itself.

futureomni.text: 919 videos with 1,034 multiple-choice questions across eight domains asking what happens next from synchronized audio and video, so a model must reason about cause and timing instead of describing events already shown.

seedttstesten.text: The English half of the Seed-TTS evaluation set: 1,000 samples drawn from Common Voice where a system clones a reference voice to read new text, scored for word error rate with Whisper-large-v3 and speaker similarity with a WavLM verifier.

charxivvalreasoning.text: The reasoning questions of CharXiv's 1,000-chart validation split: charts taken unaltered from arXiv papers, with expert-written questions that require combining information across several visual elements rather than reading one value.

longbenchwrite.text: 120 writing prompts, 60 English and 60 Chinese, each stating an explicit word count ranging from under 500 to over 4,000 words; responses get a length score for hitting the requested length and a quality score from a model judge.

swerebench.text: Real GitHub issue-fixing tasks mined continuously by an automated pipeline from thousands of Python repositories, so the evaluated set stays newer than model training cutoffs; the leaderboard runs a filtered subset under one fixed agent scaffold.

xlcost.text: Parallel code snippets and whole programs aligned across seven programming languages plus English, supporting ten cross-lingual tasks such as program translation, code summarization, code synthesis and code search.

mbe.text: The multiple-choice component of the US bar exam: a six-hour, 200-question test (175 scored and 25 unscored pretest items) split over two three-hour sessions and developed by the National Conference of Bar Examiners.

fimo.text: 149 International Mathematical Olympiad shortlist problems formalised as Lean theorem statements, each paired with the informal problem text and a LaTeX informal proof, for automated theorem proving at olympiad level.

mjhqfid30k.text: FID measured against a curated set of 30,000 high-quality Midjourney images spread evenly over ten categories (animals, art, fashion, food, indoor, landscape, logo, people, plants, vehicles), as a proxy for aesthetic quality in text-to-image models.

activitynetcap.text: 20k videos totalling 849 hours annotated with 100k natural-language event descriptions, each carrying its own start and end time, for detecting and describing every event in a video.

attributionset.text: A Gemini factuality evaluation of prompts that require grounding an answer in supplied context, such as summarising a user's source or citing given snippets; human annotators check each response for attribution using the AIS metric.

charmoffensive.text: A persuasion study in which the model and a human participant role-play two old friends walking through town; the participant then rates the agent on being funny, interesting, a good listener, kind and trustworthy on a five-point Likert scale.

findinfo.text: One of three Hidden Agenda persuasion tasks: posing as an AI tutor, the model must talk a human study participant into supplying the email address of a given paper's author, checked by looking for that address in the transcript.

hrbench8k.text: 200 images averaging 8K resolution, split evenly between fine-grained single-instance perception (attribute recognition, OCR, visual prompting) and cross-instance perception (map and chart analysis, spatial relations).

lmarenatextarena.text: The text leaderboard of a crowdsourced arena where users send a prompt to two anonymous models side by side and vote for the better reply; the pairwise votes are fitted with a Bradley-Terry model, optionally with style control.

mscxrt.text: A chest X-ray benchmark for temporal reasoning with two tasks: classifying disease progression (improving, stable, worsening) across paired images for five findings, and judging sentence pairs as paraphrase or contradiction about progression.

omnidocbench15ocr.text: Version 1.5 of a document-parsing benchmark over annotated PDF pages spanning academic papers, financial reports, newspapers, textbooks and handwritten notes; the text OCR track scores recognised text against block-level annotations by normalised edit distance.

robospatialvqa.text: Spatial question answering for robotics built from indoor and tabletop RGB-D scenes: binary and point-prediction questions about free space, whether an object fits somewhere, and relative position, each asked from egocentric, world-centric and object-centric frames.

vindrmammo.text: 5,000 full-field digital mammography exams of four standard views each, double read with disagreements resolved by arbitration, labelled with BI-RADS and density at breast level plus the category, location and BI-RADS of non-benign findings.

xquad.text: 240 paragraphs and 1,190 question-answer pairs taken from the SQuAD v1.1 development set and translated into ten languages by professional translators, for cross-lingual extractive question answering.

caltech101.text: Photographs of objects in 101 categories, roughly 40 to 800 images per category and about 50 for most, each around 300 by 200 pixels and shipped with hand-clicked object outlines.

egohos.text: 11,243 egocentric images of everyday activities with per-pixel segmentation labels for hands and the objects being interacted with, the first dataset to label detailed hand-object contact boundaries.

infinitebench.text: A long-context suite whose examples average more than 100K tokens, mixing synthetic and realistic tasks in English and Chinese that are designed so retrieving a short span of the context is not enough to answer.

mose1.text: 2,149 video clips covering 5,200 objects in 36 categories with 431,725 segmentation masks, collected so that targets are crowded, frequently occluded, and disappear and reappear, for video object segmentation in complex scenes.

pascalvoc.text: A standard image dataset with annotations and evaluation procedures for visual object category recognition and detection, run as an annual challenge from 2005 to 2012 and fixed at 20 object classes from 2007 onward.

sacoveval.text: The video split of SAM 3's SA-Co benchmark, covering three domains with one annotator per video and noun-phrase pair; a model must segment and track every instance matching a short noun phrase, scored by cgF1 and pHOTA.

visor.text: Pixel annotations over EPIC-KITCHENS egocentric video for segmenting hands and active objects: 272K manual semantic masks across 257 object classes plus 67K hand-object relations, covering 36 hours of untrimmed video.

callhome.text: Unscripted telephone conversations between family members and close friends, recorded at 8 kHz in calls of up to 30 minutes and released with transcripts, used for speech recognition and speaker and language identification research.

lmsysarena.text: An open platform where crowdsourced users put their own prompts to two anonymous models and vote for the better answer, with the pairwise votes turned into model rankings by statistical rating methods.

swebenchlite.text: A 300-instance subset of SWE-bench restricted to self-contained bug fixes: issues that edit a single file, whose gold patch has at most three hunks, and that carry no images, links or cross-references to other issues.

kimiclaw247bench.text: Moonshot's in-house test of long-horizon agentic work in persistent, multi-day coworking tasks: 17 professional scenarios and 610 evaluation points across software engineering, ML research, recruiting, trading and marketing, run through the OpenClaw harness.

researchrubrics.text: Realistic deep-research prompts from nine domains paired with more than 2,500 expert-written, fine-grained rubrics scoring factual grounding, reasoning soundness and clarity, with tasks categorised by conceptual breadth, logical nesting and exploration.

apenvironmentalscience.text: A US Advanced Placement exam combining multiple-choice and free-response questions over the course's environmental science units, including the ability to design research studies that solve environmental problems.

challengingredteamingevaluation1.text: An OpenAI adversarial set built from red teaming o3-mini, covering jailbreak attempts for illicit advice, extremism and hate crimes, political persuasion and self harm, scored on whether the response was unsafe.

dnasequencedesignfortranscriptionfactorb.text: An OpenAI preparedness test of DNA design: 50 prompts for each of 11 transcription factors drawn from Nucleobench ask the model to edit a random 3,000-base-pair sequence for higher binding affinity, scored by BPNet-family oracles against a gradient-based baseline.

genebench.text: 103 multi-stage data-analysis problems across ten domains of genomics and quantitative biology, each supplying staged data and a minimally guided prompt with obstacles such as measurement error, confounding and QC failures, and a single verifiable answer.

livebenchcoding.text: The coding category of LiveBench, made of two tasks: writing a correct solution to competition programming statements drawn from LiveCodeBench, and finishing a partially correct solution assembled from GitHub sources.

multimodalrefusalevaluation.text: An OpenAI safety set of combined text-and-image prompts covering disallowed content such as sexual or exploitative material and self-harm, scored both on whether the reply was unsafe and on whether benign requests were over-refused.

professionalcapturetheflagchallenges.text: The professional tier of OpenAI's cybersecurity evaluation: public capture-the-flag tasks in web exploitation, reverse engineering, binary exploitation and cryptography that require chaining two or more exploitation steps, attempted from a headless Kali Linux shell.

aaomniscienceindex.text: A bounded index over 6,000 questions drawn from authoritative academic and industry sources across 42 economically relevant topics in six domains, rewarding correct factual recall, penalising hallucination and leaving abstention unpenalised.

countqa.text: Over 1,500 question-answer pairs on real-world photographs chosen for high object density, clutter and occlusion, testing whether multimodal models can count objects in cluttered everyday scenes.

domino.text: A dynamic-manipulation dataset and benchmark for vision-language-action models: 35 tasks of hierarchical complexity involving moving targets, backed by more than 110K expert trajectories and a multi-dimensional evaluation suite.

fleurs20.text: A 20-language subset of the FLEURS multilingual read-speech corpus as defined in the Qwen3-ASR report: twelve core languages plus Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Dutch, Polish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese, scored by word error rate.

giantstepstempo.text: Tempo annotations for electronic dance music excerpts, derived from user corrections to Beatport metadata and published with download scripts, used to score automatic tempo estimation.

indommlu.text: 14,981 multiple-choice questions written by professional teachers, spanning 64 tasks from Indonesian primary school through university entrance exams, with roughly half aimed at the Indonesian language and nine local languages and cultures.

lveval.text: A bilingual long-context benchmark at five length levels up to 256k words, with single-hop and multi-hop QA over 11 datasets, hardened by inserting confusing facts and replacing keywords, and scored by keyword recall.

mlvu.text: Long video understanding across genres including movies, surveillance footage, egocentric video, cartoons and game recordings, with video lengths spanning a wide range and several task types per video.

mtgmoodtheme.text: The mood and theme tag subset of the MTG-Jamendo auto-tagging dataset: full-length Creative Commons tracks from Jamendo labelled with uploader-supplied mood and theme tags, scored as multi-label classification.

osworld2.text: 108 long-horizon computer-use workflows in real desktop environments, grounded in authentic input artifacts and stateful user profiles, targeting streaming interaction, dynamic environments, cross-source reasoning and implicit-state inference.

robocasa365.text: 365 everyday household tasks across 2,500 simulated kitchen environments built on the RoboCasa platform, split into 65 atomic skills and 300 composite multi-skill tasks, with large human and synthetic demonstration sets.

sifomultiturn.text: Sequential instruction following in which each instruction depends on the outcome of the previous one, so grading needs only the final step; the tasks cover text modification, question answering, mathematics and security rules.

videommewosub.text: The subtitle-free setting of Video-MME: 2,700 manually written multiple-choice questions over 900 videos running from 11 seconds to an hour across six visual domains, answered from the video frames alone.

wildspeech.text: Real-world chat prompts rendered as speech with varied speaker attributes, acoustic conditions and speech-specific phenomena such as prosody, homophones and stuttering, graded by query-aware checklists for end-to-end speech models.

mtebretrieval.text: The retrieval task group of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, reusing BEIR's datasets: the model embeds every query and corpus document, documents are ranked by cosine similarity, and nDCG@10 is the headline metric.

tauvoice.text: 278 grounded tasks extending the text-based tau-2-bench into full-duplex voice: agents hold multi-turn conversations, follow domain policies and call tools while a simulated user supplies varied accents, realistic audio and turn-taking dynamics.

gsminfinite.text: Grade-school math problems generated from computational graphs, so that reasoning complexity and context length can both be dialled up without bound by adding unnecessary nodes and edges as noise.

seedttstestzh.text: The Mandarin half of the Seed-TTS objective evaluation set: 2,000 out-of-domain utterances from DiDiSpeech-2 for zero-shot speech generation, scored by Paraformer word error rate and WavLM speaker similarity against a reference clip.

mathvltest.text: The 2,000-problem evaluation split curated alongside the MathVL fine-tuning dataset for MathGLM-Vision, covering multimodal mathematics beyond the geometry focus of earlier specialised datasets.

sysbench.text: System-message following measured on 500 hand-written system messages paired with multi-turn user conversations, probing constraint violation, instruction misjudgement and multi-turn instability across six common constraint types.

zaicodebench.text: A private in-house test of coding agents placed in complex local development environments across diverse task categories, scored on both end-to-end task completion and fine-grained checklist accuracy at several effort levels.

medcalcbenchverified.text: A re-verified release of MedCalc-Bench: 1,100 test cases pairing a patient note with a clinical calculator question, each carrying a corrected ground-truth value and step-by-step solution, across 55 rule-based and equation-based calculators.

asdiv.text: 2,305 English elementary-school math word problems, each labelled with its problem type and grade level, assembled to cover a wider range of text patterns than earlier word-problem corpora.

formalmath.text: 5,560 formally verified Lean4 theorem statements from high school olympiad to undergraduate level, autoformalized by LLMs and then filtered by semantic verification, negation-based disproof and manual expert review.

babelcode.text: An execution-based framework that ports code-generation datasets such as HumanEval, MBPP, P3 and Transcoder into other programming languages, generating language-specific test harnesses and running each prediction in a Docker sandbox.

chembench.text: More than 2,700 curated chemistry question-answer pairs across analytical, organic, inorganic, physical, materials and technical chemistry plus toxicity and safety, some requiring reasoning over SMILES structures, with refusals counted separately.

crc100k.text: 100,000 colour-normalised 224x224 patches from H and E stained colorectal cancer slides, each labelled with one of nine tissue types including tumour epithelium, stroma, lymphocytes and adipose, for tissue classification.

fintabnet.text: More than 110,000 tables pulled from the annual reports of S&P 500 companies, annotated with cell-level bounding boxes and row and column spans, for table detection and structure recognition on financial pages.

hsk79.text: The advanced band of the Chinese Proficiency Test for non-native speakers: 98 questions over listening, reading, writing, translation and speaking, drawn from news, academic writing, debates and business negotiation.

mseb.text: An open framework for sound embeddings covering eight capabilities (retrieval, reasoning, classification, transcription, segmentation, clustering, reranking and reconstruction) over datasets of spoken queries, environmental sounds and birdsong.

superglue.text: A harder successor to GLUE: language-understanding tasks spanning yes/no question answering, textual entailment, multi-sentence reading comprehension, word-sense disambiguation and Winograd-style coreference, plus diagnostic sets.

xquadindic.text: The Indic extension of XQuAD built for IndicGenBench: SQuAD-style extractive question answering in which passage, question and answer are all in the same Indic language, translated by professional native speakers.

casualconversations.text: Over 45,000 videos of 3,011 paid subjects who self-reported age and gender, with skin tone rated by trained annotators on the Fitzpatrick scale and low ambient lighting flagged, for measuring fairness across groups.

epickitchens100.text: 100 hours of unscripted head-mounted-camera footage of everyday kitchen activity in 45 homes, densely labelled with about 90,000 action segments, supporting action recognition, detection, anticipation and cross-modal retrieval.

infinitebenchenmc.text: The multiple-choice subtask of InfiniteBench: 229 questions about a novel-length fake book whose entities have been substituted, with roughly 180K tokens of context so the answer cannot be recalled from pretraining.

mose2.text: 5,024 videos annotated with 701,976 masks over 10,074 objects in 200 categories, featuring frequent disappearance and reappearance, heavy occlusion, adverse weather, low light, camouflage and reflections, for video object segmentation.

pascalvoc12.text: 11,540 natural images annotated with 27,450 objects across 20 everyday categories, carrying per-object bounding boxes with pose, truncation and difficulty flags, used for image classification and object detection.

sacovideo.text: The video half of the SA-Co benchmark for promptable concept segmentation: given a short noun phrase, a model must detect, segment and track every matching instance across a video, scored by a classification-gated F1 and a tracking metric.

vost.text: More than 700 densely mask-annotated videos, 21 seconds long on average, of objects being cut, broken or otherwise transformed, so a segmentation model must keep tracking an instance whose colour, shape and texture change.

canitedit.text: 105 hand-written Python editing problems, each pairing a before and after program with two natural-language instructions, one detailed and one terse, and graded by a hidden test suite.

gpqamain.text: The 448-question primary split of GPQA: graduate-level multiple-choice questions in biology, physics and chemistry written to be Google-proof, kept when expert and non-expert validation showed them to be objective and hard.

lmsysvisionleaderboard.text: Crowdsourced pairwise voting on vision-language models: a user submits an image with a prompt, two anonymous models answer, and the preferred reply is voted on, with the votes fitted to a Bradley-Terry rating.

switchboard.text: About 260 hours of two-sided English telephone conversation, roughly 2,400 topic-prompted calls among 543 US speakers recorded at 8 kHz and transcribed, long used as a conversational speech recognition test set.

ruler1m.text: The one-million-token setting of RULER, a synthetic long-context suite that extends needle-in-a-haystack with varied types and quantities of needles plus multi-hop tracing and aggregation tasks at a configurable sequence length.

apiinstructionfollowing.text: An internal OpenAI evaluation in which a model must obey difficult instructions drawn from real developer feedback on the API.

dsbench.text: 466 data analysis tasks and 74 data modeling tasks taken from Eloquence and Kaggle competitions, posed with their original long, multimodal descriptions and large multi-table data files.

genebenchpro.text: 129 synthetic computational-biology problems across ten domains from statistical genetics to cancer genomics: an agent gets a deliberately messy dataset, brief experimental context and a target estimand, then must choose an analysis and report a number.

internalcircumventionbenchmark.text: An internal OpenAI evaluation of how a model responds to Codex auto-review denials on knowledge-work tasks, where exploiting a poor reviewer configuration to bypass the denial counts as a failure.

longfactconcepts.text: 1,140 open-ended prompts, one half of LongFact, asking for a long-form explanation of a general concept across 38 topics; replies are split into atomic facts and checked against search by the SAFE evaluator.

multimodaltroubleshootingvirology.text: 350 single-select multiple-choice questions from SecureBio that pair text with images and ask how to diagnose and fix problems in virology wet-lab protocols.

professionalctfs.text: Capture-the-flag challenges at the professional competition tier, spanning web and binary exploitation, reverse engineering and cryptography: the model works from a Kali Linux container to exploit a vulnerability and recover a hidden flag.

aegis20.text: 34,248 human-LLM interactions annotated for content safety against a taxonomy of 12 top-level hazard categories plus 9 fine-grained subcategories, labelled by a hybrid of human annotators and a multi-LLM jury.

blend.text: 52.6k hand-written question-answer pairs on everyday cultural knowledge such as food, music, sports, customs and daily habits, from 16 countries and regions in 13 languages, asked in both short-answer and multiple-choice form.

coursera.text: A subtask of the L-Eval long-context suite: 172 multiple-choice questions over the merged subtitles of online course video lectures, and the first such set in which a question can have more than one correct option.

grit.text: Seven vision tasks (object categorization and localization, referring expression grounding, visual question answering, segmentation, keypoint detection and surface normal estimation) posed over one evaluation set built to probe robustness to image perturbations and distribution shift.

instructttseval.text: Three tasks of rising abstraction for instruction-following speech synthesis, acoustic-parameter specification, descriptive style directive and role-play, with 1,000 English and 1,000 Chinese cases each, paired with reference audio and judged by a model.

lvomnibench.text: 275 videos of 10 to 90 minutes with 1,014 four-option questions answered from video and audio together, covering speech, sound effects and music, across perception, understanding, inference and multi-step logical reasoning.

mlvumavg.text: The multiple-choice average of MLVU, covering topic reasoning, anomaly recognition, needle QA, egocentric reasoning, plot QA, action order and action count over videos running from 3 minutes to over 2 hours.

mtgtop50.text: The 50 most frequent tags of the MTG-Jamendo music collection: multi-label auto-tagging of roughly 54,000 full Creative Commons tracks with genre, instrument and mood or theme labels.

ovon.text: Open-vocabulary object-goal navigation in 181 photorealistic home scans: an agent with RGB-D and odometry must find any instance of a category named in free-form text, over more than 15,000 annotated objects in 379 categories.

robocasagr1.text: 24 simulated tabletop tasks for the GR-1 humanoid in the RoboCasa framework: language-conditioned pick-and-place between containers, plus articulated tasks such as opening a drawer or microwave, putting an object inside and closing it.

videommewsub.text: The subtitle-assisted setting of Video-MME: 2,700 expert-written multiple-choice questions over 900 videos running from 11 seconds to an hour, where the model receives subtitle text aligned to its sampled frames alongside the frames.

wildspeechbench.text: Real-world chat queries rendered as speech across varied speaker attributes and acoustic conditions and augmented with prosody, homophones and stuttering, then graded by an automatic judge against a checklist written per query.

jaqket2.text: Japanese open-domain quiz questions taken from competition quizzes, where version 2 drops version 1's answer candidates and requires the model to produce the answer string, usually a Wikipedia entity, from the question text alone.

musr.text: 756 free-text narratives generated by a neurosymbolic pipeline in three domains, murder mysteries, object placements and team allocation, each running several hundred to a thousand words and requiring facts to be extracted then chained with commonsense.

tauvoiceleaderboard.text: 278 customer-service tasks carried over from tau-bench, run over live full-duplex audio with a simulated caller, varied synthesised personas, background noise and telephony artifacts, and scored against the final database state.

gsminfinitehard.text: The hard split of GSM-Infinite: synthetic grade-school arithmetic problems built from computational graphs, carrying up to three-entity implicit relationships and semantically related filler that scales context from zero to 32K-plus tokens.

seedzh.text: The Mandarin test set of the Seed-TTS evaluation suite: 2,000 zero-shot synthesis items from DiDiSpeech-2 where a model reads target text in the voice of a short reference clip, scored by ASR error rate and speaker similarity.

mmbenchcntest.text: The Chinese test split of MMBench: 1,784 single-choice vision-language questions covering 20 ability dimensions, graded with CircularEval, which re-asks each question with the options rotated and requires every pass to be right.

tallyqa.text: Open-ended object-counting questions over images, split into simple ones answerable by detection alone and complex ones needing attributes, relationships or reasoning, such as counting only the dogs that are eating.

zaicodebench10.text: An in-house Z.ai benchmark that places coding agents in complex local development environments on realistic user tasks, scored both on end-to-end task completion and on fine-grained checklist accuracy.

cursorbench.text: Cursor's internal coding-agent suite, drawn from real Cursor sessions by tracing committed code back to the agent request that produced it, and graded by agentic graders on correctness, code quality, efficiency and interaction behaviour.

metrdatadeduplication.text: An agentic task from METR's public suite: write an efficient program, such as a fuzzy hashing scheme, that removes near-duplicate lines from a large text dataset, judged on both deduplication quality and algorithmic efficiency.

fox.text: Nine fine-grained sub-tasks over English and Chinese document pages, covering page, region, line and colour-guided OCR, region translation and summary, in-document figure captions, and cross-page question answering.

mmc.text: The Chinese-language half of MMBench, reported on its dev split: multiple-choice vision-language questions covering comprehensive image understanding, evaluated alongside MMBench's English half.

adversarialgeneral.text: 58 long-form consumer health questions written to elicit harmful or biased answers, spanning health equity, drug and alcohol use, mental health, COVID-19, obesity, suicide and medical misinformation, rated by physicians.

chembenchmini.text: A 236-question subset of ChemBench, sampled to keep topics and required skills balanced across analytical, organic, physical, inorganic, technical and safety chemistry, mixing multiple-choice and open-ended items.

floresindic.text: The machine translation task of IndicGenBench: 2,009 FLORES-200 sentences professionally translated into 29 Indic languages, scored in both the English-to-Indic and Indic-to-English directions with character F1.

huggingfaceh6.text: An independently run average over six Open LLM Leaderboard tasks (ARC-c, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, Winogrande and GSM8K), used as a prompt-independent cross-check on small-model results.

lofthardretrieval.text: The hard retrieval subset of LOFT: 300 multi-hop, multi-needle queries answered from a single long context, reported at both 128k and 1M token context lengths.

msrvtt.text: 10,000 web video clips totalling 41.2 hours, gathered from 257 video-search queries, each paired with about 20 crowd-written sentences for video-to-text description and retrieval.

pacolvis.text: The LVIS-based image half of PACO: 75 object categories, 456 object-part categories and 55 attributes, with 641K part masks over 260K object boxes for part segmentation and attribute prediction.

rsvqahr.text: The high-resolution half of RSVQA: 10,659 tiles of 15cm USGS aerial imagery over the north-eastern United States, with 1,066,316 questions built from OpenStreetMap about presence, counts, comparisons and area.

visualprobe.text: A visual search set of 500 test question-answer pairs (plus 4,000 for training) over high-resolution images with small targets and many distractors, split into easy, medium and hard so that answers usually need repeated zooming.

xsum.text: Extreme summarisation of BBC news articles: produce one sentence answering what the article is about, a framing chosen so that extractive strategies do not suffice.

causalvqa.text: Video question answering about real-world physical events, with counterfactual, hypothetical, anticipation, planning and descriptive questions, filtered so that language-prior shortcuts do not work.

eventhallusion.text: Video question answering built to expose hallucinated events, testing whether a model reports things suggested by language priors or by vision-language misalignment but absent from the video.

infinitebenchenqa.text: The free-form English question-answering task of InfiniteBench: 351 hand-written questions over whole novels averaging 192.6K tokens, whose answers require aggregating or filtering facts spread across the book.

moviegenaudiobench.text: 527 generated single-shot videos spanning an ontology of 36 audio categories and 434 sound concepts, each with human-reviewed sound and music captions, released for video-to-audio and text-to-audio generation.

pets.text: The Oxford-IIIT Pet dataset used for fine-grained classification: 37 cat and dog breeds with roughly 200 images each, also annotated with head bounding boxes and trimap segmentations.

samaudiobench.text: An in-the-wild audio separation benchmark covering speech cleaning, speaker separation, music, instrument stems and general sound, where each 10 second clip carries human-annotated text, visual masklet and temporal span prompts.

woodscape.text: A fisheye automotive dataset from four surround-view cameras: over 10,000 images annotated at instance level across 40 classes and more than 100,000 with other labels, supporting nine tasks including segmentation, depth and soiling detection.

chime4.text: Wall Street Journal sentences read by talkers in noisy real-world environments and captured on a six-microphone tablet array, with separate 6-channel, 2-channel and 1-channel recognition tracks.

talkbank.text: Open repositories of transcribed spoken communication contributed by hundreds of researchers in over 42 languages, stored in the standard CHAT transcript format so conversations can be searched and analysed automatically.

apmacroeconomics.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement exam in macroeconomics: 60 multiple-choice questions in 70 minutes plus three free-response questions in 60 minutes requiring explanations, calculations and graphs.

challengingrefusalevaluation.text: A harder companion to OpenAI's standard refusal evaluation: an internally built set of challenge prompts for disallowed content and overrefusal, used to keep measuring safety progress once the standard set saturates.

longfactobjects.text: 1,140 GPT-4-generated prompts, 30 for each of 38 topics, asking for long-form answers about specific objects such as people, places and companies, graded by splitting the response into individual facts and checking each against search.

tacitknowledgeandtroubleshooting.text: A multiple-choice set built with Gryphon Scientific spanning all five stages of the biothreat creation process, with questions obscure to anyone outside the field or without hands-on experience running the protocols.

ccocr.text: Four OCR-centred tracks (multi-scene text reading, multilingual text reading, document parsing and key information extraction) over 39 subsets and 7,058 fully annotated images, about 41 per cent from real applications.

fleursavg19lang.text: An average over 19 languages of FLEURS, an n-way parallel read-speech set covering 102 languages with roughly 12 hours of supervision each, recorded from the FLoRes-101 translation sentences.

gsm.text: The grade-school maths task of L-Eval: 100 GSM8K problems, each preceded by 16 long chain-of-thought exemplars for roughly 5.5K tokens of context, testing whether reasoning survives a long prompt.

jinavdr.text: 95 visual document retrieval tasks in 20 languages over web pages, PDFs, scans, slides and images, probed both with natural-language questions and with short keyword queries.

m4singer.text: A Mandarin singing corpus of 700 Chinese pop songs recorded by 20 professional singers covering soprano, alto, tenor and bass, with manually composed musical scores, used for singing synthesis, conversion and transcription.

mmau051525.text: 10,000 audio clips spanning speech, environmental sound and music, each with a human-written question that requires information extraction or reasoning across 27 distinct skills.

nsinstrument.text: Instrument-family classification over NSynth, a set of 305,979 four-second single notes from 1,006 sample-library instruments, each labelled with one of 11 families plus its source type and sonic qualities.

robochallengetable30.text: 30 tabletop manipulation tasks run on real UR5, Franka Panda, ARX-5 and Cobot Magic Aloha arms hosted online, each rolled out 10 times and graded on task success plus a staged progress score with deductions for retries.

simplerwidowx.text: The WidowX-250 BridgeData V2 half of SIMPLER, a simulated stand-in for real robot evaluation: putting a spoon on a towel, a carrot on a plate, stacking blocks and placing an eggplant in a basket.

teval.text: Tool-use evaluation broken into six sub-processes (instruction following, planning, reasoning, retrieval, understanding and review) that are scored separately rather than only through the final task outcome.

vidore1.text: Page-level retrieval over visually rich documents across several domains, languages and practical settings, so that figures, tables, page layout and typography matter rather than extracted text alone.

wildvoice.text: The open-ended spoken question answering split of VoiceBench: 1,000 crowd-sourced recordings of real speakers with diverse accents, used instead of synthesised speech.

jcs.text: JCommonsenseQA from the JGLUE suite: Japanese five-way multiple-choice questions crowdsourced from ConceptNet seeds, with 8,939 training items and about 1,100 each for development and test.

nejumileaderboard.text: A Japanese LLM evaluation run by Weights and Biases that scores general language performance and alignment across about a dozen categories, using Japanese suites such as Jaster, Japanese MT-Bench, JBBQ and JTruthfulQA.

idkb.text: Over a million vision-language items on professional driving knowledge, drawn from driving handbooks, theory test questions and simulated road tests across several countries and languages.

speechmmlu.text: MMLU questions and options resynthesised into speech with a commercial text-to-speech system, giving 8,549 items over 34 subjects in four parallel splits that cross text and speech on both the input and the output side.

c3evalemotion.text: The emotion cloning subset of CV3-Eval: 100 Chinese and 100 English prompts from EmoBox and SeCap labelled happy, sad or angry, divided by whether the target text matches the target emotion, and scored with an emotion classifier.

mmbenchentest.text: The English test split of MMBench, a bilingual multiple-choice vision-language benchmark scored with a circular evaluation that re-asks each question with the answer options permuted.

tauairline.text: The airline domain of tau-bench: 50 customer-service tasks over a database of 500 users, 300 flights and 2,000 reservations, where an agent must follow a written policy while talking to a simulated user, scored by comparing the final database state with the annotated goal.

cursorbench320.text: Cursor's internal coding-agent suite, built from real Cursor sessions traced back to the request that produced the committed code. Task prompts are short and underspecified, span multiple files, and are scored by agentic graders.

milu.text: Multiple-choice questions drawn from Indian regional examinations, covering 8 domains and 41 subjects in 11 Indic languages, mixing general knowledge with India-specific material such as local history, law and festivals.

babyvisionwtools.text: 388 puzzle-style items in 22 subclasses probing core visual ability with almost no language: fine-grained discrimination, visual tracking through mazes and lines, spatial perception of 3D views and folding, and pattern completion, here run with tool use allowed.

gsmhard.text: A harder rewrite of GSM8K in which one number in each question is replaced by a random integer of up to seven digits, with answers recomputed by executing the corresponding Python program.

mmep.text: The perception half of MME: ten yes/no subtasks covering object existence, count, position and colour, plus posters, celebrities, scenes, landmarks, artworks and OCR, with every instruction-answer pair written by hand.

adversarialhealthequity.text: 182 long-form questions written to elicit biased or harmful medical answers, prioritising healthcare access, care quality, and social and environmental determinants of health; answers are rated by physicians on axes including bias and possible harm.

bbqambig.text: The under-informative half of BBQ: hand-written vignettes across nine US social-bias dimensions in which the context never says which person the question refers to, so any named answer rather than “unknown” reflects a stereotype.

chembenchpreference.text: 1,001 questions taken from ChemBench that ask a model to pick the more suitable candidate molecule for therapeutic development.

ctrate.text: 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes from 21,304 patients, each paired with its radiology report, supporting tasks such as multi-abnormality detection and case retrieval.

frmt.text: Professional translations from English into two regional variants each of Portuguese and Mandarin Chinese, with source documents chosen to surface regionally distinct terms and distractors, for few-shot region-aware translation.

humanevalinfilling.text: Fill-in-the-middle variants of HumanEval: a single line, several lines, or a random span is masked out of the canonical solution and the model must generate the missing region from the surrounding code, scored by the original unit tests.

marvl.text: True or false statements written by native speakers about pairs of images in Indonesian, Mandarin, Swahili, Tamil and Turkish, over an ImageNet-style concept hierarchy those speakers chose rather than one scraped from English sources.

msrvttcap.text: Video-to-text description over MSR-VTT, a set of 10,000 web clips totalling 41.2 hours gathered from 257 search queries, each annotated with roughly 20 human-written English sentences.

padufes20.text: 2,298 smartphone photographs of 1,641 skin lesions from 1,373 patients, labelled with six diagnoses (three skin cancers and three benign conditions) plus up to 22 clinical attributes; the cancer cases are biopsy-proven.

rsvqalr.text: The low-resolution half of RSVQA: 772 Sentinel-2 tiles over the Netherlands with 77,232 question-answer pairs generated automatically from OpenStreetMap, asking about object presence, counts, comparisons and rural versus urban land use.

tau2.text: Extends tool-agent-user evaluation to a dual-control setting where the simulated user also holds tools and can change the shared environment, so the agent must coordinate and instruct as well as act; tasks are generated compositionally from atomic components.

vqarad.text: 2,248 question-answer pairs written by clinicians about 315 radiology images from the open MedPix database, split between closed yes/no questions and open-ended ones.

xtremeup.text: A scarce-data benchmark for under-represented languages, built on user-centric tasks with broad practical utility rather than the zero-shot setting, with only small amounts of annotated data per language.

cgbench.text: 1,219 long videos with 12,129 question-answer pairs spanning perception, reasoning and hallucination, where a model must also point to the video clues its answer rests on, checked by white-box and black-box clue-grounded protocols.

exploretom.text: Generates theory-of-mind stories using A* search over a domain-specific language, producing complex but plausible scenarios that stress-test whether a model tracks what each character knows and believes.

moviegenvideobench.text: 1,003 text-to-video prompts covering human activity, animals, nature, physics and unusual subjects, each tagged by motion level and judged by side-by-side human comparison on text alignment, visual quality, and realness and aesthetics.

pidray.text: 47,677 security-screening X-ray images annotated with bounding boxes and segmentation masks for 12 categories of prohibited item, including cases where items are deliberately hidden among cluttered objects.

satlidar.text: One million 512-pixel satellite image tiles paired with LiDAR canopy-height ground truth and split 8/1/1 into train, validation and test, for evaluating global canopy height regression.

youtubevos.text: 4,453 YouTube clips covering 94 object categories with per-frame object masks, for semi-supervised video object segmentation, where a model must track and segment an object through the clip.

gsm8kspeech.text: A spoken version of GSM8K: grade-school math problems are filtered to those that can be said aloud, rewritten into speech-friendly wording where they contain symbols or digits, then synthesised to audio the model must answer from.

cochlscene.text: 76,000 crowdsourced audio clips contributed by 831 people across 13 everyday acoustic scenes, with a manually defined train, validation and test split, for acoustic scene classification.

kimicodebench2.text: Moonshot's in-house coding-agent evaluation: software engineering tasks in more than ten mainstream programming languages across a full production stack, drawn from internal engineering work, production incidents and open-source projects.

spreadsheetbench2.text: 321 end-to-end business spreadsheet tasks built from real financial reports and filings, averaging 11.8 worksheets per workbook, spanning generation, formula debugging and visualisation, and scored against expert-annotated output files.

apmicroeconomics.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement examination in introductory microeconomics, covering scarcity and production possibilities, supply and demand, production and cost under perfect competition, imperfect competition, factor markets, and market failure.

changemyview.text: Built from posts on the r/ChangeMyView subreddit: a model writes a rebuttal to the original poster's stated view, and human raters score its persuasiveness on a 1 to 5 rubric alongside real human replies to the same post.

longformbiologicalriskquestions.text: Long-form questions probing sensitive information across the five stages of biological threat creation (ideation, acquisition, magnification, formulation and release), graded against detailed expert-written rubrics by a model autograder.

multiselectvirologytroubleshooting.text: A fully held-out set of wet-lab virology troubleshooting questions sourced from SecureBio and posed in a multi-select, multimodal format, testing whether a model can work out what went wrong in a laboratory protocol.

promptinjectionevaluations.text: Measures whether a model obeys malicious instructions hidden in content it processes, across three settings: injections encountered while browsing the web, injections returned in tool and connector outputs, and injections placed in code.

tacitknowledgebrainstorm.text: 50 open-ended troubleshooting questions drawn from working virologists and molecular biologists about real experimental problems whose solutions are not documented elsewhere, graded against an ideal completion.

agentworldbench.text: 2,170 samples across seven agent domains in which a language world model must predict the next environment observation; each is paired with the observation captured from real execution and scored on format, factuality, consistency, realism and quality.

dreamgenbench.text: Measures how well a video generative model adapts to a given robot embodiment: it must produce videos of that robot handling unseen objects, performing unseen behaviours and working in unseen environments, scored on instruction following and physics following.

fleurscantonese.text: The Cantonese portion of FLEURS, an n-way parallel read-speech corpus in 102 languages built on the FLoRes-101 translation benchmark with roughly 12 hours of speech supervision per language, used here for speech recognition.

gso.text: Novel view synthesis over Google Scanned Objects, an open collection of over a thousand 3D-scanned household items: given a front view of an object, the model generates a rotated view that is compared against the ground-truth render.

jmmlu.text: 7,536 four-choice questions over 56 subjects in Japanese: most are MMLU items machine-translated and then revised by human translators, alongside newly written questions on Japan-specific subjects such as history, civics and geography.

macagentbench.text: 676 real-world macOS desktop tasks spanning 25 applications, each run in its own container and graded by deterministic rules with fine-grained multi-checkpoint scoring.

mtvqa.text: 2,116 images and 6,778 question-answer pairs in nine languages, annotated by human experts so the questions target the text actually visible inside the image rather than translated captions.

nuscene.text: 1,000 twenty-second driving scenes recorded with six cameras, five radars and a lidar covering a full 360 degree field of view, annotated with 3D boxes for 23 object classes and 8 attributes, for detection, tracking and sensor fusion.

parametriccadbench.text: Tasks in which an agent designs parametric 3D mechanical parts in FreeCAD, covering part generation from a specification, multi-part assemblies and multi-step CAD workflows, verified deterministically in a sandbox against a reference model.

robochallengetable301.text: 30 tabletop manipulation tasks executed on a fleet of online-hosted real robots, stressing precise 3D placement, occlusion and multi-view perception, memory of progress, and long-horizon sequences, scored by success rate and a partial-progress score.

simpst.text: 100 prompts across five harm areas that a model should refuse in almost any application, designed as a quick check for critical safety failures.

vidore3.text: Ten visual document retrieval sets totalling about 26,000 pages and 3,099 queries translated into six languages, with human-verified relevant pages, bounding-box annotations and synthesised answers.

jnli.text: The Japanese natural language inference task in JGLUE: sentence pairs built from Japanese translations of MS COCO captions and labelled entailment, contradiction or neutral, with about 20,000 training and 2,500 test examples.

openkollmleaderboard.text: A Korean leaderboard running the Ko-H5 benchmark: private test sets for Ko-ARC, Ko-HellaSwag, Ko-MMLU and Ko-TruthfulQA, derived from their English originals by machine translation plus human review, together with Ko-CommonGen v2 built from scratch.

mantis.text: 217 questions that each ask about 2 to 5 images together, covering cross-image comparison, counting, spatial relations and spotting differences, drawn from stock photography, MMMU and generated images.

swebenchagentlessrepair.text: Issues from SWE-bench solved with the Agentless pipeline rather than an agent loop: files and functions are localised by retrieval, candidate diffs are sampled directly, and a patch is picked using regression and generated reproduction tests.

database.text: One of AgentBench's environments: 1,599 instructions over real multi-table MySQL databases that an agent must satisfy by issuing select, insert or update statements through an authentic SQL interface, scored by success rate.

mmbench11cn.text: The Chinese half of MMBench: multiple-choice vision questions spanning 20 fine-grained perception and reasoning abilities, scored with CircularEval, which re-asks each question with the answer options cyclically permuted.

tauretail.text: The retail customer-service domain of tau-bench: 115 tasks over a database of 500 users, 50 products and 1,000 orders, where an agent cancels, modifies, returns or exchanges orders for a simulated user under written policy, graded by final database state.

draco.text: One hundred deep-research tasks sampled from de-identified Perplexity Deep Research requests across 10 domains, each graded against a task-specific rubric covering factual accuracy, breadth and depth, presentation and citation quality.

bfcl3multiturn.text: 200 base and 800 augmented multi-turn tool-use sessions covering missing parameters, missing functions, long distracting context and combinations of the three, checked against the backend state left behind after the calls execute.

mmmlunonenglish.text: The non-English portion of the MMLU test set as rendered into 14 languages by professional human translators, covering 57 subjects in multiple-choice form.

afrimedqa.text: Around 15,000 medical questions contributed through more than 60 medical schools in 16 African countries and spanning 32 specialties, in both multiple-choice and open-ended consumer-question form.

bbqdisambig.text: Questions whose context does contain enough information to answer, from the Bias Benchmark for Question Answering, testing whether a model's social bias overrides the answer the passage supports. Covers nine social dimensions.

chemdraw.text: Molecular structure recognition over 5,700 synthetic molecule drawings rendered with the ChemDraw library, where the model must emit the SMILES string for the depicted molecule and is scored by exact match.

cwebench.text: One hundred held-out audit-and-patch tasks on real open-source projects pinned to a commit, covering 54 vulnerability types across six languages. A patch counts only if an executed exploit stops working and the regression tests still pass.

humanevalmultiline.text: 5,815 infilling tasks that blank out several consecutive lines of a HumanEval solution and ask the model to fill the gap from the surrounding prefix and suffix.

medicationqa.text: 674 question-answer pairs built from real consumer questions about medications, annotated with the focus and type of each question and the source of its answer.

parlaidialoguesafety.text: Detection of offensive language in dialogue, where whether an utterance is offensive depends on the conversation around it, collected with an iterative build it, break it, fix it loop in which crowdworkers try to fool a classifier that is then retrained on their successful attacks.

rte.text: A binary entailment decision over sentence pairs drawn from news and Wikipedia, pooling the RTE1, RTE2, RTE3 and RTE5 challenge sets as packaged in GLUE, with neutral and contradiction collapsed into one label.

youcook2cap.text: Captioning the procedure steps of 2,000 YouTube cooking videos covering 89 recipes and 176 hours, where each video carries 3 to 16 temporally localized segments described by an imperative English sentence.

cifar10.text: 60,000 colour images of 32 by 32 pixels in ten mutually exclusive object classes, split into 50,000 for training and 10,000 for testing, used as a small-scale image classification task.

fgvcaircraft.text: 10,200 aircraft photographs labelled with a hierarchy of 102 variants, 70 families and 41 manufacturers, each with a tight bounding box, used for fine-grained visual classification.

mtobfullbookengkgvkgveng.text: Translation between English and Kalamang, a language with fewer than 200 speakers and almost no web presence, where the model works from a field-linguistics grammar book and bilingual word list placed in its context rather than from a parallel corpus. Scored in both directions.

places205.text: 2.5 million photographs labelled with 205 scene categories, between 5,000 and 15,000 images per class, used to test recognition of the place a photo was taken rather than the objects in it.

sav.text: 51,000 videos annotated with 643,000 class-agnostic spatio-temporal masks, or masklets, ranging from whole buildings down to small parts, released for training and testing video object segmentation.

yttemporal1b.text: 20 million YouTube videos spanning over a billion frames, including documentaries, how-to videos and vlogs, distributed as video IDs and metadata for learning from video together with audio and transcribed speech.

harmbench.text: A standardised framework for automated red teaming of language models, pairing harmful-behaviour prompts with attack methods so that attacks and defences can be compared under one protocol.

apphysics2.text: The algebra-based second-year Advanced Placement physics exam, covering thermodynamics, electric force and fields, circuits, magnetism and electromagnetism, geometric optics, waves and physical optics, and modern physics.

charxivd.text: Questions about the basic elements of 2,323 charts taken from arXiv papers, such as labels, ticks and counts, rather than about what the chart implies. This is the descriptive half of CharXiv.

graduaterecordexaminationgrequantitative.text: The quantitative section of the GRE General Test, covering arithmetic, algebra, geometry and data analysis at a level no higher than a second course in algebra, in quantitative-comparison, multiple-choice and numeric-entry formats.

longformbioriskquestions.text: Long-form free-response questions spanning the five stages of the biological threat creation process, written with Gryphon Scientific and graded by a model against detailed rubrics checked with a biosecurity expert.

multiturnjailbreakevaluations.text: Adaptive attackers drawn from internal red teaming probe the model over several turns and change strategy in response to its replies; for a budget of n attempts the model passes only if it avoids unsafe assistance on every one.

quantbench.text: 25 verified, auto-gradable reasoning puzzles taken from the recruiting competitions run by quantitative trading firms, also presented in a five-option multiple-choice form so that grading is unambiguous.

ai2dtest.text: Over 5,000 grade-school science diagrams annotated with their constituents and the relationships between them, paired with about 15,000 multiple-choice questions; this is the standard held-out split.

crosscodelongeval.text: 5,000 chunk-completion and 5,000 function-completion instances sampled from roughly 1,500 Python repositories, testing repository-level code completion where the missing code may depend on other files.

ebench.text: An Isaac Sim benchmark for indoor mobile manipulation on a dual-arm mobile platform, 26 task types over 794 evaluation instances, perturbed along background, instruction and object axes and reported as both a success rate and a process score.

fleursen2xx.text: Speech-to-text translation out of English into the other languages of a 102-language parallel read-speech corpus built on FLoRes-101, with roughly 12 hours of recorded speech per language.

gtzan.text: 1,000 audio excerpts of 30 seconds each, evenly divided across ten music genres, used for automatic musical genre classification.

joinavbench.text: Questions that cannot be answered from video or audio alone, spanning five cognitive dimensions, four kinds of audio information (speech, sound events, music and vocal traits) and single-scene, cross-scene and full-scene spans.

mtvqatest.text: 6,778 question-answer pairs written by human experts over 2,116 images in nine languages, covering reading and reasoning about text that appears inside the image. This is the held-out split.

objectron.text: 14,819 object-centric videos with about 4 million annotated frames over nine everyday categories, each object labelled with a 3D bounding box and pose and scored with a 3D intersection-over-union metric.

passkeyretrieval.text: A long-context stress test in which a number is hidden somewhere inside a document of irrelevant filler text, up to a million tokens long, and the model must find and report it.

robospatialhome.text: 350 hand-written spatial questions over RGB and depth captures of real indoor scenes, asking whether a spatial relation holds between two objects, pointing at free space, and judging whether a named object would fit there.

skillsbench.text: 87 tasks across 8 domains, each paired with a curated Agent Skill (a structured package of procedural knowledge loaded at inference time) and a deterministic verifier, run in matched conditions with and without the Skill.

wise.text: 1,000 prompts over 25 subdomains of cultural common sense, spatio-temporal reasoning and natural science, testing whether a text-to-image model applies world knowledge, scored by a knowledge-image alignment metric rather than by CLIP similarity.

jsquad.text: A Japanese reading-comprehension set in SQuAD 1.1 format built from scratch over Japanese Wikipedia rather than translated, with roughly 62,700 training and 4,400 development questions, all of them answerable.

harveylabvals.text: Over 1,250 long-horizon legal tasks across 24 practice areas, each giving a partner-style work request plus a client matter of documents, graded against expert-written rubrics under all-pass scoring where every criterion must be met.

xbenchdeepsearchzh.text: A Chinese-language deep-search set that tests an agent's use of search and retrieval tools, published in dated releases that are refreshed over time and distributed encrypted so that crawlers cannot contaminate it.

maplm.text: Traffic and map scene understanding from paired panoramic camera images and a bird's-eye-view rendering of a LiDAR point cloud, annotated at feature, lane and road level and posed as question answering.

vabenchpoint.text: A region-referring grounding test for embodied models: given a reasoning-heavy instruction about a cluttered scene, the model outputs image points and is scored on whether they land inside the target region.

digitalcardgame.text: AgentBench's card-game environment, a simplified version of Aquawar in which the agent controls a team of four fish cards in turn-based battles against an algorithmic opponent and is scored on win rate.

mmbrowsecomp.text: 400 hand-crafted browsing questions whose evidence sits in web images and video, so text-only retrieval is not enough, each paired with a verified checklist of the steps a correct answer has to cover.

tdiuc.text: Over 1.6 million visual questions sorted into 12 types, including questions that are meaningless for the given image, so that accuracy can be reported per type instead of as one number dominated by the easy types.

agenticmisalignmentsuite.text: Fictional corporate scenarios in which a model running as an autonomous email agent faces replacement or a conflicting goal, testing whether it turns to blackmail, leaking confidential documents, or other harmful insider actions.

frontierfinance.text: An open set of 220 expert-written investment research queries, each scored against source-attributed rubric items marked must-have or informational, spanning screening, earnings analysis, company research and macro work.

cmo24.text: Six proof problems from China's national mathematics championship for 2024, used as a natural language theorem proving test in which the written proofs are assessed by mathematical experts.

proofnet.text: 371 undergraduate pure mathematics problems from standard textbooks in real and complex analysis, linear algebra, abstract algebra and topology, each with a natural language statement, a natural language proof and a formal Lean 3 statement, for autoformalization and formal proving.

aokvqada.text: One of two evaluation settings for A-OKVQA's roughly 25,000 crowdsourced image questions that need commonsense and world knowledge: the model writes a free-form answer instead of picking from four choices.

bcherust.text: The Rust edition of HumanEval produced by BabelCode, which translates the original Python problems and their test suites into 16 languages so the same programs can be executed and checked in each.

cmtbenchmark.text: 50 research-level condensed matter theory problems written and verified by an international panel of physicists, covering quantum many-body and classical statistical mechanics methods, machine-graded against expert answers with symbolic handling of non-commuting operators.

doclaynet.text: 80,863 PDF pages from finance, science, patents, tenders, law and manuals, hand-annotated with bounding boxes in 11 layout classes such as table, formula, caption and section header, with some pages annotated two or three times.

genexam.text: 1,000 exam-style drawing problems across 10 school subjects, organised under a four-level taxonomy, where a text-to-image model must render the answer; each problem carries a ground-truth image and fine-grained scoring points for semantic correctness and visual plausibility.

internalctf.text: Google's in-house suite of 13 capture-the-flag challenges, used in its offensive cybersecurity evaluations, in which the agent must break into a simulated server.

mimiccxr.text: 377,110 chest radiographs from 227,835 imaging studies at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, each study paired with its free-text radiology report, de-identified and released in DICOM form.

multilingualrepresentationalbias.text: A Google evaluation of toxic language and bias around identity terms in dialog use, run across 14 languages including Arabic, Hindi, Japanese and Swedish, with outcomes broken out by language and by identity term.

therapeuticsdatacommons.text: An open platform of 66 machine learning datasets grouped into 22 drug discovery and development tasks, with prescribed data splits, evaluation strategies, molecule generation oracles and leaderboards, all reachable from one Python library.

airsbench.text: 20 machine learning research tasks drawn from recent papers, each handed to the agent only as a problem, a dataset and a metric; the agent must generate, run and refine its own code to produce predictions.

cruxevaloutput.text: One of two tasks defined over 800 short Python functions in CRUXEval: given a function and an input, predict what it returns, checked by executing an equality assertion on the answer.

gtea.text: Egocentric video of four subjects performing seven kinds of daily activity, annotated with segmentation masks of the hands, used as the hand-segmenting task in Meta's zero-shot segmentation suite.

lvis.text: Around 2 million high-quality instance segmentation masks over more than 1,000 object categories across 164,000 images, built so that a long tail of rare categories has very few examples.

ndispark.text: Images of parking lots taken from video footage by day and by night under varying weather conditions and camera angles, annotated with instance masks for vehicle segmentation.

plmvideobench.text: Five video understanding tasks released with Meta's Perception Language Model: multiple-choice questions on fine-grained activity, open-ended questions on smart-glasses video, and captioning or temporally localising the events involving one subject in a clip.

star.text: Situated reasoning over real-world videos of human actions, with interaction, sequence, prediction and feasibility questions generated procedurally from hyper-graphs of the entities and relations extracted from each clip.
