codecontests.text: DeepMind's competitive programming dataset, with problems gathered from Codeforces, CodeChef, AtCoder, HackerEarth and Aizu, each paired with input-output test cases plus correct and incorrect human submissions.

humanevalfimpython.text: The Python fill-in-the-middle form of HumanEval: a span is cut out of a reference solution and the model must reconstruct it from the surrounding prefix and suffix rather than writing the function from scratch.

vlguard.text: A vision-language safety dataset of image and instruction pairs spanning harmful categories, curated for safety fine-tuning and used as a test of whether a vision-language model refuses unsafe image-text requests.

finsearchcompt3.text: The hardest of FinSearchComp's three task types, Complex Historical Investigation, which asks for multi-period aggregation or synthesis such as finding the month with the largest single-month gain of an index over a long window, annotated by professional financial experts.

arcagi2verified.text: Grid puzzle tasks from the public and semi-private ARC-AGI-2 evaluation splits, 120 each, run and certified by the ARC Prize Foundation under a cost cap rather than self-reported by the model developer.

healthbenchconsensus.text: A variant of HealthBench covering 3,671 of its health conversations, keeping only the rubric criteria that a majority of multiple physicians independently agreed were appropriate, so grading is heavily validated.

openaiprs.text: Tasks sourced from internal OpenAI pull requests: the agent starts on the pre-PR branch of an OpenAI repository, is prompted with the required change, edits files using command-line tools and Python, and is graded by hidden unit tests.

scalemultichallenge.text: Multi-turn conversations built around four categories of challenge that require accurate instruction following, context allocation and in-context reasoning, with free-form replies graded by an LLM judge against instance-level rubrics.

troubleshootingbench.text: 52 wet-lab biology protocols transcribed by PhD scientists in virology, genetics, microbiology or protein engineering, each paired with three short-answer questions that introduce a realistic execution error and describe the failed outcome.

alimeetingtest.text: The 20-session, 10-hour test split of a Mandarin meeting corpus, with 2 to 4 participants per 15 to 30 minute discussion captured both by an 8-channel far-field microphone array and by each speaker's headset, for diarization and multi-speaker transcription.

clawevalavg.text: An end-to-end benchmark for agents acting in the real world, totalling 300 tasks split into general agent work across 24 categories, multimodal tasks such as webpage generation and document extraction, and multi-turn tasks.

hm3d.text: 1,000 building-scale textured 3D reconstructions of real interiors, including multi-floor homes and stores, rendered as photo-realistic environments for training and testing embodied navigation agents.

liberoplus.text: 10,030 robot manipulation tasks built by perturbing the LIBERO benchmark along seven dimensions: object layout, camera viewpoint, robot initial state, language instruction, lighting, background texture and sensor noise.

mdeval.text: A code debugging benchmark of about 3.9K test samples covering 20 programming languages, with three tasks centred on locating and fixing bugs.

multimathematics.text: Qwen's multilingual mathematics category, reported from MGSM (Multilingual Grade School Math) with eight-shot prompts, alongside its multilingual exam, understanding and translation categories.

omni3d.text: 234,000 images carrying more than 3 million annotated 3D object instances across 98 categories, assembled from existing datasets, for predicting 3D bounding boxes from a single image across varied cameras and scene types.

speechrole.text: An evaluation of speech role-playing agents that scores the generated audio itself on interaction ability, speech expressiveness and role-playing fidelity; the accompanying corpus holds 98 roles and 111k speech-to-speech conversations.

vlmsarebiased.text: Counterfactual images across seven domains including animals, logos, chess, board games, optical illusions and patterned grids, where a familiar object is subtly altered and the model is asked to count or identify what is actually shown.

artifactsbench.text: 1,825 visual code generation tasks whose outputs are programmatically rendered and captured as temporal screenshots, then judged by a multimodal model working from a fine-grained per-task checklist alongside the source code.

cagui.text: A Chinese Android GUI benchmark in two parts: grounding, which links on-screen widgets to their text and function through OCR and captioning, and agent, which requires multi-step taps, scrolls and typing to carry out an instruction in real Chinese apps.

nolima.text: A needle-in-a-haystack long-context test whose needles share almost no wording with the question, so the answer cannot be located by literal matching and the model has to infer the latent association.

aitw.text: 715k demonstration episodes covering 30k instructions on Android phones, each recording the screens, the natural language instruction and the gestures performed; available actions must be inferred from the visual appearance of the interface rather than from UI metadata.

omnimath.text: 4,428 competition-level olympiad mathematics problems, sorted into 33 sub-domains and 10 difficulty tiers, with reference solutions and explicit answers checked by an accompanying judge model.

vcreasy.text: In the easy setting of VCR-Wiki, a Wikipedia image is shown with its caption rendered into the picture and part of the text covered over; the model must restore the hidden words from the remaining pixel fragments and surrounding context.

financeagent.text: Built by Vals AI with Stanford researchers and industry experts: 537 questions covering the work of an entry-level financial analyst, including document retrieval, market research and financial projections.

openrca.text: Root-cause analysis over software telemetry: given a natural-language query plus KPI time series, dependency trace graphs and semi-structured logs from a deployed system, a model must name the time, component and reason of a failure.

ccpm.text: A Chinese classical poetry matching task: given a modern Chinese translation of a line of poetry, pick the original line out of four candidates, with distractors drawn from similar lines in a poetry corpus.

hungarianexam.text: The 33 problems of the May 2023 Hungarian national high school mathematics final exam, released as free-response questions spanning algebra, geometry, logarithms, combinatorics and basic statistics.

mrcr1m.text: Multi-round coreference resolution run at a one-million-token context: a synthetic chat repeats several near-identical user requests, and the model must reproduce the reply to one specified instance, prefixed with a given hash.

agentclinicmedqa.text: 215 USMLE-derived cases turned into interactive clinical simulations: a doctor agent must reach a diagnosis by questioning a patient agent and ordering exams from a measurement agent, with a moderator agent checking the answer.

bchec.text: HumanEval's Python programming problems translated into C# with the BabelCode framework, so generated solutions are executed against the translated tests in that language.

chestimagenome.text: Automatically derived scene graphs for 242,072 chest X-ray images, linking 29 anatomical locations with bounding boxes to their radiological attributes, plus localized comparison relations across a patient's sequential exams.

chestxray14.text: A hospital-scale chest radiograph set of 108,948 frontal-view images from 32,717 patients, with thoracic disease labels text-mined from the accompanying radiology reports.

futuremathbasic.text: An internal Google DeepMind set of PhD-level mathematics exercises, used to probe reasoning a step beyond Olympiad-level problems.

humanevalsingleline.text: One of the HumanEval Infilling splits: a single line is removed from a HumanEval reference solution and the model must fill it in from the surrounding prefix and suffix, checked by the original unit tests.

medqa.text: Multiple-choice questions taken from professional medical board examinations in English, simplified Chinese and traditional Chinese, posed as open-domain question answering over an accompanying document collection.

msrvttqa.text: Open-ended question answering over the MSR-VTT collection of web video clips, with question-answer pairs generated automatically from the clips' human-written descriptions.

pathmcqa.text: An internal Google set of 450 histopathology patches from 354 whole slide images, each posed as a multiple-choice question on cancer identification, grading or histologic subtyping, labelled by board-certified pathologists.

runcode.text: One of the Hidden Agenda persuasion tasks: posing as an educational chatbot, the agent must talk a human study participant into running obfuscated JavaScript in their browser console.

weboflies.text: A deception test in which a person answers five binary quiz questions with help from an agent that is randomly either honest or instructed to defend the wrong answer; the metric is the shift in the person's stated belief.

youtube.text: An internal Google test set of English (en-US) YouTube audio used to measure automatic speech recognition, scored by word error rate.

cifar100.text: 60,000 colour images of 32x32 pixels across 100 classes grouped into 20 superclasses, with 500 training and 100 test images per class; each image carries both a fine and a coarse label.

flowers.text: Fine-grained classification over 102 categories of flowers common in the United Kingdom, with 40 to 258 images per category and large variation in scale, pose and lighting both within and between categories.

intphys2.text: A video benchmark for intuitive physics built on the violation-of-expectation paradigm: models must tell possible from impossible events in controlled synthetic scenes testing permanence, immutability, spatio-temporal continuity and solidity.

mtobhalfbookengkgvkgveng.text: Sentence-level translation between English and Kalamang (kgv), a language with fewer than 200 speakers and virtually no web presence, with only half of the reference grammar in context alongside a bilingual word list and a few hundred parallel sentences.

plittersdorf.text: Instance segmentation masks for wildlife in stereo images captured by the SOCRATES camera trap, used as one of the out-of-domain sets for testing segmentation transfer.

sketch.text: A robustness test set of sketch-like images matching the ImageNet-1k validation set in categories and scale, used to measure cross-domain transfer of classifiers trained on natural photographs.

ytvis21.text: The 2021 edition of YouTube-VIS: 3,859 videos with roughly 232,000 manual annotations over a 40-category label set, requiring simultaneous detection, segmentation and tracking of object instances across frames.

codesearchnetcodecode.text: A code-to-code retrieval task built from CodeSearchNet: given a snippet of real GitHub code as the query, the system must retrieve the code that appears in the same context.

swedev.text: Feature-driven development on large existing codebases: 500 test instances, each shipped with a runnable environment and developer-authored unit tests that decide whether the requested functionality works.

appsychology.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement exam in introductory psychology: 75 multiple-choice questions plus an article-analysis and an evidence-based free-response question, covering psychological theories, research methods and data interpretation.

charxivdescriptive.text: One of the two question types in CharXiv: 9,292 questions from 19 templates about basic elements of 2,323 real arXiv figures, such as titles, axis labels, tick counts and subplot layout, a quarter of them deliberately unanswerable.

economicallyimportanttasks.text: An internal OpenAI set of complex, economically valuable knowledge-work tasks sourced from experts across many occupations and industries, with model outputs judged by experts against baselines written by top performers in each field.

graduaterecordexaminationgreverbal.text: One of the three measures of the GRE General Test, made up of reading comprehension, text completion and sentence equivalence questions that probe analysis of written material and relationships among words and concepts.

lsmdc.text: 118,114 short movie clips from 202 films, each paired with a sentence taken from the film's audio description or script, used to evaluate automatic video description.

nanogpt.text: An AI self-improvement eval in which an agent gets a single H100 GPU and must rewrite a small language-model training script, tuning hyperparameters and diagnosing bottlenecks, to reach a target validation objective as fast as possible.

tau2benchairline.text: One of three domains in the tau-squared benchmark, carried over from tau-bench: 50 customer-service tasks where an agent uses read and write tools over a database of users, flights and reservations to satisfy a simulated user under a written airline policy.

aiarena.text: An open Elo-based platform for image generation run by Alibaba: two anonymous models generate from the same prompt and a human voter picks the better image, drawing on about 5,000 prompts spanning subject, style and photographic perspective.

chartmimic.text: Chart-to-code generation over 4,800 human-curated triplets of a figure, a textual instruction and reference code: the model sees the chart and instruction and must emit code that renders the same chart.

fleurss2tt.text: One of the four tasks supported by FLEURS, an n-way parallel read-speech corpus of roughly 12 hours per language in 102 languages built by recording the FLoRes-101 translation benchmark: translating spoken input into text in another language.

gymanything.text: A framework that wraps real desktop software such as browsers, IDEs, medical records systems and CAD tools as agent environments behind one API, pairing each task with a setup script and an automatic checker.

kernelbenchl3.text: The hardest of KernelBench's three tiers: 50 full PyTorch model architectures drawn from popular GitHub repositories, for which a model must write faster GPU kernels that still match the reference outputs on random inputs.

magicdataramc.text: 180 hours of Mandarin conversational speech recorded over mobile phones across 15 topic domains, with manual transcriptions and speaker voice-activity timestamps.

mmbenchendev11.text: A bilingual multiple-choice vision-language set spanning 20 fine-grained perception and reasoning skills; this is the publicly released English dev portion of version 1.1, scored with CircularEval, which demands the right answer under every cyclic shift of the options.

ocnli.text: Around 56,000 Chinese premise-hypothesis pairs written and annotated from scratch by native speakers rather than machine translated, labelled for entailment, contradiction or neutrality.

pawsx.text: 23,659 human-translated paraphrase identification pairs in French, Spanish, German, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, adapted from PAWS so that the two sentences share most of their words but differ in structure.

robotwineasy.text: The clean evaluation setting of the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual manipulation benchmark: policies trained on 50 expert demonstrations per task are rolled out on 50 dual-arm simulation tasks without the clutter, lighting and texture randomization of the Hard setting.

theoremqa.text: 800 expert-curated questions that each require applying one of 350 named theorems, for example Taylor's theorem or Huffman coding, to solve a challenging science problem.

visfactor.text: 20 vision-centric subtests digitized from FRCT, an established cognitive psychology assessment covering four domains of human visual cognition, with a generator that builds further test cases at controllable difficulty.

wode2e.text: 4,000 Waymo driving segments mined for long-tail situations, where a model must predict five seconds of future bird's-eye-view waypoints from camera images, the vehicle's pose history and routing information.

kbankmmlu.text: An in-house Korean finance benchmark from Upstage, drawn from recent national and accredited private financial qualification exams.

wikitablequestions.text: 22,033 complex questions over semi-structured HTML tables drawn from Wikipedia, whose answers require compositional reasoning across table cells rather than a single lookup.

xbrowse.text: An internal xAI evaluation of an agent's multi-hop search and browsing ability over content on X.

metavqa.text: A closed-loop benchmark for embodied spatial reasoning in driving scenes, with visual questions generated automatically from Set-of-Mark prompts and top-down ground truth over nuScenes and Waymo data, plus simulated driving episodes.

visualwebbench.text: Seven web-page tasks over 1.5K human-curated instances, covering captioning, OCR, understanding and grounding on screenshots, to measure fine-grained web abilities separately from end-to-end agent behaviour.

eli5.text: 270,000 threads from the Explain Like I'm Five subreddit, pairing open-ended questions with multi-sentence community answers, plus a large set of web documents supplied to help answer them.

mmlongbench128k.text: Long-context vision-language evaluation over 13,331 examples in five task families (visual retrieval-augmented generation, needle-in-a-haystack, many-shot in-context learning, summarization and long-document VQA), here at the 128K-token input bucket.

tedstest.text: A 93-image table recognition test set combining generated wired and wireless tables, images from WTW and PubTabNet, and hand-labelled photographs, each with ground-truth HTML and scored by tree-edit-distance-based similarity.

firefox.text: An exploit-development evaluation built with Mozilla: given 50 crash categories in Firefox 147 and the matching crashes, a model works inside a SpiderMonkey shell container to turn one into a working exploit, graded 0, 0.5 or 1.0 over 250 trials.

organicchemistry2.text: An internal Anthropic chemistry evaluation covering prediction of molecular structures from spectroscopy data, design of multi-step synthetic routes, reaction product prediction and reading of chemical structure images, updated with harder problems suggested by expert chemists.

chartographywtools.text: A Surge AI benchmark of 100 chart-reading tasks on specialist chart types (Kaplan-Meier curves, candlestick charts, contour maps, Sankey diagrams, Bode plots), each graded against an expert-set acceptable range; the tooled variant adds a container and an image-cropping tool.

hungariannationalhighschoolexam.text: A held-out set of 33 problems from the 2023 Hungarian national high-school mathematics finals, covering set theory, combinatorics, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, sequences and probability, graded by hand against the official rubric.

multiloko.text: A multilingual knowledge benchmark over 31 languages: 500 locally sourced questions per language plus human-authored and machine-authored translation partitions, split evenly into a development set and a blind out-of-distribution test set.

agentclinicmimiciv.text: 200 simulated clinical cases built from single-diagnosis MIMIC-IV electronic health records, in which a doctor agent questions a patient agent and orders tests from a measurement agent before committing to a diagnosis that a moderator agent grades.

bchego.text: The HumanEval Python programming problems and their unit tests translated into Go with Google's BabelCode framework, then scored by executing the translated tests.

delec2.text: The C2 (mastery) level of the Spanish proficiency exam issued by the Instituto Cervantes; models answered recent past or practice papers zero-shot, with the writing section rated by three native-speaker contractors and weighted equally with the rest.

icdar15incidental.text: Challenge 4 of the ICDAR 2015 Robust Reading Competition, using scene photos captured incidentally by wearable cameras: about 4,500 readable words over 1,000 training images, annotated as four-corner word boxes, for text localisation, word recognition and end-to-end reading.

medqausmle.text: Multiple-choice questions collected from professional medical board exams; the English portion of roughly 12,700 questions comes from the US Medical Licensing Examination and is posed open-domain, with no reference passage supplied.

msvdqa.text: Open-ended question answering over short YouTube clips from the Microsoft Video Description corpus, with question-answer pairs generated automatically from the clips' human-written descriptions and then post-processed.

pathvqa.text: 32,799 open-ended questions over 4,998 pathology images drawn from textbooks and online digital libraries, with question-answer pairs generated from the image captions by an NLP pipeline and then manually verified.

scaleaisaudiomultichallenge.text: An audio multi-turn conversation evaluation from Scale AI, testing complex instruction following and long-horizon reasoning in speech that carries the interruptions and hesitations typical of real-world audio.

tcf.text: The standardised French proficiency exam designed by France Education International and accredited by the French Ministry of Education; models answered recent past or practice papers zero-shot at the C2 level, with writing rated by three native speakers.

wic.text: A word sense task from SuperGLUE: given two sentences that share a target word, decide whether the word carries the same meaning in both, built from expert-curated annotations to probe context-sensitive representations.

abcbench.text: Three agentic biology tasks from SecureBio, each solved by a ReAct agent with biotools: designing DNA fragments that assemble into a full-length construct, altering those fragments to evade DNA synthesis screening, and writing a liquid-handling robot protocol.

cimemories.text: A contextual-integrity benchmark for persistent memory: synthetic user profiles carry over 100 attributes each, paired with tasks where an attribute is essential in some and out of scope in others, scoring both inappropriate disclosures and missing attributes.

food101.text: 101 food categories with 101,000 photographs, 750 uncleaned training images and 250 manually reviewed test images per class, all rescaled to a maximum side length of 512 pixels.

ishape.text: Six sub-datasets, one real and five synthetic, for instance segmentation of irregularly shaped objects whose bounding boxes overlap heavily and which have extreme aspect ratios and many connected components per instance.

multilingualholisticbias.text: 20,459 sentences in 50 languages, formed by crossing 118 demographic descriptors across 13 axes with three sentence patterns, used to expose demographic imbalance in translation quality.

plmfgqa.text: The fine-grained question answering split of PLM-VideoBench: 4,371 multiple-choice questions about short video segments probing what an actor does and how it is done, reported as multi-binary accuracy so every binary form of a question must be answered correctly.

smartglasses.text: The egocentric subset of SAM 3's SA-Co/VEval video benchmark, recorded on wearable glasses: each video ships with a list of roughly 2,400 noun phrases, and the model must segment and track every instance matching each phrase.

ytvos19.text: The 2019 release of YouTube-VOS for semi-supervised video object segmentation: 3,471 training videos over 65 categories plus 507 validation videos, with only the first-frame mask given and 26 validation categories held out of training.

codesearchnetdoc2code.text: A code retrieval task built on CodeSearchNet: given a docstring taken from real GitHub code, retrieve the corresponding code.

humanevalbash.text: Python programming problems from HumanEval and their unit tests rendered in Bash, so a model writes a shell solution that is scored by executing the translated tests.

mbppbase.text: Short crowd-sourced Python programming problems from MBPP scored only with the dataset's own original assert statements, the base half of EvalPlus's MBPP and MBPP+ pair, whose plus tests add roughly 35 times more cases.

deckbench.text: An in-house Moonshot evaluation of whether an agent can produce presentation decks from task descriptions drawn from real usage scenarios.

legalresearchbench.text: A Vals AI benchmark testing whether agents can carry out realistic US legal research across eight practice areas using case-law search, web search and document retrieval, graded against rubrics written by practising lawyers.

valsindex.text: A composite score from Vals AI aggregating its own evaluations of economically valuable work, spanning coding (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, Vibe Code Bench), finance, legal case law, and knowledge and reasoning suites.

apstatistics.text: A College Board Advanced Placement exam taken by US high-school students: 42 multiple-choice questions and four multi-part free-response questions, 90 minutes per half, covering data exploration, sampling, probability and statistical inference.

charxivmissingimage.text: A deception probe made by stripping the images out of the multimodal CharXiv chart benchmark, measuring how often a model fabricates an answer instead of flagging that the referenced image is missing.

emotionalreliance.text: An OpenAI disallowed-content evaluation set covering unhealthy emotional dependence on or attachment to ChatGPT, built around cases where earlier models fell short and graded by LLM policy graders on whether the response is unsafe.

graduaterecordexaminationgrewriting.text: The essay measure of the GRE General Test, in which the writer analyses an issue prompt and builds a supported argument against the clock in a basic word processor without spell-check, rated on argument quality rather than subject knowledge.

makemepay.text: An open-sourced manipulation evaluation in which two models role-play a con artist and a mark who has just been awarded $100; the con artist tries to talk the mark into paying, scored by how often a payment occurs and what share of the available money is extracted.

nucleobench.text: A benchmark of neural nucleic acid design algorithms over 16 biological optimisation tasks spanning cell-type-specific gene regulation, transcription factor binding, chromatin accessibility and gene expression, with sequences from 200 base pairs to nearly 200,000.

sad.text: Over 13,000 questions in seven task categories probing whether a model recognises its own generated text, predicts its own behaviour, can tell an internal evaluation from real deployment, and follows instructions that depend on self-knowledge.

tau2benchretail.text: Order management, returns and product inquiries handled by a customer-service agent under a written domain policy, calling tools against a database while a simulated user supplies information, graded on the resulting database state.

airbench.text: An audio instruction benchmark in two parts: a foundation set of roughly 19,000 single-choice questions over 19 tasks on speech, natural sound and music, and a chat set of about 2,000 open-ended exchanges scored by a language-model judge given the audio's meta-information.

chartmimic2direct.text: Chart-to-code generation in its direct setting: shown a scientific chart, the model must write code that re-renders it faithfully, drawn from human-curated figure, instruction and code triplets and scored by multi-level metrics over the code and the rendered chart.

cruxo.text: The output-prediction half of CRUXEval: given one of 800 short Python functions of 3 to 13 lines and an input, predict what the function returns.

editingbench.text: 1,500 image-editing cases split evenly across six categories (scene-level semantic transformation, perceptual enhancement, object-centric manipulation, text editing, identity-preserving editing and style transfer), judged by vision-language models against per-category rubrics.

fleursxx2en.text: The into-English speech translation split of FLEURS, an n-way parallel read-speech corpus in 102 languages built on the FLoRes-101 translation benchmark with roughly 12 hours of supervision per language.

gymcards.text: Four gym-style visual decision tasks that require reading numbers off an image and reasoning arithmetically: moving a number toward a target on a number line, building card expressions that evaluate to 12 or to 24, and playing blackjack.

kespeech.text: An open-source Mandarin speech corpus covering standard Mandarin and eight regional subdialects, among them Northeastern, Ji-Lu, Zhongyuan and Jiao-Liao, with audio paired to Chinese transcripts for dialectal speech recognition.

magnatagatune.text: A music auto-tagging dataset of short audio clips from the Magnatune label, annotated with tags collected from players of the TagATune game and distributed with clip metadata, tag annotations and similarity judgements.

mmbenchgui.text: A hierarchical GUI-agent benchmark across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android and web, with four levels covering interface content understanding, element grounding, task automation and task collaboration, plus an efficiency-quality metric for online runs.

ocrbench2en.text: The English half of a bilingual text-centric benchmark for multimodal models, with 10,000 human-verified question-answer pairs over 31 scenarios covering text recognition, localisation, layout understanding and reasoning over document elements.

pbench.text: A world-model benchmark of 1,044 items pairing a text prompt and a conditioning image with yes/no questions about physical behaviour across driving, robotics, industry, physics, human activity and common sense, reported alongside video-quality metrics.

robotwineasyhard.text: Two evaluation settings of a 50-task bimanual manipulation benchmark: policies trained on 50 clean demonstrations per task are rolled out either in clean scenes (Easy) or under randomised clutter, lighting, textures and table heights (Hard).

songbench.text: A fine-grained benchmark for song quality assessment that rates generated songs on seven dimensions (vocal, instrument, melody, structure, arrangement, mixing and musicality), fitted to 11,717 samples annotated by music professionals.

think.text: A response-safety test set built by prompting reasoning models with BeaverTails prompts and manually annotating the resulting reasoning traces and answers, so a guard model is judged on moderating thinking content rather than final replies.

visrag.text: Page-image retrieval over six document question-answering sets (ArXivQA, ChartQA, MP-DocVQA, InfographicsVQA, PlotQA and SlideVQA), where a query must be matched to the right page embedded directly as an image rather than parsed into text.

workspacebench.text: 388 curated tasks set in five simulated professional workspaces holding 20,476 files across 74 file types, testing whether an agent can explore a noisy workspace and find, interpret and combine the files a task depends on.

kbl.text: A Korean legal benchmark of roughly 3,300 examples: seven knowledge tasks, four reasoning tasks and bar exam questions across four domains, run both closed-book and with retrieval over a corpus of Korean statutes and precedents.

3dcodebench.text: Agentic procedural 3D modelling through code: a vision-language agent authors engine-ready 3D assets by calling software APIs and reasoning geometrically, graded on whether the code executes and how closely the resulting shape matches.

imageeditarena.text: A public leaderboard for image-editing models in which people compare two models' edits side by side and vote, with the pairwise battles aggregated into rankings across 16 categories of single-image and multi-image edits.

aime2425.text: Two years of the American Invitational Mathematics Examination, 2024 and 2025, pooled into one set: 15 problems per paper, each answered with an integer from 0 to 999 and marked by exact match.

vlrewardbench.text: 1,250 curated examples for testing vision-language reward models on general multimodal queries, visual hallucination and complex reasoning, with preferences produced by an AI-assisted selection pipeline and then verified by humans.

facts.text: Google's grounding benchmark, in which a user request is paired with a document of up to 32,000 tokens; a response is first discarded if it fails to address the request, then judged by an ensemble of automated judges on whether it is fully grounded in that document.

mmsearch.text: 300 manually collected multimodal search queries across 14 subject areas, none answerable from training data, used to test a model as a search engine over four tasks: requery, rerank, summarisation and an end-to-end run.

tiifbench.text: 5,000 text-to-image prompts spanning several dimensions at three complexity levels, each written in a short and a long form with identical meaning, plus 100 designer-level prompts, with vision-language models acting as binary judges of instruction following.

firefox147.text: An exploit-development eval: starting from vulnerabilities already found in Mozilla's Firefox 147 JavaScript engine, the model must turn each one into a working JavaScript shell exploit, with partial credit for reaching register control.

ossfuzz.text: Models are run against roughly a thousand open source repositories from the OSS-Fuzz corpus, across about 7,000 entry points, and the worst crash each one produces is graded on a five-tier ladder running from a plain crash up to full control-flow hijack.

chid.text: A large-scale Chinese cloze test in which idioms are blanked out of passages and the model must choose the correct four-character idiom from a set of deliberately designed candidates.

icpcwf25.text: The twelve problems (A through L) set at the 2025 ICPC World Finals, a five-hour international collegiate team programming contest, with submissions graded automatically by the Kattis online judge.

amc202223.text: 250 problems from the 2022 and 2023 American Mathematics Competitions: 100 from AMC 12, 100 from AMC 10 and 50 from AMC 8, posed as multiple choice.

bchejava.text: The Java split of HumanEval as converted by Google's BabelCode, a framework that translates benchmarks such as HumanEval and MBPP into other programming languages and compiles and runs candidate solutions against language-specific tests inside a container.

chexpert.text: 224,316 chest radiographs from 65,240 patients, labelled for 14 observations by an automated report labeller that also records uncertainty, with models predicting the probability of each observation from frontal and lateral views.

dermmcqa.text: An internal Google dermatology set of one skin image per patient from 1,996 patients covering 136 conditions, turned into four-option multiple choice questions with random distractors and dermatologist-assigned ground truth.

geckonum.text: Prompts that probe numerical reasoning in text-to-image models, covering exact and approximate object counts, linguistic quantifiers, the concept of zero and fractional quantities, paired with human annotations of the generated images.

medvidqa.text: 3,010 annotated medical questions over 899 instructional videos, where a system must locate the start and end timestamps of the video segment that answers the question.

mtebcode1.text: The code track of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: twelve code retrieval tasks spanning more than 14 programming languages, including code search, code editing, text-to-SQL and StackOverflow question answering.

perceptiontestmcqa.text: The multiple-choice video question answering task of the Perception Test, built on 11.6k filmed real-world videos averaging 23 seconds and probing memory, abstraction, physics and semantics through descriptive, explanatory, predictive and counterfactual questions.

scenetextvqa.text: Visual question answering in which the answer can only be produced by reading text that appears in the scene, across a series of tasks of increasing difficulty, with a metric that accounts for both reasoning and text-recognition errors.

widgetcap.text: Generating a natural-language description of a single mobile UI element from the screen image and the interface's structural representation, using 162,859 human-written phrases over 61,285 elements drawn from 21,750 unique app screens.

ade20k.text: A scene parsing dataset whose images carry dense annotations of stuff regions, whole objects, object parts and in some cases parts of parts, used to test pixel-level segmentation of diverse scenes.

cityscapes.text: Stereo video of urban street scenes recorded in 50 cities, with 5,000 finely annotated frames plus 20,000 coarsely annotated ones, used for pixel-level and instance-level semantic labelling.

fortress.text: 500 expert-written adversarial prompts spanning CBRNE, political violence and terrorism, and criminal or financial illicit activity, each paired with a benign counterpart and a rubric of four to seven binary questions so risk and over-refusal are graded automatically.

jester.text: Short video clips of people performing hand gestures in front of a camera, recorded by more than 1,300 crowdsourced actors in their own unconstrained environments, posed as a gesture classification task.

plmrcap.text: The region captioning task of Meta's PLM-VideoBench: given a video, a mask tracking one subject and a time interval, the model describes the event that subject performs, over 10,060 human-annotated instances graded by an LLM judge.

somethingsomething2.text: More than 100,000 short videos of people performing everyday physical actions on objects, labelled with 174 caption-template classes, designed to test intuitive physics and common sense rather than object or scene recognition.

zeroscrolls.text: Ten long-text understanding datasets with only test and small validation splits, six adapted from SCROLLS and four new, including information-fusing tasks such as aggregating the share of positive reviews.

commitpack.text: A code retrieval task built from real GitHub commits: given a commit message, the system must retrieve the files that the commit modified.

mmluspeech.text: A speech-synthesized version of MMLU: questions that can be spoken naturally are kept or rewritten into speech-friendly wording, then rendered to audio by a TTS engine with randomly sampled speaker voices, and the model answers in text.

deepresearchbench.text: An in-house Moonshot evaluation of deep-research-style queries curated by domain experts, with model answers graded against expert-aligned rubrics.

windowsagentarena.text: More than 150 tasks carried out inside a real Windows operating system, where an agent uses the same applications, tools and web browsers a person would, requiring planning, screen understanding and tool use.

apusgovernment.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement exam in United States Government and Politics: 55 multiple-choice questions plus four free-response questions covering concept application, quantitative analysis, a Supreme Court case comparison and an evidence-based argument essay.

grayswanipiarena.text: A public red-teaming competition in which participants hide malicious instructions in emails, webpages and documents to hijack tool-use, coding and computer-use agents across 41 scenarios; an attack counts only if the agent both performs the harmful action and conceals it from the user.

aishell2test.text: The held-out evaluation split of AISHELL-2, a 1,000-hour Mandarin read-speech corpus, with development and test recordings captured on Android phones and a microphone as well as on iOS, so recognition error can be compared across channels.

ego3d.text: Over 8,600 human-annotated question-answer pairs about ego-centric, multi-view outdoor scenes of the kind a robot or self-driving car sees, split between multiple-choice spatial reasoning and absolute distance estimation.

fleursxx2zh.text: The into-Chinese direction of FLEURS speech translation: spoken utterances in each of the other covered languages must be translated into Chinese text, scored with BLEU.

korbench.text: Rule-driven reasoning questions in five categories (operation, logic, cipher, puzzle and counterfactual), written so that answering depends on applying a newly supplied rule description rather than on domain knowledge.

math401.text: 401 arithmetic expressions (one Euler equation plus 16 groups of 25 problems) covering integer and decimal arithmetic, exponentiation, bracketed expressions, trigonometric functions, logarithms and constants such as pi and e.

mmbenchvideo.text: Long-form, multi-shot YouTube videos paired with free-form human-written questions organised by an ability taxonomy, with answers graded automatically by GPT-4 instead of by multiple choice.

ocrbench2enzh.text: A bilingual English and Chinese successor to OCRBench with 10,000 human-verified question-answer pairs across 31 scenarios, covering text spotting and localisation, handwriting, layout parsing and reasoning about visual text.

phyx.text: 3,000 curated multimodal physics questions over six domains (thermodynamics, electromagnetism, mechanics, modern physics, optics, and waves and acoustics), spanning 25 sub-domains and six reasoning types.

robotwinhard.text: The hard difficulty setting of RoboTwin 2.0's simulated dual-arm manipulation tasks, in which scenes add strong randomisation of clutter, background texture, lighting and tabletop height rather than the clean scenes of the easy setting.

songeval.text: More than 2,399 full-length English and Chinese songs, over 140 hours across nine genres, rated by 16 professional annotators on five aesthetic dimensions: coherence, memorability, naturalness of vocal breathing and phrasing, structural clarity and musicality.

tirbench.text: 13 tasks that can only be solved by operating on the image during reasoning, using tools such as zooming, rotating, raising contrast, drawing auxiliary lines, or segmenting and reassembling jigsaw pieces.

visulogic.text: 1,000 human-verified multiple-choice problems in six categories, including quantitative shifts, spatial relations and attribute comparison, written so the answer cannot be reached by first translating the image into words.

worldmodelbench.text: Video generation models are judged as world models on instruction following and on physics violations such as object size changing in ways that break conservation of mass, using 67,000 crowdsourced labels and a fine-tuned automatic judge.

kmmlupro.text: A Korean professional-knowledge benchmark built from Korean National Professional Licensure exams, meant to test how well models handle the specialist knowledge used in Korean industry.

ami.text: 100 hours of multi-modal meeting recordings captured with close-talking and far-field microphones plus cameras, roughly two thirds of them scripted design-team scenarios, with orthographic transcription serving as the speech recognition reference.

mmaupro.text: 5,305 instances pairing one or more audio clips with expert-written questions over speech, non-speech sound and music, testing 49 skills including long-form listening, spatial audio and reasoning across several clips, in multiple-choice and open-ended form.

flamereacteval.text: 80 manually written front-end tasks, each pairing a UI screenshot with a layout description, functional requirements and a reference React component, used to test generation of React code from a design mockup.

topicstorycloze.text: A spoken variant of StoryCloze in which five-sentence stories are synthesized by a single-speaker TTS system and the wrong ending is drawn at random from elsewhere in the dataset, so the model is tested on coarse topical coherence of the continuation.

imoproofbench.text: Sixty olympiad problems, 30 basic and 30 advanced, across algebra, combinatorics, geometry and number theory, each answered with a full written proof that is graded against detailed problem-specific guidelines by an LLM autograder.

ocw.text: 272 undergraduate STEM problems harvested from MIT OpenCourseWare, covering areas such as solid-state chemistry, differential equations and special relativity, each rewritten to be self-contained with a numeric or symbolic answer that can be checked automatically.

anlir1.text: Annotators wrote hypotheses about short Wikipedia passages chosen to fool a BERT-Large model trained on SNLI and MNLI, forming the first of three adversarial rounds; each premise and hypothesis pair is labelled entailment, neutral or contradiction.

bchejavascript.text: HumanEval's Python programming problems translated into JavaScript by the BabelCode framework, which re-expresses a benchmark's prompts and unit tests in a target language so the generated code can be executed and checked.

cholec80cvs.text: Annotations by skilled surgeons of Strasberg's Critical View of Safety criteria across all 80 laparoscopic cholecystectomy videos in the Cholec80 corpus, for training and testing automatic recognition of when that view has been achieved.

diversevul.text: 18,945 vulnerable and 330,492 non-vulnerable source functions pulled from vulnerability-fixing commits found by crawling security issue trackers, spanning 150 CWE types, for training and testing vulnerability detectors.

geckorel.text: A prompt and image alignment set from the Gecko text-to-image benchmark, restricted to prompts whose human ratings had high inter-annotator agreement, with per-category breakdowns for colour, counting, spatial relations, shape, scale, action and compositional difficulty.

imoproofbenchadvanced.text: The harder of IMO-ProofBench's two tiers: 30 olympiad problems spanning algebra, combinatorics, geometry and number theory, answered with a full written proof that an LLM autograder scores against detailed grading guidelines.

medxpertqa.text: 4,460 expert-level medical exam questions across 17 specialties and 11 body systems, split into a text-only subset and a multimodal subset whose questions carry diverse images and structured clinical information.

mtebmultilingual2.text: A multilingual track of the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, drawn from MMTEB's community-curated pool of over 500 quality-controlled tasks in more than 250 languages, covering retrieval, classification, clustering and reranking.

scicap.text: More than two million figures extracted from computer science arXiv papers published between 2010 and 2020, paired with their author-written captions, so a model can be asked to caption a scientific figure.

cocoo.text: A COCO-derived object detection test set built from six kinds of natural distribution shift, used to check whether a detector's gains on the COCO test set survive out-of-distribution imagery.

gdmstealth.text: Four tasks from Google DeepMind's stealth evaluations, testing whether a model can reason about and circumvent oversight: spotting low-oversight opportunities and evading monitoring, and taking subversive actions without being noticed.

kinetics400.text: 400 human action classes with at least 400 ten-second YouTube clips each, covering human-object interactions such as playing instruments and human-human interactions such as shaking hands, used for video action recognition.

multilingualmmmlu.text: MMLU's multiple-choice questions machine-translated into German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish and Thai, with task instructions left in English and answers scored five-shot.

plmrdcap.text: The region dense captioning task of PLM-VideoBench: given a video and a region masklet, the model must emit a sequence of start, end and caption tuples covering the whole clip, including stretches when the subject is off screen, judged by an LLM.

squad.text: Over 100,000 questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a span of text taken from the corresponding reading passage.

zerowastef.text: The fully annotated split of ZeroWaste, 4,503 frames from an industrial waste-recycling line labelled for detecting and segmenting highly deformable and often translucent objects in extreme clutter.

mozillacommonvoice151.text: Volunteer-read sentences gathered and checked by crowdsourcing through Mozilla's web platform, published as versioned multilingual releases and used here as a speech recognition test set.

faithjudge.text: Hallucination testing over three retrieval-augmented tasks, summarisation, question answering and data-to-text writing, in which an LLM judge is first shown human-annotated hallucination spans for the same source before ruling on the model's output.

loogle.text: Long-document question answering over post-2022 documents of more than 24,000 tokens each, with roughly 6,000 questions split between short-dependency tasks and over 1,100 hand-written questions that need information gathered across the document.

apushistory.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement exam in United States history: 55 source-based multiple-choice questions, three short-answer questions, a document-based essay built on seven documents, and a long essay.

codeforcesrating.text: Timed competitive programming contests on Codeforces, with performance reported on the site's Elo-style rating scale, which converts a contestant's finishing place relative to the field into a rating.

hackerrankastra.text: 65 multi-file project problems in stacks such as Node.js, React, Angular, Django and Java Spring Boot, averaging about 12 source and configuration files per question with around seven test cases each, and repeated over many runs to measure consistency.

satevidencebasedreadingwriting.text: The reading and writing section of the SAT: short passages of 25 to 150 words drawn from literature, history and social studies, the humanities and science, each followed by one multiple-choice question on comprehension, rhetoric, revision or standard English conventions.

tau3voicetelecom.text: The telecom domain of tau-cubed-bench run as an end-to-end full-duplex voice conversation: the agent must follow the domain's written policy and use its tools to resolve a simulated customer's problem while listening and speaking at once.

aishell4.text: 120 hours of real Mandarin meetings, 211 sessions with four to eight speakers each, recorded on an eight-channel circular microphone array for speech enhancement, separation, recognition and speaker diarisation.

chineseword.text: A character-level test of Chinese text rendering in image generation: prompt templates ask a text-to-image model to produce an image containing a single Chinese character, over three difficulty tiers from the official list of common standard characters (3,500, 3,000 and 1,605 characters).

c15en.text: The English portion of version 15 of Mozilla's crowdsourced Common Voice corpus, built from sentences read aloud by volunteers and validated by other volunteers, used as a speech recognition test set.

harmb.text: A standardised red-teaming framework organised around a fixed set of harmful behaviours, with a classifier that judges whether a response actually carried the behaviour out, used to compare attack methods and refusal robustness.

lcb5.text: Release v5 of LiveCodeBench: 880 competitive programming problems published between May 2023 and January 2025, collected continuously so that problems postdate model training, and checked against the problems' own test cases.

maxife.text: 1,667 verifiable instruction-following tasks in 23 languages, covering both multilingual prompts and cross-lingual ones where the instruction and the response language differ, graded by a mix of programmatic rule checks and model-based judging.

mmeb2.text: An extension of the Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark adding five task types to its image tasks: visual document retrieval, video retrieval, temporal grounding, video classification and video question answering, all scored with one embedding model.

ocrbench2zh.text: The Chinese half of OCRBench v2, a bilingual text-centric benchmark of 10,000 human-verified question and answer pairs over 31 scenarios such as street scenes, receipts, formulas and diagrams, covering recognition, text localisation, layout parsing and reasoning.

pickscore.text: A CLIP-based scoring function trained on Pick-a-Pic, an open dataset of real users' pairwise preferences between generated images, used as an automatic stand-in for human judgement of text-to-image output.

robotwinxe.text: A zero-shot cross-embodiment test built on RoboTwin: a policy fine-tuned only on AgileX demonstrations is run on the same tasks with the robot swapped for ARX-X5, UR5-WSG or Franka Panda, holding camera placement, scenes, layouts and seeds fixed.

songformbenchcn.text: The 100 Chinese pop songs in SongFormBench, an expert-verified music structure set where a model must place section boundaries and label each section, scored by boundary hit rate at 0.5 and 3 second tolerances and by functional label accuracy.

toefl.text: The TOEFL subtask of L-Eval: the 15 longest lectures assembled from TOEFL Practice Online listening material, each followed by multiple-choice comprehension questions, used as a closed-ended long-context reading test.

vitabench.text: 100 cross-scenario and 300 single-scenario agent tasks derived from real user requests in food delivery, in-store consumption and travel services, sharing 66 tools with no domain-specific policy, and judged by a rubric-based sliding window evaluator.

wsyueshortlong.text: The short (0 to 10 seconds) and long (10 to 30 seconds) subsets of WSYue-ASR-eval, 11.4 hours of Cantonese speech with multi-round manual transcripts covering code-switching and several domains.

koaime24.text: Korean translations of the official AIME 2024 competition problems, built in-house by Upstage to measure mathematical reasoning in Korean alongside its other Korean benchmarks.

aaspeechtospeechqualityindex.text: An equally weighted composite of three speech-to-speech evaluations: Big Bench Audio for spoken reasoning, a Full Duplex Bench subset for conversational dynamics, and tau-Voice for agentic customer service tasks.

ivebench.text: 600 source videos of 32 to 1,024 frames spanning seven semantic dimensions, paired with editing instructions in 8 task categories and 35 subcategories, scored on video quality, instruction compliance and fidelity to the source.

arenahardcreativewriting.text: The creative writing category of Arena-Hard v2: 250 open-ended writing prompts taken from real Chatbot Arena traffic, with answers compared pairwise by frontier-model judges under style control.

mmbrowsercomp.text: 224 hand-crafted browsing questions that often embed images in the prompt and whose evidence is frequently locked inside images or videos on the pages an agent must find, with a verified checklist per question.

websrc.text: 400,000 question and answer pairs collected from 6,400 web pages, where answering needs the page's structure as well as its text; each answer is a span on the page or yes/no, and HTML, screenshots and metadata are supplied.

flamevlmcode.text: The Flame project's React code generation evaluation: given a UI design mockup, a model must write a React component, scored for syntactic precision, functional correctness and visual consistency by rendering the result and comparing screenshots.

naturalcodebench.text: 402 Python and Java problems selected from natural user queries sent to online coding services, spanning six domains and checked against test cases built with a semi-automated construction pipeline.

treebench.text: 405 visual question and answer pairs over dense-object images sampled from SA-1B and annotated by multimodal experts, requiring a model to spot subtle targets, cite bounding boxes as evidence, and reason about object interactions and spatial hierarchy.

chineseqa.text: An in-house Chinese question answering set built by DeepSeek and modelled on TriviaQA, reported beside C-Eval and CMMLU as a check on Chinese factual knowledge.

instructionfollowingevaluation.text: Google's IFEval set: around 500 prompts, each carrying one or more of 25 verifiable instruction types, so compliance can be checked programmatically instead of judged.

pile.text: An 825 GiB English corpus built from 22 sources including books, GitHub, PubMed and arXiv; held-out splits serve as a language modelling test scored in bits per byte.

anlir2.text: Round two of Adversarial NLI: premise and hypothesis pairs written by annotators trying to fool a RoBERTa ensemble trained on SNLI, MultiNLI, FEVER and round one, with each kept example checked by separate verifiers.

bchekotlin.text: HumanEval's Python problems and their unit tests transpiled into Kotlin by the BabelCode framework, so the same tasks can be run in a non-Python language.

civilcomments.text: Roughly two million public comments from the Civil Comments platform rated for toxicity by crowd workers, with a subset further labelled for mentions of gender, religion and race so subgroup bias can be measured.

docci.text: 15,000 photographs taken and curated by a single researcher, each paired with a long human-written English description, around 136 words, crafted to distinguish it from visually similar images.

genaibench.text: 1,600 prompts collected from professional designers who use text-to-visual tools, tagged by compositional skill such as counting, negation, comparison and spatial or action relations, with human ratings of the generated images.

indicgenbench.text: A generation suite covering 29 Indic languages across 13 scripts and 4 families, extending CrossSum, FLORES, XQuAD and XorQA with human translations for summarisation, translation and cross-lingual question answering.

mendeleyclinicallaboratorytestreports.text: 260 laboratory test reports from 24 Egyptian labs, supplied as PDF renders plus scanner and phone captures, used to test extraction of structured results from document images.

mtob.text: Translating between English and Kalamang, a language with under 200 speakers and almost no web presence, from a single field grammar book plus a 2,000-entry wordlist and a few hundred parallel sentences placed in context.

physicsfinals.text: An unreleased Google set of 61 undergraduate physics problems written by professors for offline final exams, spanning wave and quantum mechanics, special relativity and introductory general relativity, graded by a physicist.

screen2words.text: Summarising the purpose of an Android app screen in a single coherent phrase, over 22,417 unique screens drawn from Rico with 112,085 human-written summaries.

wikilingua.text: Around 770,000 article and summary pairs scraped from WikiHow in 18 languages, aligned across languages by matching the images used for each how-to step, for cross-lingual abstractive summarisation.

agenticcybermisuse.text: An internal Meta prompt set simulating malicious multi-step cyber workflows in which the model has shell and Python access; what is measured is how often it complies rather than refuses.

gorillaapibench.text: Over 11,000 instruction and API-call pairs covering TorchHub, TensorFlow Hub and HuggingFace model APIs; a generated call is checked by matching its abstract syntax tree against the reference.

lccbalanced.text: A resampled version of the Long Code Completion set used in the Code Llama paper, with examples spread evenly over context-length buckets so single-line completion is not dominated by short files.

navi.text: About 29,000 casually captured images of 36 objects, each aligned to a high-quality 3D scan so camera pose, dense pixel correspondences and depth are known almost exactly.

plmrtloc.text: The region temporal localisation task of PLM-VideoBench: given a video, a region masklet and a text description of an event, return its start and end frames, scored by mean recall at one over several IoU thresholds.

squality.text: Question-focused summaries of public-domain Project Gutenberg short stories of 4,000 to 6,000 words; every story carries five questions and four independently written reference summaries per question.

aegis2.text: Around 33,000 annotated human and LLM interactions labelled against a taxonomy of 12 core and 9 fine-grained safety violation categories, built for training and testing prompt and response moderation guardrails.

financebench.text: An in-house Moonshot evaluation of realistic financial work, requiring a model to carry a complete workflow end to end from source materials through to a reviewable deliverable.

mbppsanitized.text: The hand-verified split of Mostly Basic Python Problems: 427 crowd-sourced tasks whose natural-language descriptions were re-annotated for clarity, each with a reference solution and three test cases.

zerobenchmain.text: The 100 hand-crafted main questions of ZeroBench, multi-step visual reasoning problems with a deliberately wide answer space so guessing does not help; its 334 intermediate subquestions are scored separately.

apworldhistory.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement exam in modern world history, covering 1200 to the present: 55 multiple-choice questions on texts, images, charts and maps, three short-answer questions, a document-based essay and a long essay.

satmath.text: The mathematics half of the College Board SAT, two adaptive modules of multiple-choice and student-produced-response questions across algebra, advanced math, problem solving and data analysis, and geometry and trigonometry.

taubankingvoice.text: The banking domain of the τ³-bench agent suite, a knowledge-retrieval customer service setting where a tool-using agent handles a simulated customer, run end to end over speech so interruptions and latency count.

aitz.text: 18,643 Android screen and action pairs annotated with chain-of-action-thought, tying what is visible on screen to the reasoning behind the next action and the outcome it produces.

c15zh.text: The Mandarin Chinese portion of Mozilla Common Voice 15, a crowdsourced corpus in which volunteers read donated sentences aloud and other contributors vote each clip valid or invalid, used here for speech recognition.

ego3drmse.text: Over 8,600 human-checked question and answer pairs built from ego-centric multi-view outdoor driving footage taken from nuScenes, Argoverse and Waymo, covering absolute and relative distance, localisation, motion reasoning and travel time.

fleurszh.text: The Mandarin Chinese split of FLEURS, an n-way parallel read-speech corpus in 102 languages recorded from FLoRes-101 sentences with roughly 12 hours of speech per language, used here for speech recognition.

hipho.text: 13 physics olympiad exams from 2024 and 2025, international and regional, mixing text-only problems with ones that hinge on illustration, variable or data figures, graded at answer and step level against the official marking schemes.

leval.text: 20 subtasks over 508 long documents with more than 2,000 human-labelled query and response pairs, from 3k to 200k tokens, split into closed-ended comprehension tasks and open-ended summarisation judged by a model.

mmevideoocr.text: 1,464 videos paired with 2,000 hand-annotated questions across 10 categories and 25 tasks, testing whether a model can read and reason over text that appears in video despite motion blur, scene changes and visual effects.

odinw.text: 35 real-world object detection datasets gathered from Roboflow into one transfer suite within ELEVATER, evaluated zero-shot, few-shot and full-shot; a 13-dataset version introduced with GLIP is also widely reported.

plawbench.text: 850 questions across 13 practical legal scenarios covering public legal consultation, case analysis and document drafting, each with expert-written rubrics, about 12,500 rubric items in total, applied by a model judge.

rtc2r.text: RoboTwin Clean2Rand: a dual-arm manipulation policy is fine-tuned on the clean RoboTwin split, then tested under randomised background, lighting, clutter and table height in easy and hard settings.

songformbenchharmonixset.text: The HarmonixSet half of SongFormBench, 200 expert-revised pop songs for music structure analysis: split a track into intro, verse, chorus and similar sections, scored by boundary hit rate at 0.5 and 3 second tolerances and frame-level label accuracy.

zerobenchsub.text: The 334 subquestions of ZeroBench, each an intermediate step of one of its 100 main visual reasoning problems, for instance reading a single item price or a tax rate off a cluttered image.

koaime25.text: An in-house Korean translation of the official 2025 American Invitational Mathematics Examination, used by Upstage alongside HRM8K to gauge mathematical reasoning in Korean.

apexswe.text: Software engineering work of two kinds: integration tasks that build end-to-end systems across cloud services, business applications and infrastructure-as-code, and observability tasks that debug production failures from logs and dashboards in Loki, Grafana and Prometheus.

arenahardhardprompt.text: The 500 challenging real-world queries of Arena-Hard v2, drawn from Chatbot Arena and WildChat and covering open-ended software engineering and maths, scored by a model judge; a separate 250-prompt creative writing split is reported apart.

agentbench.text: Eight interactive environments for testing a model as an agent: operating system, database, knowledge graph, digital card game and lateral thinking puzzles, plus household tasks, web shopping and web browsing.

flicker30kcaptioning.text: Caption generation over roughly 31,000 Flickr photographs of everyday scenes, each carrying five crowd-written English descriptions that serve as references.

ncb.text: NaturalCodeBench: 402 Python and Java problems distilled from real user queries to the CodeGeeX online service across six domains, with test inputs that include files and other complex structures, not just plain values.

unimernet.text: UniMER-Test, the evaluation half of the UniMER dataset: 23,789 formula images covering clean printed and handwritten LaTeX as well as screen captures with mixed fonts and background noise, for mathematical expression recognition.

amc8.text: A 25-question, 40-minute multiple-choice mathematics contest for students in grade 8 and below, covering algebra, arithmetic, counting, geometry, logic, number theory and probability, with problems ordered by increasing difficulty.

frontierswe2.text: 34 ultra-long-horizon engineering tasks across system implementation, scientific computing, performance optimisation, visual reasoning and AI research, each giving an agent a 20-hour budget and a full Linux machine, graded 0 to 1 by a deterministic verifier run in a separate container.

realworldfinance.text: An Anthropic internal evaluation spanning roughly 50 investment and financial analysis use cases across spreadsheets, slide decks and document generation and review, scored with a mix of rubrics and preference judgements covering domain knowledge, task completeness, accuracy and presentation.

leetcode.text: 126 programming problems crawled from LeetCode Weekly Contests 351 to 372 and Bi-Weekly Contests 108 to 117 (July to November 2023), each with over 20 test cases; a problem counts as solved only when the generated program passes every test.

proofnettest.text: The held-out test split of ProofNet, which pairs natural-language statements and proofs of undergraduate pure mathematics exercises with formal Lean statements, and is used for both autoformalization and formal theorem proving over analysis, algebra and topology.

aokvqamc.text: The multiple-choice setting of A-OKVQA, a crowdsourced set of about 25,000 image questions that need commonsense and world knowledge rather than a knowledge-base lookup; the model picks one of four supplied options.

bcmbppc.text: The C# portion of BabelCode-MBPP, which converts Google's MBPP Python programming problems into 16 languages along with per-language test code and run commands, so generated solutions are executed against the translated test cases.

coco35l.text: A machine-generated multilingual captioning set built by translating COCO Captions into 34 further languages with Google's translation API, giving parallel image captions in 35 languages.

ecgqa.text: Question answering paired with electrocardiogram recordings, built from 70 question templates validated by an ECG expert, covering single-recording interpretation as well as questions that compare two recordings.

gifteval.text: A time series forecasting benchmark of 23 datasets, over 144,000 series and 177 million observations across seven domains and ten frequencies, with univariate and multivariate inputs, short to long horizons, and a separate non-leaking pretraining corpus for zero-shot evaluation.

internalctfsuite.text: Thirteen easy to medium capture-the-flag challenges built in-house by Google DeepMind so that no solutions sit in training data, covering web application vulnerabilities, off-the-shelf exploits, database navigation and password attacks; the agent works from a Bash shell and must read a flag file.

mimiciii.text: A deidentified critical care database covering over 40,000 patients admitted to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center between 2001 and 2012, holding demographics, vital signs, laboratory results, medications, procedures, caregiver notes, imaging reports and mortality across 26 relational tables.

pointbench.text: The static evaluation component of PointArena: roughly 1,000 language-guided pointing tasks over natural images spanning five reasoning categories, where a model must point at the object a language prompt describes.

winograd.text: Pairs of sentences differing in one or two words and containing an ambiguous pronoun that resolves to the opposite noun in each version, so that choosing the referent is meant to need world knowledge rather than word co-occurrence statistics.

cub.text: A fine-grained visual recognition dataset of 11,788 photographs of 200 bird species, each image annotated with a bounding box, 15 part locations and 312 binary attributes.

hitom.text: Template-generated Sally-Anne style stories in which agents enter rooms, move objects between containers and optionally make public or deceptive private claims, followed by multiple-choice questions probing beliefs from order zero up to fourth-order theory of mind.

lvis1.text: Large-vocabulary instance segmentation with about 2 million high-quality masks for more than 1,000 entry-level object categories across 164,000 images, deliberately long-tailed so many categories have only a handful of examples.

needleinhaystack.text: A long-context sweep that plants a fact at varying depths inside filler text while varying total context length, then checks by exact match whether the model retrieves it; variants scatter several facts or a chain of UUID hops.

ppdls.text: Leaf segmentation images of tobacco and arabidopsis plants from the Plant Phenotyping Datasets, used as one of the 23 zero-shot transfer sets in Segment Anything, where a model must produce an instance mask from a single point prompt.

streets.text: Instance segmentation masks of cars in traffic camera footage, used as one of the 23 zero-shot transfer sets in Segment Anything, where a model must turn a single point prompt into a valid mask.

amiihm.text: The individual headset microphone condition of the AMI meeting corpus, roughly 100 hours of English multi-party meetings recorded in three rooms with differing acoustics, chunked and transcribed for speech recognition and scored by word error rate.

earnings21.text: A 39-hour corpus of earnings calls from nine financial sectors, chosen for entity-dense speech, used to test speech recognition on real-world audio and to break error rates down by named entity category.

polyguard.text: A multilingual safety moderation benchmark covering 17 languages, whose evaluation set of about 29,000 prompt and response pairs is labelled for prompt harmfulness, response harmfulness and whether the response is a refusal.

wikisql.text: 80,654 natural language questions hand-annotated with the SQL query that answers them, over 24,241 tables drawn from Wikipedia; a model must produce the query for an unseen question and table.

generalagentbenchmark.text: Moonshot AI's internal expert productivity evaluation, which measures multi-step, production-grade professional workflows against human expert performance on the same tasks.

abstentionbench.text: 20 datasets of questions a model ought to decline, covering unanswerable, underspecified, false-premise, subjective and stale-information prompts, used to measure whether a model abstains instead of guessing.

attackplanningredteaming.text: An OpenAI red-teaming campaign in which 25 testers from defense, intelligence and law enforcement backgrounds probe a model for help planning violent attacks, then rate anonymized side-by-side responses from two models for which is safer.

firstpersonfairness.text: A counterfactual audit of whether a chatbot treats its own user differently by gender or race, covering 66 tasks in nine domains, with a language model research assistant producing the bias measures and human annotators corroborating them.

healthbenchhard.text: A 1,000-example subset of HealthBench picked because current frontier models struggle on it; each example is a multi-turn health conversation whose final reply is graded by a model against physician-written, conversation-specific rubric criteria.

medicalknowledgeselfassessmentprogram.text: The American College of Physicians' internal medicine board-review resource, whose current edition pairs a 12-section syllabus with roughly 1,200 psychometrically validated multiple-choice questions used for certification and continuing education.

openscorestringquartets.text: A public corpus of 698 string quartet scores by 63 'long 19th century' composers, transcribed by the OpenScore project and distributed in MuseScore's uncompressed score format with per-composer and per-score metadata.

clawevalmultimodal.text: The multimodal split of Claw-Eval: 101 human-verified agent tasks covering perception and creation such as webpage generation, video question answering and document extraction, audited over the full trajectory against rubric items for completion, safety and robustness.

hmeqa.text: 500 multiple-choice embodied question answering episodes across 267 Habitat-Matterport 3D scenes, drafted with GPT-4V and manually filtered, where a robot must explore the house until it has enough evidence to pick an answer.

librispeechcleanother.text: The two read-speech test sets of LibriSpeech, taken from public-domain audiobooks and separated by ranking speakers on the error rate of a reference recogniser, so 'clean' holds the easier half and 'other' the harder; systems are scored by word error rate.

megabench.text: 505 realistic multimodal tasks with more than 8,000 samples from 16 expert annotators, whose answers can be numbers, phrases, code, LaTeX, coordinates, JSON or free text and are checked by over 40 task-specific metrics rather than multiple choice.

mmmuprostd.text: The standard setting of MMMU-Pro: 1,730 college-level multimodal questions supplied as separate text and images, filtered to remove text-only-answerable items and expanded from four to ten answer options so guessing is harder.

omnibench.text: Human-annotated questions that supply an image, an audio clip and text at once and can only be answered by combining all three, used to test simultaneous tri-modal recognition and reasoning.

qwenwebbench.text: Qwen's internal front-end code generation evaluation: bilingual English and Chinese prompts in seven categories (web design, web apps, games, SVG, data visualisation, animation, 3D), auto-rendered and judged by a multimodal grader on code and visual correctness under a Bradley-Terry Elo rating.

spider2.text: 632 real-world text-to-SQL workflow problems over enterprise databases that often exceed 1,000 columns on BigQuery, Snowflake or local systems, usually requiring the model to search database metadata, dialect documentation and project code and to write queries over 100 lines long.

touchstone.text: An open-world visual dialogue set spanning five ability categories and 27 subtasks, from basic recognition through comprehension to visual storytelling, scored by turning each image into a detailed text annotation so a language model can judge the dialogue.

vlnce.text: Language-guided navigation in continuous 3D environments, where the agent follows natural language directions with low-level actions instead of hopping between nodes of a known navigation graph, without oracle teleportation or perfect localisation.

click.text: 1,995 Korean question and answer pairs taken from official Korean exams and textbooks, split into eleven subcategories under language and culture, each annotated with the cultural or linguistic knowledge needed to answer.

kobalt.text: 700 expert-curated Korean multiple-choice questions spanning 24 linguistic phenomena across syntax, semantics, pragmatics, phonetics and phonology, and morphology, written to have minimal n-gram overlap with standard Korean corpora.

berkeleyfunctioncalling4benchmark.text: The fourth version of the Berkeley function-calling evaluation, which adds an agentic block: 100 human-written multihop questions answered with search and URL-fetch tools under injected network failures, a memory read and write section, and a format sensitivity section across languages.

nuinstruct.text: 91,000 multi-view video question and answer pairs for autonomous driving across 17 subtasks, generated automatically by an SQL-based pipeline so each task needs temporal, multi-view and spatial information together.

alfworld.text: Household tasks aligned between a TextWorld text environment and the ALFRED visual simulator, so an agent can plan abstractly in language and then carry out the same goal with low-level actions in the 3D scene.

helmeticl.text: The in-context learning slice of the HELMET long-context benchmark: classification over five large-label-space datasets (TREC coarse and fine, BANKING77, CLINC150 and NLU) with natural labels replaced by numbers, varying how many balanced demonstrations fill the context; scored by accuracy.

omnispatial.text: Over 8,400 manually annotated question and answer pairs grounded in cognitive psychology, organised into dynamic reasoning, complex spatial logic, spatial interaction and perspective taking across 50 fine-grained subcategories.

vcrhard.text: The hard configuration of VCR-wiki, a 5,000-instance test set in which a Wikipedia image caption is crossed out in the upper part of the image, leaving less visible context than the easy setting, and the model must restore the obscured text.

arxivmath.text: Research-level mathematics with short checkable answers, released in monthly sets of about 40 problems extracted from arXiv papers posted in the preceding month and filtered by automated checks and human review for self-containment and non-triviality.

realworldfinance1.text: An internal Anthropic eval covering about 50 investment and financial analysis use cases across spreadsheets, slide decks and documents, run with code execution and tool use harnesses and graded by rubrics and preferences for domain knowledge, completeness and presentation.

cmrc.text: Span-extraction reading comprehension in Chinese: questions written over Wikipedia passages where the answer must be returned as an exact span of the passage, distributed in SQuAD-style format.
