leetcodecontest.text: 180 problems collected from LeetCode contests held between July 2023 and January 2024, spread across easy, medium and hard difficulty, with 100 hidden test cases per problem that a generated solution must pass.

proverbench.text: 325 mathematical statements formalized in Lean 4, including 15 drawn from recent AIME competitions alongside textbook and tutorial material, spanning competition and undergraduate-level mathematics.

arcade.text: 1,082 natural language to code problems over pandas in Jupyter data science notebooks, where each request comes with the preceding notebook cells and their execution state, and several rounds are drawn from the same notebook.

bcmbppgo.text: The Go split of BabelCode-MBPP, which converts the MBPP Python programming problems into 16 languages with per-language test code and execution commands, so generated Go is scored by running the translated tests.

egdcxr.text: 1,083 chest radiographs from MIMIC-CXR paired with a radiologist's transcribed report, dictation audio and eye-tracking data recorded while they read the image, covering normal, pneumonia and congestive heart failure cases.

globalmmlulite.text: A compact subset of Global MMLU, the human-translated and post-edited multilingual version of MMLU, balancing questions annotated as culturally sensitive against culturally agnostic ones so many languages can be evaluated cheaply.

mindcube.text: 21,154 questions over 3,268 images testing whether a vision language model can build a spatial mental model from limited views: representing object positions, taking other viewpoints, and simulating hypothetical movement.

multimedbench.text: An open benchmark of 14 biomedical tasks spanning clinical language, medical imaging and genomics, including medical question answering, mammography and dermatology interpretation, radiology report generation and summarization, and genomic variant calling.

precisionfdatruthchallenge2.text: A genomics challenge in which teams submit variant callsets for the Genome in a Bottle Ashkenazi trio from Illumina, PacBio HiFi and Oxford Nanopore reads, scored against GIAB truth sets with stratifications for difficult-to-map regions and the MHC.

selfproliferationearlywarning.text: Agentic tasks approximating autonomous setup and operation online, such as installing a model on a cloud server, acquiring resources and self-improvement, each split into three to seven milestones so partial progress registers before any end-to-end success.

wmt21.text: The news translation shared task of the Sixth Conference on Machine Translation, with full-document test sets of 2020 news across pairs such as English to and from Chinese, Czech, German, Hausa, Icelandic, Japanese and Russian, scored by BLEU, chrF and human evaluation.

amstertime.text: 2,500 curated image pairs matching present-day street-level photographs of Amsterdam, crowdsourced through Mapillary, to archival photographs of the same place, posing verification and retrieval under a severe shift in camera, viewpoint and appearance.

cute.text: Character-level tasks built from synthetically generated text, covering spelling, inverse spelling, character containment, orthographic similarity and insertion, deletion, substitution and swapping, to test whether a model can manipulate the characters inside its own tokens.

hlecalibration.text: Calibration on Humanity's Last Exam: the model states a confidence alongside each answer, and the gap between that stated confidence and whether the answer was actually right is reported as calibration error.

lvos.text: 220 densely annotated videos totalling 421 minutes, averaging about a minute and a half each, where targets disappear, reappear and are confused with similar objects, so pixel-level masks must be propagated over long horizons.

nexus.text: Nine function-calling task sets built on real-world APIs such as VirusTotal, the NVD library and a places API, grouped by whether a request needs a single call, several parallel calls, or nested calls where one call's output feeds another.

qasper.text: 5,049 information-seeking questions over 1,585 NLP papers, written by practitioners who saw only the title and abstract and answered by a different set of practitioners from the full text, who also mark the supporting paragraphs.

amisdm.text: Transcription of the AMI meeting corpus, 100 hours of mostly scenario-driven English meetings with many non-native speakers, taken from the distant room microphone track rather than the individual headset track.

earnings22.text: 125 recordings totalling about 119 hours of English-language earnings calls from companies around the world, organised by country of origin, for measuring speech recognition on accented real-world audio.

humanevaljavascript.text: HumanEval's hand-written Python function-completion problems ported to JavaScript, with prompts, signatures and unit tests translated automatically, and generated code scored by running the translated tests.

qwen3guardtest.text: 2,441 items for testing safety guard models in two settings other guardrail sets skip: classifying the safety of a reasoning model's full thinking trace, and streaming moderation where annotators mark the first sentence that turns unsafe.

wildbench.text: 1,024 tasks selected from over a million real human-chatbot conversation logs, graded by a language model against task-specific checklists, both as pairwise comparisons and as individual scores.

gsm8kplatinum.text: A cleaned 1,209-question version of the GSM8K test set of grade-school math word problems, where every example a frontier model missed was reviewed by hand, wrong labels corrected and ambiguous questions dropped.

mirabench.text: Multimodal questions that can only be worked out by drawing or imagining an intermediate picture, built from 546 input images and 936 hand-constructed intermediate images across 20 reasoning task types, in single-step and multi-step settings.

automatedevaluationforriskyadvice.text: Conversations gathered in a targeted red teaming campaign on risky advice, such as attack planning, converted into an automated grader in the style of OpenAI's disallowed content evaluations and scored on whether a response is unsafe.

collegiatectfs.text: The collegiate tier of a curated capture-the-flag set covering web exploitation, reverse engineering, binary and network exploitation, cryptography and miscellaneous challenges, attempted in a headless Kali Linux environment with iterative debugging and tool use.

healthbenchhardhallucinations.text: The intersection of HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Consensus, difficult health conversations each validated by two or more physicians, used to measure whether a model asserts things that are not true.

medmcqadev.text: The development split of MedMCQA, multiple-choice questions taken from the Indian AIIMS and NEET PG medical entrance exams, covering 21 subjects and roughly 2,400 healthcare topics.

opqa.text: OpenAI-Proof Q&A: 20 internal research and engineering bottlenecks that each took an OpenAI team more than a day to resolve, where the model gets a container with the code and run artifacts and must diagnose and explain the issue.

standarddisallowedcontentevaluation.text: OpenAI's long-standing refusal set, covering hate, sexual content and content involving minors, illicit violent and non-violent advice, personal data and self-harm, graded by a model on whether the response was unsafe.

uhuraeval.text: About 1,200 reading comprehension and true or false questions in six African languages: Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili, Yoruba and Zulu.

clotho.text: 4,981 audio clips of 15 to 30 seconds taken from Freesound, each with five crowdsourced captions of 8 to 20 words, for audio captioning: describing general sound events rather than transcribing speech.

hmmt25feb.text: The 30 problems from the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, covering algebra, number theory, combinatorics and geometry, each paired with a single gold answer that can be checked automatically.

livebench0831.text: The 31 August 2024 release of LiveBench, whose questions are refreshed monthly from recent competitions, arXiv papers, news and datasets across math, coding, reasoning, language, data analysis and instruction following, all graded automatically against ground truth.

multiswebenchmini.text: A 400-instance lightweight version of Multi-SWE-bench covering eight programming languages, built to cut the compute needed to run the full multilingual issue-resolving benchmark.

omnicapif.text: Instruction following for omni-modal video captioning: models caption video with audio while obeying structural, stylistic, temporal, visual, audio and audio-visual constraints, graded by a language model against fine-grained checklists.

spotsoundbench.text: 387 needle-in-a-haystack audio grounding items, where a short acoustic event averaging about four seconds must be located by timestamp inside a noisy recording averaging around 54 seconds.

voicebenchcommoneval.text: The open-ended question answering split of VoiceBench: 200 human-recorded spoken prompts that a voice assistant must answer, with the replies graded by GPT-4o-mini.

nuscenesqa.text: Visual question answering for autonomous driving: about 460,000 template-generated question-answer pairs over 34,000 nuScenes street scenes, answered from multi-view camera images and LiDAR point clouds.

allanglesbench.text: Over 2,100 hand-annotated multi-view question-answer pairs across 90 real scenes, covering counting, attribute identification, relative distance and direction, object manipulation and camera pose, testing whether one consistent reading is kept across views.

hotpotqa.text: 113,000 Wikipedia-based questions that need facts combined from more than one document, including comparison questions, with sentence-level supporting facts annotated so systems can be judged on their evidence as well as their answer.

gre.text: A graduate-admissions test with three measures: verbal reasoning over written discourse, quantitative reasoning covering arithmetic, algebra, geometry and data analysis, and analytical writing on argument-based essay prompts.

bcmbppjava.text: 855 MBPP Python problems whose signatures and unit tests the BabelCode framework machine-translates into 14 languages including Java, with generated code checked by executing the translated tests.

egotempo.text: Question answering over egocentric video, built so that items cannot be answered from a few frames or from commonsense alone and instead require integrating information across the entire clip.

grandstaff.text: 53,882 rendered images of single-system pianoform sheet music paired with Humdrum text transcriptions, used for end-to-end optical music recognition of two-staff piano notation.

multimedqa1066.text: A set of 1,066 consumer medical questions on which long-form model answers and physician answers are compared head to head by physician raters along nine axes of clinical utility.

primevul.text: A function-level vulnerability detection dataset whose labels come from techniques validated against human-verified benchmarks, with rigorous de-duplication and a chronological train/test split to limit data leakage.

sgprompt.text: ShieldGemma's held-out test set of synthetically generated, adversarially seeded user prompts, each labeled benign or violating for hate speech, dangerous content, sexual content or harassment, for safety classifiers to predict.

totaltext.text: 1,555 natural scene photographs annotated for text detection and recognition, deliberately including curved text alongside horizontal and multi-oriented text that earlier scene-text datasets almost entirely lacked.

wmt23.text: The 2023 Conference on Machine Translation's general translation task, with multi-domain test sets (news, social, conversational, e-commerce) across pairs such as Chinese, German, Japanese and Ukrainian with English, ranked by human judgement in context.

apibank.text: A runnable tool-use evaluation built around 73 API tools and 314 annotated dialogues containing 753 API calls, testing whether a model can plan, retrieve and correctly invoke APIs mid-conversation.

cvss.text: Sentence-level speech-to-speech translation pairs from 21 languages into English, derived from Common Voice and CoVoST 2, released both in one canonical synthetic voice and in voices transferred from the source speaker.

how2qa.text: Video question answering over clips from HowTo100M instructional YouTube videos, introduced alongside the HERO video-and-language model and scored by answer accuracy.

lvos2.text: The second release of a long-term video object segmentation benchmark, expanded to 720 videos with dense pixel-level masks, where an object must be tracked and segmented through long sequences in which it can disappear and reappear.

reasonseg.text: 1,218 image, instruction and mask triples drawn from OpenImages and ScanNetv2, where a model must return a binary segmentation mask for an implicit query rather than a direct object name.

arabicalghafa.text: An Arabic multiple-choice evaluation suite of eleven tasks, spanning Modern Standard and dialectal reading comprehension, exam questions, sentiment rating and translated commonsense sets, for zero- and few-shot testing.

humanevalphp.text: The PHP split of MultiPL-E: 161 HumanEval problems whose Python signatures, docstrings and unit tests are compiled into PHP, with generated code graded by running the translated tests.

r2rce.text: Room-to-Room navigation instructions ported into continuous 3D Matterport3D scenes, where an agent follows a written route using low-level forward, turn and look actions instead of hopping between graph nodes, scored by success rate and SPL.

wildbench2.text: 1,024 challenging tasks selected from real user chat logs in WildChat, with responses graded by an LLM judge against task-specific checklists, either scored on their own or compared pairwise against a baseline model.

helmet.text: A long-context evaluation spanning seven application categories including retrieval-augmented generation, long-document QA, passage re-ranking, citation, summarization and in-context learning, at controllable lengths up to 128K tokens with model-based scoring.

mlvumcq.text: The multiple-choice half of MLVU, covering videos from three minutes to two hours across movies, surveillance, egocentric and game footage, with tasks grouped into holistic, single-detail and multi-detail understanding.

bigfinancebench.text: 928 expert-authored, open-ended financial research tasks, each paired with a reference answer and a point-weighted rubric that splits the derivation into independently checkable steps for partial credit.

cotcontrol.text: An evaluation suite for chain-of-thought controllability: a model must solve a problem while obeying constraints on its own reasoning trace, for example answering a genetics question without using the word 'chromosome'.

medqamainlandchina.text: The simplified-Chinese split of MedQA: 34,251 multiple-choice questions collected from professional medical board exams in Mainland China.

uniformbarexammbemeempt.text: The three-part US Uniform Bar Examination, combining the multiple-choice Multistate Bar Examination, the essay-based Multistate Essay Examination, and two Multistate Performance Test lawyering tasks.

cmteb.text: A Chinese text embedding benchmark covering six task types across 35 datasets, used to compare general-purpose Chinese embedding models.

followir.text: Built from three deeply judged TREC collections by turning the assessors' narrative guidelines into retrieval instructions and re-annotating relevance, with a pairwise framework that measures how a retriever's ranking shifts when the instruction changes.

miabench.text: 400 image and prompt pairs whose prompts stack several explicit requirements at once, such as a fixed number of sentences or particular elements to mention, testing whether a multimodal model follows every layer of the instruction.

omnicloze.text: A cloze-style stand-in for detailed captioning: roughly 2,000 clips carrying about 70,000 fine-grained blanks across audio-only, visual-only and audio-visual settings, with an LLM matching a generated caption to each blank.

rxr.text: 126,000 navigation instructions in English, Hindi and Telugu paired with human following demonstrations in Matterport3D scenes, plus pose traces that align each word to what the annotator was looking at.

spreadsheetbench1.text: 912 spreadsheet manipulation instructions taken from online Excel forums, each shipped with several input and output workbook test cases and graded online-judge style so a solution must generalize across files.

voxpopuli10en.text: The English transcribed portion of VoxPopuli, 543 hours of European Parliament recordings from 2009 to 2020 with aligned transcripts, used for automatic speech recognition.

dpbench.text: 200 documents from the Library of Congress, open educational resources and internal Upstage files, annotated with 12 layout element types, scoring a parser's text serialization with NID and its table structure with TEDS.

rekaresearcheval.text: 374 search-dependent questions written by in-house tutors, each carrying a checklist of correctness requirements applied by an LLM judge, covering lookups such as regulations, business contact details and academic deadlines.

codalm.text: Road images of self-driving corner cases paired with three tasks, general perception, region perception and driving suggestions, where a text-only LLM judges the vision-language model's written answers.

omnidrive.text: Counterfactual question answering built on nuScenes driving scenes, covering scene description, traffic elements, hypothetical maneuvers scored against rule-based collision and traffic-violation checklists, and trajectory decision making.

androidlab.text: 138 tasks across nine Android apps run on fixed virtual devices, with a shared action space so text-only and multimodal agents can be compared, and per-task completion checked reproducibly.

humanevalx.text: A hand-written port of the HumanEval problems into C++, Java, JavaScript and Go alongside Python, each with reference solutions and test cases, supporting both code generation and translation between the five languages.

videochatgptbench.text: 500 clips from ActivityNet-200 with human-written descriptions, used to generate questions whose free-form video-chat answers are graded by GPT-3.5 on correctness, detail, context, temporal understanding and consistency.

gregeneraltest.text: The graduate admissions exam from ETS, made up of five scored sections: one analytical writing task, two verbal reasoning sections and two quantitative reasoning sections covering reading, vocabulary and quantitative interpretation.

redlinebench.text: 140 contract redlining tasks spread over three multi-turn SaaS negotiation scenarios. An agent edits a Word document with tracked changes and margin comments, and an LLM judge panel grades the result against weighted rubrics written by senior attorneys.

racem.text: The middle school half of RACE, a reading comprehension set drawn from English exams for Chinese students: passages aimed at 12 to 15 year olds with multiple-choice questions written by English instructors.

arenaaitext.text: A crowdsourced human preference ranking for text-to-text models. Users compare two models' answers to the same prompt and vote, and the votes are aggregated into scores with confidence intervals across math, coding, creative writing and other open-ended domains.

bcmbppjavascript.text: The JavaScript portion of BabelCode-MBPP, which ports Google's MBPP basic Python programming problems and their test cases into 16 languages so generated code is checked by executing the language-specific tests.

codefeedbackmt.text: A multi-turn code retrieval task in the CoIR benchmark. The query is a user and assistant programming dialogue up to but excluding the final reply, and the model must retrieve that final assistant answer from a corpus.

ehrnoteqa.text: 962 patient-specific multiple-choice questions written over MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, drafted with GPT-4 and reviewed by three clinicians. Most items require reading two or more of a patient's notes to answer.

grayswanipibenchmark.text: An indirect prompt injection evaluation drawn from a public red teaming arena spanning 41 tool-use, coding and computer-use agent scenarios. Instructions are hidden in content the agent reads, and an attack counts only if the agent both acts on them and conceals that from the user.

internationalphysicsolympiad25.text: Held at Ecole Polytechnique near Paris in July 2025, the annual secondary school physics competition: students from over 80 countries sit theoretical and experimental papers testing analysis, critical thinking and problem solving.

mmlumed.text: The medicine-related subjects of MMLU treated as one set: anatomy, clinical knowledge, college biology, college medicine, medical genetics, professional medicine and virology, 3,685 multiple-choice questions in all.

multimedqa140.text: 140 long-form medical questions sampled from HealthSearchQA, LiveQA and MedicationQA. Answers are rated by physicians and lay people on axes such as factuality, possible harm and bias rather than scored automatically.

primevulpaired.text: The paired split of PrimeVul, where each vulnerable C or C++ function is matched with its patched version that shares most of its text, so a detector must label both correctly and surface cues are not enough.

trialbench.text: 23 clinical trial datasets assembled from ClinicalTrials.gov for eight prediction tasks, including trial duration, patient dropout, serious adverse events, mortality, approval outcome and eligibility criteria design, with drug structures, trial text and disease codes as inputs.

wmt24chrf.text: A machine translation test set extending WMT24 to 55 languages and dialects with professional reference translations and post-edits over literary, news, social and speech text, here scored with the character n-gram F-score chrF.

davis17.text: Densely annotated video sequences for object segmentation. Pixel masks for the objects are given in the first frame and a method must segment and track them through the rest of the clip, with several instances annotated per video and official metrics computed at 480p.

lvvis.text: 4,828 videos annotated with over 26,000 instance masks from 1,196 object categories, for open-vocabulary video instance segmentation: segmenting, tracking and naming objects whose categories were never seen in training.

nyud.text: Indoor RGB-D video from 464 scenes recorded with a Kinect, used as the standard monocular depth benchmark: predict per-pixel depth from a single 480x640 image, evaluated on the 654-image Eigen test split.

rf100vl.text: 100 object detection datasets covering concepts rare in vision-language pretraining, such as defect inspection, material properties and medical, thermal and aerial imagery, run in zero-shot, few-shot, semi-supervised and fully supervised settings.

temporalbench.text: Roughly 10,000 video question-answer pairs derived from about 2,000 detailed human annotations of temporal dynamics in clips, probing fine-grained abilities such as action frequency, motion magnitude and event order.

humanevalplus.text: An extension of HumanEval that keeps the original Python problems but adds roughly 80 times more test cases, catching solutions that pass the sparse original tests while being subtly wrong.

repobench.text: A repository-level code completion benchmark over multi-file Python and Java projects with three linked tasks: retrieving relevant cross-file snippets, predicting the next line given in-file and cross-file context, and running both together as a pipeline.

hhem21.text: Vectara's factual consistency check: a FLAN-T5 based classifier scores whether a piece of text is supported by the source passage it was generated from, used to flag summaries in retrieval-augmented pipelines that stray from their evidence.

mmluredux20.text: 5,700 MMLU questions spanning all 57 subjects, re-annotated by hand against the original sources so items with wrong answer keys, bad options or unclear wording are identified.

frontiermath.text: Several hundred unpublished mathematics problems written by professional mathematicians, spanning undergraduate difficulty up to research-grade work across four tiers. Every answer is an object a script can check, so no proof review is needed.

ioi24.text: Held in Alexandria, Egypt in September 2024, the 36th edition of the international secondary school informatics contest: students compete individually over two competition days on algorithmic problems requiring algorithm and data structure design, programming and testing.

medqataiwan.text: The traditional Chinese portion of MedQA, free-form multiple-choice questions taken from Taiwan's professional medical board examination.

usabosemifinalexam20.text: The second round of the USA Biology Olympiad, a proctored 120 minute online exam in three parts: mostly single-answer multiple choice, multiple true-false items, and short answer or essay questions on the International Biology Olympiad host's practical topics.

cmtebr.text: The retrieval group of C-MTEB, a Chinese text embedding benchmark of 35 datasets over six task types. A model embeds queries and candidate passages and is judged on ranking the relevant passage highest.

eth3d.text: A 3D reconstruction benchmark built from high-resolution images and low-resolution multi-camera video of indoor and outdoor scenes, with tracks for two-view and many-view stereo, multi-view stereo reconstruction and, since 2019, SLAM.

fullstackbenchen.text: The English split of FullStack Bench, real-world programming instructions covering basic programming, data analysis, software engineering, mathematics and machine learning across 16 languages, with solutions run against unit tests in a sandbox.

livebench20241125.text: A contamination-resistant benchmark that ships new questions every month, drawn from recently released datasets, arXiv papers, news articles and film synopses. Its 18 tasks across six categories each carry a verifiable answer scored automatically rather than by a judge model.

minervamath.text: The MATH dataset of 12,500 competition mathematics problems run in the Minerva setup: four-shot prompting with the exemplars from the Minerva paper, and answers checked for symbolic equivalence using sympy.

mobileminiwob.text: MiniWoB++ web tasks reimplemented inside the AndroidWorld Android environment, 92 in all. HTML inputs render as native Android widgets, the agent sees the accessibility tree and screenshots, and each task carries its own success check.

polymath.text: A multilingual mathematical reasoning benchmark spanning 18 languages and four difficulty levels, with parallel problems produced by controlled translation so results are comparable across languages.

safim.text: 17,720 code fill-in-the-middle examples taken from submissions made after April 2022, masking syntax-aware units such as whole code blocks and conditional expressions rather than arbitrary character spans.

waymoqa.text: Multi-view driving questions built on Waymo Open Dataset clips, with eight synchronised camera views per scene. Multiple-choice items test safety-critical reasoning in two stages: resolving the immediate risk, then handling the secondary risk it induces.

relbench.text: Predictive tasks defined directly over relational databases from several domains and scales, where a model must learn across many tables linked by primary and foreign keys rather than a single flat table.

openasrleaderboard.text: A public comparison of speech recognition systems over English short-form and long-form test sets plus multilingual ones, reporting word error rate and an inverse real-time factor, with every run executed on identical hardware for reproducibility.

ape210k.text: 210,000 Chinese elementary school math word problems, assembled to be far larger and more template-diverse than earlier word problem datasets.

partiprompts.text: Over 1,600 English prompts for text-to-image generation, released with the Parti model and organised by category and by the kind of challenge each prompt poses.

visual7w.text: Grounded visual question answering with multiple-choice what, where, when, who, why, how and which questions, where an answer can be text or a specific image region, linking questions to objects rather than whole images.

biglawbench.text: Real-world legal tasks across transactional and litigation practice, graded with per-task rubrics written by lawyers that award points for correct work product and subtract for errors, plus a separate score for citing source documents.

grereadingandwritingexams.text: The Verbal Reasoning and Analytical Writing sections of the GRE General Test: reading comprehension, text completion and sentence equivalence questions, plus a timed essay analyzing an issue.

riemannbench.text: A private set of research-level mathematics problems written by professors, graduate students and PhD-holding IMO medalists, each double-blind verified by two independent experts and having a unique closed-form answer checked by a programmatic verifier.

combibench.text: 100 combinatorics problems, each formalized in Lean 4 and paired with an informal statement, spanning middle school to IMO and university level and including every IMO combinatorics problem since 2000 but one.

arenatext.text: Crowdsourced blind comparison of text responses: a user submits a prompt, two anonymous models answer, the user picks the better reply, and the votes are aggregated into a public ranking.

bcmbppkotlin.text: The Kotlin split of MBPP as converted by Google's BabelCode framework, which translates Python programming problems and their test cases into other languages so generated solutions can be checked by execution.

codefeedbackst.text: A code retrieval task in the CoIR benchmark: given a single-turn question that mixes text and code, retrieve the answer that also mixes text and code, over a corpus built from CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction.

ehrqa.text: Question answering over synthetic FHIR-formatted patient records generated with Synthea, using 42 question types in 10 categories written with clinicians in multiple-choice, yes/no and free-response form, graded automatically.

guiec.text: Instance-level image-to-image retrieval, matching a query image against an index of 200,000 images, from the Google Universal Image Embedding Challenge.

jtestac.text: The advanced A to C band of a Japanese proficiency exam run by the Japanese Language Testing Association, taken under simulated conditions: multiple-choice reading questions plus writing answers rated by native speakers.

multirc.text: About 10,000 questions over short paragraphs from seven domains, each written so no single sentence answers it. The number of correct options is not fixed, so every candidate answer must be judged on its own.

siimarc.text: Binary classification of chest X-rays for the presence of pneumothorax, taken from the SIIM-ACR pneumothorax challenge data and posed to the model as a multiple-choice question about the image.

tydiqagoldp.text: The gold passage variant of TyDi QA: given a passage guaranteed to contain the answer, predict the answer span, across nine typologically diverse languages with unanswerable questions removed and SQuAD 1.1 metrics.

wmt25.text: Document-level machine translation test sets in 16 language pairs across news, speech, social media and literary domains, from the 2025 WMT general translation shared task, judged by human annotators under the ESA protocol.

auroracapvdc.text: Over a thousand videos annotated with long structured captions, scored by VDCscore, which splits a long caption into short question-answer pairs judged by a language model.

davisinteractivebenchmark.text: Video object segmentation driven by scribbles instead of full masks: a simulated user draws a scribble, the model segments every frame, and further scribbles are fed back on the worst frame over repeated rounds, scored by region and contour accuracy.

machiavelli.text: 134 text-based Choose-Your-Own-Adventure games with over half a million annotated scenarios, used to measure how far an agent goes toward power seeking, causing harm and ethical violations while pursuing in-game reward.

omnilabel.text: Language-based object detection over more than 25,000 images with over 28,000 free-form object descriptions, each of which may refer to one, several or no objects, scored by a modified average precision.

sa23.text: A suite of 23 image segmentation datasets assembled for deliberately varied image distributions, used to test zero-shot mask prediction from a single point prompt.

textquests.text: Infocom interactive fiction games played by an agent with no external tools, testing sustained self-directed exploration and trial-and-error reasoning over a single long, growing context.

humanevaltypescript.text: Python programming problems from HumanEval, together with their unit tests, translated into TypeScript by MultiPL-E so that generated solutions can be checked by execution.

ruler128k.text: Thirteen synthetic long-context tasks covering multi-needle retrieval, variable tracking, word aggregation and question answering, run at the 128K-token input length of the RULER suite.

acebench.text: Tool-use evaluation split into three data types: Normal for straightforward calls, Special for ambiguous or incomplete instructions, and Agent for multi-turn, multi-agent dialogues that simulate real interactions.

mmvuval.text: The public 1,000-question validation split of MMVU, with multiple-choice and open-ended questions written from scratch by experts about specialized-domain videos across 27 subjects in science, healthcare, humanities and engineering.

aiderspolyglotdiff.text: 225 of the hardest Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust, with the model required to return its changes as search/replace diff blocks rather than rewriting whole files.

frontiermathtier13.text: The first three difficulty tiers of FrontierMath, unpublished problems written by mathematicians that run from undergraduate level up to exploratory questions suited to an advanced graduate student, with automatically verifiable answers.

jailbreakaugmentedexamples.text: Publicly known jailbreak techniques applied to prompts drawn from OpenAI's standard disallowed content evaluation, measuring whether the model still declines to comply.

medqausmle4options.text: US Medical Licensing Examination style questions from the MedQA dataset, restricted to the version in which every question has exactly four answer options, with about 10,200 training and 1,270 test items.

audioboxaesthetic.text: No-reference automatic prediction of audio aesthetics along four axes (Production Quality, Production Complexity, Content Enjoyment and Content Usefulness) for speech, music and general sound, trained against human mean opinion scores.

cnmiddleschool24.text: Multiple-choice mathematics problems from China's 2024 high school entrance examination, used by Qwen as a Chinese exam evaluation alongside Gaokao in a five-shot setting.

cweval.text: Outcome-driven evaluation of generated code for functionality and security at once, pairing detailed task specifications with test oracles that exercise the vulnerability, over the multilingual security-critical CWEval-bench tasks.

fullstackbenchzh.text: The Chinese-language half of FullStack Bench, 1,690 problems whose instructions are written in Chinese, covering full-stack application domains across 16 programming languages and checked by unit tests.

hummusqa.text: 320 hand-written questions about music audio, curated and validated by annotators with musical training, paired with checks for whether a model can answer from text alone without listening.

livebench241125.text: The question set released on 25 November 2024 for LiveBench, whose contamination-resistant tasks span math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following and data analysis and are graded automatically against ground-truth answers.

mobileworld.text: 201 mobile agent tasks across 20 Android applications, weighted toward long-horizon cross-app workflows and including agent-user interaction and MCP tool tasks, verified against the applications' backend databases.

musicavqa.text: Over 45,000 question-answer pairs built from 33 templates about musical performance videos, requiring joint reasoning over the sounds, the visible instruments and their spatial and temporal relationships.

omnivideobench.text: 1,000 question-answer pairs over 628 videos running from seconds to 30 minutes, each annotated with a step-by-step reasoning trace, across 13 question types that require combining audio and visual evidence.

popcs.text: 117 Mandarin pop songs, roughly 5.89 hours sung by one female singer in a studio and recorded at 24 kHz, with lyrics force-aligned to phonemes and pitch extracted from the raw waveform.

scienceboard.text: 169 human-curated tasks in a desktop environment running real scientific software, where an agent must drive the applications through their own interfaces to carry out workflows in areas such as biochemistry, astronomy and geoinformatics.

streamingbench.text: 900 videos with 4,500 human-curated question-answer pairs over 18 tasks, asking five questions at different timestamps per video to test understanding of a stream as it arrives rather than after it ends.

turkishmmlu.text: Over 10,000 multiple-choice questions written by curriculum experts for the Turkish high school syllabus, covering nine subjects from natural sciences and mathematics to Turkish literature and history.

waymoqaall.text: 35,000 human-annotated question-answer pairs about safety-critical driving scenes, given as multi-view images and video in both multiple-choice and open-ended form, where avoiding one risk can create another.

koifeval.text: A Korean adaptation of IFEval: verifiable instruction-following prompts professionally translated and revised for Korean usage, scored zero-shot with prompt-level and instruction-level strict accuracy.

bigbencharithmetic.text: Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division on numbers of one to five digits, posed in words as both free-response and multiple-choice items and graded by exact string match.

kernelbench.text: 250 PyTorch machine learning workloads for which a model must write a GPU kernel, graded on whether the kernel is functionally correct and how much it speeds the workload up over the PyTorch baseline.

webarenalite.text: A 165-task subset of WebArena, manually reviewed so that every task is correctly specified and actually feasible, cutting a full evaluation run from hours to minutes.

bioasq.text: Expert-written biomedical questions that systems must answer by retrieving relevant PubMed articles and text snippets, then producing both an exact answer and a paragraph-length ideal answer.

healthadminbench.text: 135 expert-defined healthcare administration tasks covering prior authorization, appeals and denials, and durable medical equipment orders, run in four simulated GUIs (an EHR, two payer portals and a fax system) and broken into 1,698 verifiable subtask checks.

swebenchmultimodal.text: 617 issue-resolution tasks from 17 user-facing JavaScript libraries covering web interfaces, diagramming, data visualization and mapping, where every task carries at least one image in its problem statement or tests.

corpusqa1m.text: The roughly one-million-token setting of CorpusQA: 329 question and answer pairs over finance, education and real estate corpora in English and Chinese, graded by a model judging semantic equivalence to the reference answer.

mawps.text: An online repository of 3,320 math word problems pooled from earlier collections, with tooling to build sub-datasets that control lexical and template overlap and to filter ungrammatical problems.

repobench11.text: Next-line code completion in Python and Java repositories, built from GitHub code committed between October and December 2023 and deduplicated against Stack v2, with prompts bucketed by context length.

artcap.text: 3,606 Impressionism and Expressionism paintings drawn from WikiArt, each annotated with five human-written descriptions, for captioning fine art rather than photographs.

bcmbpppython.text: The Python portion of BabelCode's translation of MBPP, a set of crowd-sourced entry-level programming tasks each stated in natural language and checked by per-language unit tests.

encyclopedicvqa.text: 221k question and answer pairs about fine-grained species, landmarks and other entities, each matched with up to five images and answerable from a controlled Wikipedia-derived knowledge base, including two-hop questions.

hackthebox.text: 13 capture-the-flag challenges taken from the Hack The Box platform, covering reverse engineering, binary exploitation and cryptography; the agent works through a Bash shell to recover a hidden flag string.

k600.text: 600 human action classes with at least 600 video clips each, gathered from YouTube using multiple queries per class including non-English ones, for trimmed-clip action classification.

mmmuhm.text: The Health and Medicine slice of MMMU: 1,752 college-level multiple-choice questions over medical images and diagrams, spanning basic medical science, clinical medicine, diagnostics, pharmacy and public health.

n2c.text: Google's held-out set of Python code generation tasks (Natural2Code), produced internally from non-web sources so that no examples leak from the web, used as a contamination-free counterpart to HumanEval.

qvhighlights.text: 10,310 free-form natural language queries over more than 10,000 YouTube vlog and news videos, annotated with the disjoint moments each query matches plus five-point saliency scores for every two-second clip.

slakevqa.text: 642 radiology images (CT, MRI and X-ray) with 14,028 bilingual English and Chinese question and answer pairs, split between purely visual questions and ones needing recalled medical knowledge, plus segmentation masks and a knowledge graph.

unjustifiedrefusals.text: An automated Google evaluation of whether a model answers borderline prompts rather than declining them, tracking refusals of requests that did not warrant one while still requiring safe responses.

wsc.text: Pairs of near-identical sentences differing by one or two words, where a pronoun resolves to a different noun in each; the binary choice is designed to need world knowledge and to resist corpus statistics. A published collection holds 150 schemas.

bbbc0381.text: Microscopy images of nuclei from humans, mice and flies under varied stains, magnifications and lighting, where each nucleus must be segmented individually; ground truth is supplied as one mask per nucleus.

iheval.text: 3,538 examples across nine tasks testing whether a model honours the instruction hierarchy running from system message to user message to conversation history to tool output, covering cases where those instructions align and where they conflict.

mapillarystreetlevelsequences.text: 1.6M street-level images grouped into sequences across cities including Miami, Athens, Stockholm and Bengaluru, for long-term visual place recognition, with subtasks for summer against winter, day against night, and old against new imagery.

openrewriteeval.text: 1,629 triples of instruction, source text and human rewrite covering formality, paraphrase, shortening, elaboration and open-ended Wikipedia and web edits, aimed at cross-sentence rewriting and scored with NLI, SARI, GLEU and an updated ROUGE.

tgifqa.text: 165K question and answer pairs over animated GIFs, split into repetition counting, repeating action, state transition and single-frame questions, scored by accuracy except for counting, which uses squared error.

fatex.text: 100 abstract algebra and commutative algebra exercises formalised in Lean, drawn from textbooks, final exams, PhD qualifying exams and research papers; each statement ends in a `sorry` that must be replaced by a proof the Lean toolchain accepts.

advancedif.text: Over 1,600 prompts paired with expert-curated rubrics for advanced instruction following, covering complex, multi-turn and system-prompted instructions, with each response graded against its own rubric.

multiswebench.text: 1,632 issue-resolution instances in Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C and C++, annotated down from 2,456 candidates by 68 expert annotators, extending the SWE-bench format beyond Python.

aiderspolyglotwhole.text: 225 Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust, run in the edit format where the model rewrites each file in full instead of emitting a diff, and checked against the exercises' tests.

biorisktoolingevaluation.text: Browsing tasks checking whether an agent can drive external biological resources, such as a protein design tool, a cloud lab or a DNA supplier, far enough to complete a key step like ordering synthetic DNA.

cyberrange.text: Long-form exercises in a realistic emulated network, such as one modelled on a small online retailer, where the model must plan toward an adversary objective, exploit vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, and chain those exploits together.

frontiermathtier132.text: The first three difficulty tiers of Epoch AI's unpublished mathematics problem set, running from undergraduate level up to exploratory problems suited to an advanced graduate student, with answers that are computationally verifiable.

jailbreakevaluations.text: Adversarial prompts meant to talk a model past its refusals, drawn from OpenAI's human red teaming and from the academic StrongREJECT set, scored on whether the resulting output is unsafe.

medqausmle5options.text: English board-exam questions in the style of the US Medical Licensing Examination, kept with their original five answer choices rather than the reduced four-option variant of the same collection.

personidentificationandungroundedinferen.text: Automated checks on whether a model refuses to name a person shown in a photo, and refuses inferences the input cannot support, such as who is more dangerous or what job a pictured person has, run in non-adversarial and adversarial variants.

swelancer.text: Over 1,400 real freelance software engineering jobs taken from Upwork, split between coding tasks graded by end-to-end tests triple-verified by engineers and manager-style choices between competing implementation proposals.

visionselfharmrefusalevaluation.text: Prompts combining an image with text requesting self-harm content, taken from OpenAI's standard disallowed-content set, checking refusals across the self-harm intent and self-harm instructions categories.

audiocaps.text: About 46k audio clips sampled from AudioSet, each given a crowdsourced natural language description, for captioning in-the-wild sound.

deepplanning.text: Long-horizon agent planning in two offline sandboxes, travel and shopping, with 120 tasks each; the agent gathers state through Python tool APIs and must satisfy budget, timing and coupon constraints, checked by rule-based graders.

ewmbench.text: Evaluation of video-generating embodied world models on scene consistency, motion quality and semantic alignment with the language command, rather than on general perceptual video metrics.

livecodebench23052409.text: Competitive programming problems scraped from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces and tagged with their release date; this slice keeps problems published between May 2023 and September 2024, judged by the problems' own test cases.

mir1k.text: 1,000 karaoke clips totalling about 133 minutes, recorded with the accompaniment on one stereo channel and the singing voice on the other, with manual pitch contours, unvoiced-frame labels, lyrics and vocal segment marks.

mustbench.text: 1,264 music-expert-validated question and answer pairs over full-length tracks, covering five temporal grounding tasks: locating when a source enters or exits, recognising and describing transitions, ordering them, and finding mood peaks.

oneigbench.text: Fine-grained evaluation of text-to-image models along separate dimensions: alignment between prompt subjects and generated elements, text rendering accuracy, reasoning-driven content, stylisation and diversity.

redteamcua.text: 864 adversarial cases that plant indirect prompt injections in a hybrid sandbox pairing an OS virtual machine with Reddit, ownCloud and Rocket.Chat replicas, testing whether a computer-use agent breaks confidentiality, integrity or availability.

scienceqaimg.text: The image-context portion of ScienceQA: 10,332 of its multiple-choice elementary and high school science questions that come with a diagram, photo or map, spanning natural, social and language science.

surds.text: Spatial reasoning over nuScenes driving images, with 9,250 evaluation questions across six dimensions: a single object's yaw, pixel location and depth range, plus distance, left-right and front-behind relations between objects.

uivision.text: Desktop GUI demonstrations recorded across 83 real applications with dense bounding-box, semantic-label and action-trajectory annotations, split into element grounding, layout grounding and action prediction.

waymoqasafety.text: The safety-critical questions of a 35k-pair multi-view driving QA set built from rare pre-crash scenes in the Waymo End-to-End data, where the maneuver that resolves the first hazard induces a second risk the model must also handle.

komiracl.text: The Korean portion of MIRACL, a multilingual retrieval benchmark of human-written queries over Wikipedia passages, converted to BEIR format so it can be run through MTEB.

cursorbench32.text: Coding agents are run on realistic IDE-style tasks from production Cursor workflows: multi-file edits, natural language instructions, tools, APIs and MCPs, and iterative fixing.

searcharena.text: Crowdsourced side-by-side comparisons of search-augmented chat models: users ask their own questions, see two anonymous answers with numbered citations, and vote for one, a tie, or both bad. The released data covers over 24,000 multi-turn interactions in 71 languages.

physreason.text: 1,200 physics problems split evenly across knowledge, easy, medium and hard tiers, most carrying a diagram, graded by a framework that scores both the final sub-answers and the individual solution steps.

browsecompvl.text: 399 visual question answering pairs across five domains, built by masking entities in text questions with visual references, so a browsing agent must combine image understanding with multi-source web search.

refl4test.text: Referring expression comprehension relabelled to fix the annotation errors found in RefCOCO-style benchmarks: 45,341 annotations over 365 object categories, with expressions averaging 24.2 words and instances ranging from tiny to very large.

webquestmultiqa.text: The multi-screen split of WebQuest: questions spanning several semantically related web page screenshots, filtered so that every page is needed to answer, simulating tasks such as comparison shopping across sites.

usamo26.text: The six proof problems from the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad, with model-written proofs graded point by point by a jury of LLM judges and then verified by hand.

defects4j.text: A database of 854 reproducible bugs drawn from widely used open-source Java projects, each shipped with the faulty and fixed versions plus infrastructure for compiling and testing them.

mcpatlaspublic.text: The 500-task public split of MCP-Atlas: expert-written natural language requests executed against production MCP servers, with answers scored against atomic factual claims grounded in the tool outputs.

svamp.text: A challenge set of elementary-school arithmetic word problems, created by applying targeted variations to existing problems so that solvers relying on shallow heuristics fail.

asimov.text: A collection of datasets for measuring the semantic safety of foundation models used as robot brains, built by generating undesirable situations from real visual scenes and hospital injury reports.

bcmbpprust.text: The MBPP Python programming problems converted to other languages by the BabelCode framework and graded by executing the translated tests; this is the Rust version.

ett.text: Two years of readings from two electricity transformers at two stations, covering power load and oil temperature, used as a long-sequence time-series forecasting task.

hardpromptsinlmarena.text: A Chatbot Arena leaderboard slice limited to user prompts that score high on hardness criteria such as domain knowledge, complexity and problem-solving, ranked by head-to-head human votes.

lbpp.text: 161 Python programming prompts with reference solutions and unit tests, written from scratch by annotators with competitive programming experience so the problems are harder than HumanEval and uncontaminated.

natural2code.text: Google's held-out Python code generation set, written in-house in the same format as HumanEval but with different prompts and hidden unit tests, to avoid leakage from public web pages and repositories.

usdermmcqa.text: An internal teledermatology set of one image per patient for 1,996 US patients across 136 skin conditions, recast as four-option multiple choice with the dermatologist's diagnosis among the options.

xgqa.text: The English GQA visual question answering set extended to seven typologically diverse languages, for measuring zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on questions about images.

beavertails30k.text: A 30,000-example round of the BeaverTails safety corpus: question and answer pairs each labelled safe or unsafe with separate harm-category annotations.

diving48.text: A fine-grained video action recognition set of competitive diving, assembled with the RESOUND procedure so static scene and object cues give little away and the 48 dive classes must be told apart by motion.

imagenet22k.text: The full ImageNet collection of 14.2 million labelled photographs indexed against 21,841 WordNet synsets, used for very large vocabulary image classification.

mbppbaseversion.text: The MBPP+ set of hand-checked Python programming tasks scored with the original MBPP tests rather than with EvalPlus's much larger augmented test suite.

orbench.text: 80,000 automatically generated prompts that look unsafe but are harmless, plus a hard subset and 600 genuinely toxic prompts, for measuring how often a safety-tuned model refuses benign requests.

sa3dao.text: 1,000 pairs of a natural image and a hand-built, image-aligned 3D mesh made by professional artists, for measuring real-world reconstruction of object shape and layout from a single image.

timberseg.text: 220 densely annotated forestry images containing 2,500 individually segmented wood logs, with both bounding boxes and pixel masks, for log detection and grasping.

rxrce.text: Room-across-Room's crowdsourced route instructions in English, Hindi and Telugu ported to continuous environments, where the agent moves freely through photorealistic scans instead of hopping between graph nodes.

hletext.text: The subset of Humanity's Last Exam questions that carry no image reference, so text-only models can be run on the same expert-written, closed-ended academic questions.

nonspeech7k.text: Recordings of human non-speech sounds to be classified into seven categories: breath, cough, cry, laugh, scream, sneeze and yawn.

aparthistory.text: The College Board's Advanced Placement art history exam: 80 multiple-choice questions built around colour images of artworks, plus six timed essays that compare, contextualise and attribute works.

browsecomplongcontext.text: BrowseComp's agentic search questions turned into a long-context task: rather than browsing, the model is handed the contents of a human-checked list of required pages mixed with supplementary and noise pages.

cybersafetyevaluations.text: Prompts from production traffic and synthetic data covering cyber abuse topics such as malware creation, credential theft and chained exploitation, scored on whether the model refuses or de-escalates while still supporting educational security questions.

frontiermathtier4.text: The expansion tier of FrontierMath: 43 exceptionally difficult research-level problems crafted and vetted by expert mathematicians, answered by submitting a Python function that returns the result.

kernelgen1p.text: An agent is given a kernel development environment, benchmark harness and correctness tests, and must write a kernel for OpenAI's first-party hardware that is correct and faster than a baseline, without shortcuts such as host-side compute or benchmark spoofing.

mentalhealth.text: One category of OpenAI's production safety benchmarks: deliberately difficult conversations touching on mental health concerns, graded on whether the reply is disallowed under OpenAI's policy.

personqa.text: A set of questions about people paired with publicly available facts, measuring how often a model answers correctly and how often it fabricates when it attempts an answer.

swelancerdiamond.text: The public evaluation split of SWE-Lancer, built from real paid freelance software engineering jobs posted on Upwork and graded by end-to-end tests that experienced engineers triple-verified.

visionsexualrefusalevaluation.text: One of OpenAI's multimodal refusal tests: combined text and image prompts asking for disallowed sexual or exploitative content, autograded on whether the response violates OpenAI policy.

avspeakerbench.text: 3,212 multiple-choice questions on speaker-centric reasoning in real videos, where a cue given in one modality anchors a moment and the answer has to be read off the other modality.

gaokao2023en.text: Math questions in English compiled from the 2023 Chinese national college entrance exam together with the 2023 American Mathematics Competitions and American College Testing, each with a short reference answer.

ifevalmultilingual.text: IFEval's automatically checkable instruction-following prompts extended beyond English, with instructions that depend on a particular language, such as starting with the letter A, removed.

livecodebench1.text: The first release of LiveCodeBench's code generation set: 400 competition problems published between May 2023 and March 2024, each with a description, worked examples and hidden test cases.

mrcr2256k8needle.text: A synthetic long-context test where the model reads a long user and assistant conversation full of near-identical writing samples and must reproduce one specified instance, here with eight candidates at a 256K context.

mypcbench.text: 184 personal-assistant tasks on a Linux desktop seeded for one fictional persona, with 17 simulated web applications behind logins, testing computer-use agents against natural language rubrics.

oneigbenchtexten.text: The text rendering slice of OneIG-Bench run on its English prompt set, scoring how accurately a generated image reproduces the specific written characters the prompt asks for.

prbenchfinance.text: The finance half of PRBench: open-ended, economically consequential problems written by credentialed practitioners and marked against expert-curated rubric criteria.

refadvs.text: The public 1,142-case subset of Ref-Adv, a referring expression benchmark that pairs long descriptions, often containing negation, with several hard visual distractors to block shortcut matching.

sciqaimg.text: The image-context subset of ScienceQA: multiple-choice school science questions whose context is a diagram or photograph, annotated with a lecture and an explanation of the answer.

swebenchlive.text: 1,319 issue-resolving tasks taken from GitHub issues filed since 2024 across 93 repositories, each with its own Docker image, produced by an automated curation pipeline that can be rerun to keep the set fresh.

uniclawbench.text: 400 bilingual real-world tasks for proactive agents, run in live Docker containers with step-by-step completion checkpoints and a closed loop of executor, hidden supervisor and simulated user.

h6.text: The six-task average of the original Open LLM Leaderboard, combining ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, Winogrande and GSM8K into a single number.

kommlu.text: A Korean multiple-choice test of comprehension and subject knowledge across a wide range of fields, one of the privately held datasets behind the Open Ko-LLM Leaderboard.

securecodereview.text: An internal agentic software engineering evaluation that scores both whether an agent fixes the security issues present in a realistic codebase and whether its patch avoids merging new ones.

driveaction.text: 16,185 question and answer pairs from 2,610 real driving scenarios, with the high-level action labels taken from what the human driver actually did, arranged in a tree that links vision, language and action tasks.

pinchbenchavg.text: Real assistant tasks such as scheduling meetings, writing code, triaging email, researching topics and managing files, run through an OpenClaw agent and averaged over the task set.

libriclean.text: The clean test split of the LibriSpeech corpus, read English speech from public-domain audiobooks, used to measure recognition error on well-recorded, easier audio.

webquestsingleqa.text: The single screen split of WebQuest: questions answered from the contents of one web page screenshot, often needing small counting or logical steps over what is displayed.

codearenawebdev.text: Models build and deploy interactive web applications from a prompt such as building a markdown editor with dark mode, working through create_file, edit_file and read_file calls, with evaluators comparing two builds pairwise on functionality, usability and fidelity.
